mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q01.stem: Once insulation has been removed, broken strands do not affect connection quality.
reasons: This statement is false. Check conductor damage; successful stripping alone does not establish acceptance.
Check conductor damage; successful stripping alone does not establish acceptance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q02.stem: Values near a tolerance boundary may be rounded toward the passing side when recorded.
reasons: This statement is false. Preserve actual measurements and assessment procedures.
Preserve actual measurements and assessment procedures.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q03.stem: Converting 8 mA to amperes for an equation gives 0.008 A.
reasons: 1 A equals 1000 mA.
This statement is true. 1 A equals 1000 mA.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q04.stem: An inspected label means later abnormalities must always be ignored.
reasons: This statement is false. A label alone does not unconditionally guarantee the current condition passes.
A label alone does not unconditionally guarantee the current condition passes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q05.stem: Control limits concern process monitoring; specification limits concern conformity to product requirements.
reasons: Do not equate the two types of limit.
This statement is true. Do not equate the two types of limit.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q06.stem: Hidden lines show the shapes of normally invisible parts.
reasons: Read using drawing conventions and line purposes.
This statement is true. Read using drawing conventions and line purposes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q07.stem: In a common four-band code, a gold tolerance band always means ±50%.
reasons: This statement is false. Check the correspondence in the marking system.
Check the correspondence in the marking system.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q08.stem: Different diode types, including Zener diodes, have different intended applications.
reasons: Check the type and specifications.
This statement is true. Check the type and specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q09.stem: Determining maintenance needs from vibration, temperature and other conditions is predictive maintenance.
reasons: Distinguish condition monitoring from responding after failure.
This statement is true. Distinguish condition monitoring from responding after failure.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q10.stem: AM, FM and PM are identical methods that change only carrier amplitude.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish the quantity changed by modulation.
Distinguish the quantity changed by modulation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q11.stem: In a basic holding circuit, the relay’s own contact provides a path parallel to the start contact.
reasons: The contact path maintains coil energization.
This statement is true. The contact path maintains coil energization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q12.stem: Installing one circuit breaker unconditionally prevents all earth leakage and electric shocks.
reasons: This statement is false. Select the required protection functions separately.
Select the required protection functions separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q13.stem: A keep-dry symbol guarantees the contents will be protected even when exposed to rain.
reasons: This statement is false. The symbol specifies handling conditions.
The symbol specifies handling conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q14.stem: A dial indicator may be used to indicate deviation from a reference.
reasons: Check the graduation and reference.
This statement is true. Check the graduation and reference.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q15.stem: Small needle files matching the shape may be selected for detailed finishing.
reasons: Protect surfaces to retain and finish gradually.
This statement is true. Protect surfaces to retain and finish gradually.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q16.stem: Even without knowing a tool’s name, you may try it freely if the deadline is near.
reasons: This statement is false. Check suitability and authorization.
Check suitability and authorization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q17.stem: Containers of the same color may use the SDS for a different product.
reasons: This statement is false. Different products may have different hazards and handling requirements.
Different products may have different hazards and handling requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q18.stem: Compare improvement rates after checking inspection conditions and denominators.
reasons: The denominator and comparison conditions affect the result.
This statement is true. The denominator and comparison conditions affect the result.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q19.stem: A JIS mark makes a dropped instrument safe to use without an accuracy check.
reasons: This statement is false. A mark does not unconditionally guarantee the present condition.
A mark does not unconditionally guarantee the present condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q20.stem: Check the PSE marking category separately from equipment suitability and worker requirements.
reasons: The product regime is separate from installation and worker responsibilities.
This statement is true. The product regime is separate from installation and worker responsibilities.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q21.stem: Do not read roughness Ra in μm as the same numerical scale as a length in mm.
reasons: The required quantity and unit differ.
This statement is true. The required quantity and unit differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q22.stem: Trapezoidal threads are used only for fastening and never for machine-tool feeds.
reasons: This statement is false. They are also used in machine-feed mechanisms.
They are also used in machine-feed mechanisms.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q23.stem: At the same material and temperature, wire resistance is proportional to length and inversely proportional to area.
reasons: Use R=ρℓ/S.
This statement is true. Use R=ρℓ/S.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q24.stem: Adding phosphorus to silicon produces p-type material whose majority carriers are holes.
reasons: This statement is false. Phosphorus is a donor example producing n-type material with majority electrons; boron is an acceptor example associated with p-type material.
Phosphorus is a donor example producing n-type material with majority electrons; boron is an acceptor example associated with p-type material.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q25.stem: Experienced workers are never affected by fatigue, even over long periods.
reasons: This statement is false. Follow rest-break and other management arrangements.
Follow rest-break and other management arrangements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q26.stem: Ns=120 f/p gives the synchronous speed of the rotating magnetic field.
reasons: The actual speed of an induction machine involves slip.
This statement is true. The actual speed of an induction machine involves slip.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q27.stem: Work labeled hoshu always means only repair after failure in every standard and workplace.
reasons: This statement is false. Avoid generalizing terminology; read the actual work description.
Avoid generalizing terminology; read the actual work description.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q28.stem: Etching exposed unwanted copper and stripping the remaining film remove different materials.
reasons: Protect and retain the copper of the required pattern.
This statement is true. Protect and retain the copper of the required pattern.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q29.stem: At the same shaft torque, doubling actual rotational speed doubles mechanical power.
reasons: P is proportional to the product of N and T.
This statement is true. P is proportional to the product of N and T.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-theory-q30.stem: If a tool handle comes off, gripping its tip firmly by hand preserves the same safety conditions.
reasons: This statement is false. Check tool integrity and injury prevention.
Check tool integrity and injury prevention.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q01.stem: The identity of a chemical was lost while transferring it to another container. What should you do?
options: Guess from its smell and mix it.
Stop using it and ask the responsible person to verify identification and SDS information.
Put it in a drink container because it looks like water.
reasons: Guessing by smell and mixing risk misidentification and harmful reactions.
Without identification, hazards and measures cannot be selected. Check labels and documents instead of guessing.
Even small quantities can injure skin; do not touch unidentified chemicals.
Clear liquids may be hazardous; drink containers create ingestion risks.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q02.stem: A basic on-delay is set to five seconds, but its input turns off after three. What is the basic output behavior?
options: It always turns on for five seconds after the input turns off.
It never turns on because the set time is not reached.
It always turns on immediately with the input.
It latches on after three seconds regardless of the input.
reasons: An on-delay times sustained input-on; this is not a question about holding after input-off.
The input must remain on for the set time. Check model-specific holding functions separately.
The set delay prevents immediate output-on.
The input ends after three seconds, before the five-second condition is met.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q03.stem: The goods and quantity are correct, but the destination label names another customer. What should happen before dispatch?
options: Ship because the contents are correct.
Hide only the item number on the label.
Stop dispatch and reconcile and correct the goods, documents and destination.
reasons: A wrong destination prevents delivery to the correct customer; contents alone are insufficient.
Cushioning addresses impact, not an incorrect address.
Hiding an item number neither corrects the destination nor preserves identification.
Logistics quality requires the correct destination. Strong packaging and correct quantity do not resolve an address mismatch.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q04.stem: Which resistance gives 2 mA from a 6 V source in an ideal DC circuit?
reasons: Multiplying 6 V and 2 mA is not the V/I calculation for resistance.
Calculate V/I rather than I/V, with consistent units.
This treats 2 mA as 2 A, creating a factor-of-1000 error.
R=6/0.002=3000 Ω=3 kΩ. Convert mA to A before division.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q05.stem: A period spans eight divisions at 0.5 ms/div. What is the frequency?
reasons: This takes the reciprocal of four seconds instead of four milliseconds.
Four milliseconds is the period, not a frequency of 4 Hz.
The reciprocal of 0.004 s is 250 Hz, not 4000 Hz.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q06.stem: A 0.01 mm micrometer shows 8.5 mm on the sleeve and 17 on the thimble. What is the dimension?
reasons: 8.5+17×0.01=8.67 mm. Add the sleeve’s half-millimeter and scaled thimble reading separately.
The sleeve’s 0.5 mm has been omitted.
This multiplies 17 by 0.1 mm, but each graduation is 0.01 mm.
Seventeen divisions represent 0.17 mm, not 0.017 mm.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q07.stem: A material has three times the mass of reference water of the same volume. What is its specific gravity under the same conditions?
reasons: The mass ratio is three, neither its reciprocal nor a value in kilograms.
Specific gravity is a density ratio and does not carry density units of kg/m³.
Equal volumes make the mass ratio three, a dimensionless density ratio. Do not attach mass or density units.
Volumes must correspond; specific gravity cannot be replaced by a mass of three kilograms.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q08.stem: A drawing at scale 1:2 is dimensioned 80 mm. What length should be manufactured?
options: Use only the length measured on paper.
reasons: Do not multiply the written dimension by the inverse drawing scale.
Scale controls drawing size; manufacture to the written 80 mm dimension.
Paper measurements vary with printing scale, so written dimensions take priority.
Applying the drawing scale again halves the specified 80 mm.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q09.stem: Using P=2πNT/60, estimate shaft power at an actual speed of 600 min⁻¹ and torque of 3 N·m.
reasons: This fails the angular-speed conversion including 2π and is about ten times too large.
600 min⁻¹ is 10 s⁻¹, so output is 2π×10×3, about 188 W.
2π×600×3/60=60π≈188.5 W. Losses distinguish input power from shaft output.
This omits division by 60 when converting revolutions per minute to per second.

mfg1-electrical-mock-02-practical-q10.stem: A shaft and hole have the same nominal diameter but different tolerance ranges. What is needed to judge their fit?
options: The combination of permitted dimensions of both shaft and hole.
reasons: Without the shaft limits, minimum and maximum clearance cannot be established.
Nominal diameter alone does not establish dimensional limits, clearance or interference.
The combination of permitted dimensions determines clearance, interference or transition fit; matching nominal values alone is insufficient.
The hole limits must also be included to establish the combined fit.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q01.stem: Check stripping length against the connection and work standard.
reasons: The specified length must suit the terminal and process.
This statement is true. The specified length must suit the terminal and process.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q02.stem: Do not omit a visible 0.5 mm sleeve line from a micrometer reading.
reasons: Combine sleeve and thimble readings.
This statement is true. Combine sleeve and thimble readings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q03.stem: Current in an ideal resistor is always calculated as I=V×R.
reasons: This statement is false. Divide voltage by resistance using consistent units.
Divide voltage by resistance using consistent units.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q04.stem: A report is easier to understand when its conclusion is followed by facts such as the item, time and quantity.
reasons: Make the conclusion, specific facts and required decision clear.
This statement is true. Make the conclusion, specific facts and required decision clear.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q05.stem: A one-direction trend over time warrants checking even while values remain within specification.
reasons: Monitor process stability separately.
This statement is true. Monitor process stability separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q06.stem: Two parts drawn close together in a connection diagram must also be installed next to each other.
reasons: This statement is false. Logical connections and physical arrangement differ.
Logical connections and physical arrangement differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q07.stem: Do not infer the original value of a burnt, discolored resistor from visible colors alone.
reasons: Verify its original specification or model.
This statement is true. Verify its original specification or model.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q08.stem: If no static electricity is felt at the fingertips, an IC certainly has no damage.
reasons: This statement is false. Invisible damage is possible.
Invisible damage is possible.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q09.stem: Recording when an abnormal sound occurred and the operating conditions assists investigation.
reasons: Record specific facts that can be traced.
This statement is true. Record specific facts that can be traced.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q10.stem: Only a computer’s display screen is called the CPU.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish the output device from the processing component.
Distinguish the output device from the processing component.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q11.stem: During self-holding, energization always continues forever even if the stop path is opened.
reasons: This statement is false. The stop condition interrupts the complete holding path.
The stop condition interrupts the complete holding path.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q12.stem: If protection operates with a burning smell, do not repeatedly reenergize before establishing the cause.
reasons: This risks worsening the fault or causing a restart.
This statement is true. This risks worsening the fault or causing a restart.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q13.stem: All resins can be reheated and remolded into the same condition indefinitely after curing.
reasons: This statement is false. Check resin category and processing history.
Check resin category and processing history.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q14.stem: A surface plate provides a reference plane; placing an item on it does not itself display its dimensions.
reasons: Distinguish the reference surface from the measuring instrument.
This statement is true. Distinguish the reference surface from the measuring instrument.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q15.stem: When removing burrs, no check is needed even if the specified hole diameter is exceeded.
reasons: This statement is false. Excessive removal compromises conformity.
Excessive removal compromises conformity.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q16.stem: In 5 S, standardizing means disposing of unnecessary items once and doing no further upkeep.
reasons: This statement is false. Maintenance and habits are necessary.
Maintenance and habits are necessary.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q17.stem: A corrosive symbol relates to hazards of damage to metals, skin and similar materials.
reasons: Treat it as hazard information.
This statement is true. Treat it as hazard information.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q18.stem: In PDCA, Act improves methods or the next plan based on the evaluation.
reasons: Apply the evaluation before proceeding.
This statement is true. Apply the evaluation before proceeding.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q19.stem: Kilograms and newtons are the same quantity and unit without any conversion conditions.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish the types of physical quantity.
Distinguish the types of physical quantity.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q20.stem: Interpretation of technical standards only identifies products under PSE and has no relation to installation requirements.
reasons: This statement is false. Interpretation of technical standards specifies installation requirements; it is not limited to PSE product categories.
Interpretation of technical standards specifies installation requirements; it is not limited to PSE product categories.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q21.stem: A transition fit may produce clearance or interference depending on the combination of permitted dimensions.
reasons: Check the relationship of the tolerance ranges.
This statement is true. Check the relationship of the tolerance ranges.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q22.stem: Changing solder alloy never requires checking its melting point or process conditions.
reasons: This statement is false. Approved conditions depend on the alloy.
Approved conditions depend on the alloy.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q23.stem: At the same voltage, a smaller ideal resistance consumes more power.
reasons: Keep conditions consistent and use P=V²/R.
This statement is true. Keep conditions consistent and use P=V²/R.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q24.stem: A depletion layer is a vacuum hole containing neither matter nor any charge.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse fewer mobile carriers with absence of matter.
Do not confuse fewer mobile carriers with absence of matter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q25.stem: In binary logic, x+x equals x.
reasons: Do not confuse OR with ordinary addition.
This statement is true. Do not confuse OR with ordinary addition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q26.stem: P=NT always gives watts without considering unit conversion or 2π.
reasons: This statement is false. Use P=2πNT/60 to convert rotational speed in min⁻¹.
Use P=2πNT/60 to convert rotational speed in min⁻¹.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q27.stem: Collecting one number automatically completes predictive maintenance for every machine.
reasons: This statement is false. Judgment and operational conditions are necessary.
Judgment and operational conditions are necessary.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q28.stem: The SI base unit of thermodynamic temperature is K, and that of luminous intensity is cd.
reasons: Match the seven base quantities to their units.
This statement is true. Match the seven base quantities to their units.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q29.stem: If secondary voltage matches, every transformer can be used at any increased load current.
reasons: This statement is false. Observe capacity and temperature ratings.
Observe capacity and temperature ratings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-theory-q30.stem: Choose hacksaws and files according to their different cutting and hand-finishing roles.
reasons: Hacksaws cut; files are used for hand finishing and similar work.
This statement is true. Hacksaws cut; files are used for hand finishing and similar work.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q01.stem: A 0.05 mm vernier caliper shows 18 mm on the main scale and a 0.45 mm vernier fraction. What is the reading?
reasons: This adds the 0.45 mm fraction twice.
0.05 mm is the minimum reading, not the actual 0.45 mm fraction.
Add the 0.45 mm fraction to 18 mm to get 18.45 mm; do not just add one minimum division.
This misplaces the decimal, treating 0.45 mm as 0.0045 mm.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q02.stem: Which basic machine rotates the workpiece while a cutting tool machines its outside diameter or threads?
reasons: Milling mainly rotates the tool, unlike the workpiece rotation fundamental to a lathe.
A lathe uses workpiece rotation. Milling mainly rotates the tool, so distinguish which item moves.
A drill press primarily feeds a rotating drill into a workpiece to produce a hole.
A surface grinder mainly finishes flat surfaces with an abrasive wheel, rather than turning diameters and threads.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q03.stem: Which pairing gives the majority carriers in n-type and p-type silicon?
reasons: The types distinguish majority carriers, not simply negative and positive charge on the entire material.
Electrons are the majority in n-type, so both cannot be holes.
Holes are the majority in p-type, so both cannot be electrons.
The carrier assignments are reversed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q04.stem: Which component primarily intended for temperature sensing uses the change in resistance caused by a change in temperature?
reasons: A CdS cell mainly uses resistance changing with light.
A varistor mainly uses resistance changing with applied voltage, unlike a temperature-sensing thermistor.
A thermistor uses the temperature–resistance relationship. Also check its ratings and characteristic type.
A fixed resistor provides a specified resistance; it is not the name of an element primarily exploiting temperature-dependent resistance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q05.stem: You will inspect equipment containing a capacitor after power-off. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Verify residual-charge treatment under the specified procedure.
Short it with a screwdriver without authorization.
Touch all terminals immediately after power-off.
Assume passive components cannot cause electric shock.
reasons: A capacitor may retain charge after power-off. Follow approved isolation and residual-charge measures.
Unauthorized shorting creates discharge-current, spark and other hazards.
Charge may remain in the capacitor after power-off.
The passive classification does not rule out electric shock from stored charge.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q06.stem: Which device mainly switches using semiconductors without movable contacts?
reasons: An electromagnetic contactor mainly operates movable contacts, unlike semiconductor switching in an SSR.
A reed relay also operates contacts magnetically rather than using only semiconductor switching.
An SSR mainly uses semiconductors. Absence of mechanical contacts does not remove leakage-current or heating checks.
An ordinary electromagnetic relay uses electromagnetic force to move mechanical contacts.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q07.stem: You see the textbook example of thermal class F at 155°C. What is the proper interpretation?
options: Every machine may operate at 155°C ambient.
Treat it as an insulation class under specified conditions, separate from product ambient temperature.
reasons: An insulation thermal class is not the permitted ambient temperature of the entire machine.
The class does not give the melting point of all materials.
155°C is temperature, not conductor area in mm².
Thermal classes are conditional classifications of materials or insulation systems, not blanket operating-environment permission.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q08.stem: A continuous sensor voltage must be converted into numbers a computer can process. Which function is needed?
reasons: Filtering selects frequency components but does not itself convert the signal into numbers.
A/D converts analog signals into digital values; D/A works in the reverse direction.
Amplification alone does not encode a continuous voltage as digital numbers.
D/A converts digital values back into analog signals, the reverse direction.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q09.stem: What is one period of a 50 Hz sine wave?
reasons: This converts 0.02 seconds incorrectly to 20 seconds.
1/50 second is 0.02 seconds, not 0.002.
The frequency’s number cannot simply be relabeled as milliseconds.
T=1/50=0.02 s=20 ms. Distinguish direction reversals from complete cycles.

mfg1-electrical-mock-03-practical-q10.stem: Apply 12 V to an ideal 24 Ω DC resistor. What power is consumed?
reasons: 0.5 is the current in amperes; multiply by 12 V to obtain 6 W.
This multiplies V by R rather than using V²/R.
Power is not obtained from a difference or similar operation on 12 and 24; calculate 144/24.
P=V²/R=144/24=6 W. Current is 0.5 A; do not confuse current with power.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q01.stem: Merely placing solder melted on the iron onto a cold joint may fail to produce the required connection.
reasons: Proper joint heating and wetting are necessary.
This statement is true. Proper joint heating and wetting are necessary.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q02.stem: Even with the same name, outside and inside measuring instruments measure different features.
reasons: Check model, range and application.
This statement is true. Check model, range and application.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q03.stem: Horizontal s/div indicates voltage per division.
reasons: This statement is false. The horizontal axis indicates time; the vertical axis may indicate voltage.
The horizontal axis indicates time; the vertical axis may indicate voltage.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q04.stem: If a terminal number is unknown, guess a nearby number, connect it, then report.
reasons: This statement is false. Resolve uncertainties before working.
Resolve uncertainties before working.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q05.stem: Defect counts and defective-product counts differ when products have multiple defects.
reasons: Define what constitutes one counted case.
This statement is true. Define what constitutes one counted case.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q06.stem: All contacts switch in the same direction when equipment operates.
reasons: This statement is false. Relate state to the basic a-contact closing and b-contact opening behavior.
Relate state to the basic a-contact closing and b-contact opening behavior.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q07.stem: Series resistors may carry different steady currents even without branches.
reasons: This statement is false. Steady current is the same along a single unbranched path.
Steady current is the same along a single unbranched path.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q08.stem: Do not equate an ordinary transparent bag with specified ESD packaging.
reasons: Check packaging type and suitability.
This statement is true. Check packaging type and suitability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q09.stem: With matching capacitance, voltage rating and polarity are merely decoration.
reasons: This statement is false. Compare all relevant specifications.
Compare all relevant specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q10.stem: A barcode-reader beep alone does not guarantee that subsequent processing and display updates succeeded.
reasons: Verify facts at each functional stage.
This statement is true. Verify facts at each functional stage.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q11.stem: As long as a motor rotates, position accuracy, speed and pressing-force requirements are automatically met.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish controlled quantities and specifications.
Distinguish controlled quantities and specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q12.stem: Using photovoltaic DC output in AC equipment requires suitable conversion and other compatibility.
reasons: Distinguish generation from DC/AC conversion.
This statement is true. Distinguish generation from DC/AC conversion.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q13.stem: Check material input records because different materials may look similar.
reasons: Appearance alone may not reveal wrong materials.
This statement is true. Appearance alone may not reveal wrong materials.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q14.stem: An LCR meter measures only voltage and DC current, never capacitance or inductance.
reasons: This statement is false. It measures inductance, capacitance, resistance and related values.
It measures inductance, capacitance, resistance and related values.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q15.stem: For point charges under unchanged conditions, doubling their separation reduces force magnitude to one quarter.
reasons: Force is inversely proportional to distance squared.
This statement is true. Force is inversely proportional to distance squared.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q16.stem: The basic 5 S sorting rule is to discard every unidentified item without permission.
reasons: This statement is false. Maintain identification and responsible-person verification.
Maintain identification and responsible-person verification.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q17.stem: Every event without injury is irrelevant to safety management.
reasons: This statement is false. Also share warning signs of accidents.
Also share warning signs of accidents.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q18.stem: Management frequency in a QC process chart specifies inspection timing.
reasons: Read what is managed, when and how.
This statement is true. Read what is managed, when and how.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q19.stem: One mm² equals 10⁻³ m², using the same conversion factor as length.
reasons: This statement is false. For area, square the length conversion factor.
For area, square the length conversion factor.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q20.stem: Distinguish the issuers and scopes of industry standards such as JEM and JEITA.
reasons: Their issuers and fields differ.
This statement is true. Their issuers and fields differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q21.stem: A coil and its contacts are never drawn apart.
reasons: This statement is false. They may be separated in a developed diagram for clarity.
They may be separated in a developed diagram for clarity.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q22.stem: Excessive heating duration or force may damage circuit-board pads.
reasons: Observe component and board limits for heat and force.
This statement is true. Observe component and board limits for heat and force.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q23.stem: One period at 50 Hz is 50 ms.
reasons: This statement is false. 1/50 second equals 0.020 seconds.
1/50 second equals 0.020 seconds.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q24.stem: Characteristics such as switching time serve a different purpose from maximum ratings.
reasons: Characteristic values do not replace limits.
This statement is true. Characteristic values do not replace limits.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q25.stem: NOT(x·y) equals (NOT x)·(NOT y) for every input.
reasons: This statement is false. De Morgan’s law exchanges AND and OR.
De Morgan’s law exchanges AND and OR.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q26.stem: Even if winding current doubles, copper loss always halves.
reasons: This statement is false. At the same winding resistance, I²R makes loss four times greater.
At the same winding resistance, I²R makes loss four times greater.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q27.stem: Do not necessarily treat a no-stacking instruction like a stack-height limit.
reasons: Follow the marking and specification requirements.
This statement is true. Follow the marking and specification requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q28.stem: Hall-effect sensors are used to detect magnetic flux density.
reasons: They use electromotive force associated with current and magnetic field.
This statement is true. They use electromotive force associated with current and magnetic field.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q29.stem: Environmental testing covers appearance only, excluding all temperature, humidity and vibration conditions.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish tests applying environmental conditions from appearance checks.
Distinguish tests applying environmental conditions from appearance checks.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-theory-q30.stem: Check electrical steel and permanent magnets against the different magnetic properties needed for their applications.
reasons: Distinguish core-loss and permeability requirements from permanent-magnet retention properties.
This statement is true. Distinguish core-loss and permeability requirements from permanent-magnet retention properties.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q01.stem: What is the equivalent resistance of ideal 60 Ω and 120 Ω resistors in parallel?
reasons: 180 Ω is the series sum, not a parallel value.
1/R=1/60+1/120=3/120, so R=40 Ω. Being below the smallest branch, 60 Ω, also checks the result.
90 Ω is only their average, not the reciprocal-sum result.
The product must also be divided by the sum.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q02.stem: After etching in a subtractive PCB process, protective film remains. Which conceptual next step is appropriate?
options: Strip the film under specified conditions while retaining required conductors.
Mix all chemicals regardless of process.
reasons: In the negative-resist concept, the film protecting required copper is removed last. Actual stripping and cleaning conditions follow material and process specifications.
Unconditional shipping mid-process skips subsequent work and inspection.
Chemicals have reaction hazards and process-specific requirements; indiscriminate mixing is unacceptable.
Dissolving required conductors destroys the intended circuit pattern.
Multiply by 1000 when converting kΩ to Ω, rather than dividing.
This multiplies by a million instead of the k multiplier of 1000.
k means 1000, not ten, so the result is not 24 Ω.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q04.stem: Someone proposes guaranteeing a product’s lifetime because it operated once. What is appropriate?
options: Treat insulation resistance and withstand-voltage tests as identical.
Distinguish one functional check from prescribed reliability evaluation.
Guarantee every environmental resistance from appearance.
One operation guarantees the entire lifetime.
reasons: Insulation-resistance measurement and withstand-voltage testing have different purposes and applied conditions.
Functional, environmental, reliability and electrical-safety tests differ in purpose and conditions. One operation cannot guarantee lifetime.
Appearance cannot substitute for temperature, humidity, vibration and other environmental tests.
One operational check does not establish failure resistance over the required period.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q05.stem: When comparing an induction motor’s nameplate and measured speed, how should synchronous speed be understood?
options: It depends only on frequency, never pole count.
It always matches shaft speed at full load.
It means only the load-dependent rotor speed.
It is rotating-field speed, distinct from actual rotor speed under load.
reasons: Ns=120 f/p depends on pole count as well as frequency.
A loaded induction motor has slip, so shaft and synchronous speed differ.
Synchronous speed describes the field determined by frequency and poles, not the measured shaft speed.
Slip means the synchronous-speed equation does not guarantee loaded shaft speed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q06.stem: An ideal AC transformer has a 120 V primary, 600 primary turns and 150 secondary turns. What is secondary voltage?
reasons: This reverses the turns ratio; fewer secondary turns step voltage down.
Adding turn counts does not produce a voltage.
V2=120×150/600=30 V. This ideal ratio does not replace actual rating and connection checks.
Voltage is proportional to the turns ratio, not found by subtracting a turn difference from voltage.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q07.stem: At the same winding resistance, current doubles. By what factor does copper loss I²R change?
reasons: (2 I)²R=4 I²R because loss depends on current squared.
Changing current changes I²R.
Doubling current quadruples its squared term, rather than doubling it.
With fixed resistance, increasing current raises copper loss rather than halving it.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q08.stem: In a third-angle drawing, where is the right-side view normally placed relative to the front view?
reasons: Above is normally the plan view in third-angle projection.
Below is not the normal right-side-view position.
Third-angle places the right-side view on the right and plan view above. Also verify the projection symbol.
Left confuses first-angle or other arrangements; third-angle places it on the right.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q09.stem: A different grease brand arrives for a lubrication point. What should you do?
options: Check specifications and mixing compatibility; do not mix without approval.
Reach into running machinery to feel it.
Mix if the colors are similar.
reasons: More grease does not resolve compatibility or mixing issues.
Type, suitability and specified quantity matter. Mixing or overgreasing may cause faults; continue safety procedures.
Reaching into moving equipment risks entanglement and other harm.
Similar colors do not establish the same base oil, thickener or composition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-05-practical-q10.stem: Specifications are 19.90–20.10 mm; measured values are 19.80, 20.00 and 20.20 mm. Which judgment is correct?
options: The centered average means all pass.
Creating a control chart automatically passes out-of-specification items.
Even with an average of 20.00 mm, the two outer values are outside specification.
reasons: The centered average does not change the out-of-specification 19.80 and 20.20 values.
The average alone hides the two nonconforming items.
Control charts monitor process changes; they do not change product specifications.
Individual specification assessments differ from the average. These three points also do not guarantee overall process capability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q01.stem: Match crimping-tool die shape to the terminal type used.
reasons: Combine the specified terminal with its compatible tool.
This statement is true. Combine the specified terminal with its compatible tool.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q02.stem: To keep measuring force constant, tighten as hard as possible every time.
reasons: This statement is false. Excessive force causes deformation and variation.
Excessive force causes deformation and variation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q03.stem: Once current can be calculated, source capacity and resistor ratings no longer need checking.
reasons: This statement is false. Calculation and actual equipment suitability are separate checks.
Calculation and actual equipment suitability are separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q04.stem: If only a color change has been observed, do not report that the cause of burning is established.
reasons: Separate observations from inferred causes.
This statement is true. Separate observations from inferred causes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q05.stem: A histogram always has time on its horizontal axis and monitors an upper control limit.
reasons: This statement is false. Its purpose differs from a time-ordered control chart.
Its purpose differs from a time-ordered control chart.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q06.stem: Across multiple drawing sheets, match components by following the same equipment identifiers and terminal numbers.
reasons: Check identification and cross-references.
This statement is true. Check identification and cross-references.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q07.stem: Matching resistance values allow differences in rated power and temperature to be ignored.
reasons: This statement is false. Check specifications beyond resistance value.
Check specifications beyond resistance value.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q08.stem: ESD precautions need be applied only after all work is finished.
reasons: This statement is false. Prevent exposure before handling begins.
Prevent exposure before handling begins.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q09.stem: A capacitor may retain charge after power-off.
reasons: Check residual energy and perform the specified treatment.
This statement is true. Check residual energy and perform the specified treatment.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q10.stem: Binary 1101 has exactly the same value as decimal 1101.
reasons: This statement is false. 8+4+0+1=13.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q11.stem: An explanation that power restoration alone will not restart equipment depends on assumptions such as a non-latching relay and a released start input.
reasons: Check circuit construction and input states.
This statement is true. Check circuit construction and input states.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q12.stem: Solar cells and storage batteries merely store unlimited electricity in the same way.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse their roles because both names include cell or battery.
Do not confuse their roles because both names include cell or battery.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q13.stem: FRP electrical properties depend on factors such as glass versus carbon fiber.
reasons: Fiber, resin, orientation and content affect properties.
This statement is true. Fiber, resin, orientation and content affect properties.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q14.stem: A height gauge is used for heights from a reference plane and for marking out.
reasons: Match the dimension required to the instrument’s purpose.
This statement is true. Match the dimension required to the instrument’s purpose.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q15.stem: Positive charges always attract one another, while positive and negative charges always repel.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish force direction by charge signs.
Distinguish force direction by charge signs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q16.stem: The fixed-item element of the three fixed rules includes deciding which item belongs at a designated location.
reasons: Make the item to be placed clear.
This statement is true. Make the item to be placed clear.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q17.stem: Check local exhaust conditions before chemical work.
reasons: Conditions must prevent vapor exposure.
This statement is true. Conditions must prevent vapor exposure.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q18.stem: Any old standard for any product can always be used unchanged within the same factory.
reasons: This statement is false. Check applicability and revision.
Check applicability and revision.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q19.stem: Before units, m and M always represent the same multiplier.
reasons: This statement is false. Record uppercase and lowercase correctly.
Record uppercase and lowercase correctly.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q20.stem: Do not determine current regulatory coverage from only the item count in old documents.
reasons: Check the regime’s date and applicable conditions.
This statement is true. Check the regime’s date and applicable conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q21.stem: LEDs and photodiodes only emit light in the same direction.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish light-related functions and arrow directions.
Distinguish light-related functions and arrow directions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q22.stem: Whether flux residue requires cleaning depends on material and product specifications.
reasons: Check type and process conditions.
This statement is true. Check type and process conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q23.stem: W and Wh are interchangeable expressions for the same quantity regardless of time.
reasons: This statement is false. Separate the rate of consumption from the total energy.
Separate the rate of consumption from the total energy.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q24.stem: FET gate drive and BJT base drive do not use the same terminal names and conditions.
reasons: Check the device type and data sheet.
This statement is true. Check the device type and data sheet.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q25.stem: x·0 always equals x, and x+1 always equals 0.
reasons: This statement is false. Apply the AND/OR laws for zero and one.
Apply the AND/OR laws for zero and one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q26.stem: Reduction ratios for starting methods have assumptions about connections and equipment conditions.
reasons: Winding compatibility, protection and approval are needed.
This statement is true. Winding compatibility, protection and approval are needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q27.stem: Every PPM value always has the same number as the corresponding percentage.
reasons: This statement is false. The conversion factors differ.
The conversion factors differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q28.stem: The SI base unit of amount of substance is mol.
reasons: Distinguish mol from derived resistance units.
This statement is true. Distinguish mol from derived resistance units.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q29.stem: Checking component polarity or missing components and checking solder cracks examine different things.
reasons: Separate the different assembly-inspection items.
This statement is true. Separate the different assembly-inspection items.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q30.stem: Chamfering only means enlarging the entire hole diameter without limit.
reasons: This statement is false. Preserve required edge shape and dimensions.
Preserve required edge shape and dimensions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q01.stem: A tightening standard specifies 4 N·m, but the tool displays another unit. What should you do?
options: Check units, conversion and tool applicability before setting it.
Remove a washer to make tightening easier.
Tighten as much as possible by feel.
reasons: Torque is controlled by value and unit; do not leave a unit mismatch and copy the number.
Removing the washer changes the specified assembly and does not resolve units.
The number four in another unit may not equal 4 N·m.
Maximum tightening by feel risks excessive torque and broken parts.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q02.stem: You observe unusual equipment vibration. Which information should be central to the report?
options: Only criticism of the responsible person.
A decision to call it normal without records.
Equipment ID, time, operating state and observed vibration.
reasons: Criticism alone provides no equipment, timing or vibration conditions for investigation.
Presenting an uninvestigated cause as fact miscommunicates the situation.
Observed abnormality should not be declared normal without records.
Separate observed facts from inference and follow safety and reporting procedures.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q03.stem: A developed connection diagram shows coil K3 and contact K3 far apart. How should it be read?
options: Erase identifiers and wire by appearance.
Treat nearby K2 contacts as K3.
Trace operation using the corresponding equipment identifiers.
Assume they are unrelated because they are far apart.
reasons: Removing identifiers prevents tracing the correct coil/contact relationship.
Match identifiers, not proximity; do not relabel K2 as K3.
Coils and contacts may be drawn separately. Match equipment numbers and cross-references.
The same device may be separated in a developed diagram to make functions easier to follow.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q04.stem: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns, 800 secondary turns and 24 V primary voltage. What is the secondary voltage?
reasons: Different turn counts mean the voltage ratio is not one.
Twice the turns gives twice the ideal voltage: 48 V. This ratio alone establishes neither capacity nor losses.
Adding turns does not produce a voltage; use the turns ratio.
This reverses the ratio; the secondary has more turns, so voltage rises.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q05.stem: A substitute transistor has its B, C and E terminals in a different order from the drawing. What should you do?
options: Ignore maximum ratings if the shape is similar.
Insert it in any orientation because it has three leads.
Verify terminal arrangement and rating compatibility in model documentation.
reasons: Matching shape does not prevent failure caused by insufficient maximum ratings.
B/C/E order can differ between three-lead device models.
B and E have different functions and cannot be swapped arbitrarily.
Three leads alone do not establish compatibility; compare both terminals and electrical conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q06.stem: There are three relevant defects among 20000 shipped units. What is the PPM?
reasons: 15 results from multiplying the fraction by 100000 rather than a million.
1500 is ten times too high due to an incorrect conversion factor.
0.00015 is the fraction; multiply it by a million for PPM.
3/20000×1000000=150 PPM. Align case definitions and periods when comparing.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q07.stem: Under this app’s equally weighted practice scoring, theory is 20/30 and practical is 5/10. What is the section-by-section result?
options: Theory meets its threshold; practical does not, so there is no overall pass.
A total of 25 means a guaranteed pass.
Passing theory guarantees a pass regardless of practical.
reasons: The app requires at least 20/30 and 6/10 separately; practical 5/10 falls short. This does not guarantee unpublished official scoring or answer-count thresholds.
Separate practice thresholds do not allow a combined total to compensate for a shortfall.
Practical must independently reach at least 6/10.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q08.stem: You are preparing to crimp 2.0 mm² stranded wire, but the tool only states “2.0 mm solid wire.” What should happen before starting?
options: Use the blade because the numbers match.
Check the tool’s applicability to the stranded cross-section and terminal.
Crush the terminal with ordinary pliers.
Cut away half the conductor to make it thinner.
reasons: A solid-wire diameter marking is not the same application as stranded-wire area.
mm indicates diameter and mm² area; matching numbers do not establish compatibility. Check wire, terminal and tool together.
General pliers do not guarantee the specified crimp shape or force.
Cutting strands compromises the required area and connection performance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q09.stem: After zeroing a dial indicator on a reference part, you compare another part’s deviation. What conditions are required?
options: Do not record the reference dimension if the pointer moves.
Contact a different surface obliquely each time.
Keep the reference surface, contact direction and probe displacement consistent.
Leave dirt on the surface plate.
reasons: Without a reference dimension, deviation cannot be related to actual size or specifications.
Changing direction or reference adds measurement differences beyond product differences.
Comparisons depend on reference and measuring posture. Changed conditions confound product and measurement differences.
Dirt changes the reference and posture, causing measurement error.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q10.stem: A supplier presents an ISO certificate. What is the correct approach to product inspection?
options: Check certification scope and product requirements, then perform necessary inspections.
Abolish inspections without reading the scope.
reasons: Organizational certification differs from individual product conformity; compare scope and requirements separately.
The applicable revision matters when verifying requirements.
Certification does not automatically guarantee all individual products pass.
Abolishing inspections without reading the scope may violate contractual or product requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q01.stem: Fixing one button of a two-hand control can allow the machine to operate while the freed hand is inside the danger area.
reasons: Fixing one button removes the requirement to keep both hands at the controls, creating crushing and other hazards.
This statement is true. Fixing one button removes the requirement to keep both hands at the controls, creating crushing and other hazards.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q02.stem: Drawing hatching consists of lines used only to show the travel range of moving parts.
reasons: This statement is false. Hatching indicates specific areas such as section cuts. Phantom lines may indicate movement ranges.
Hatching indicates specific areas such as section cuts. Phantom lines may indicate movement ranges.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q03.stem: An ammeter symbol in a circuit diagram directly shows the physical positions of its real terminals.
reasons: This statement is false. A functional symbol differs from actual shape and terminal layout; check terminal diagrams and specifications.
A functional symbol differs from actual shape and terminal layout; check terminal diagrams and specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q04.stem: Even at the same length and cross-section, conductor resistance may change with material or temperature.
reasons: The resistivity ρ in R=ρℓ/S depends on material and temperature.
This statement is true. The resistivity ρ in R=ρℓ/S depends on material and temperature.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q05.stem: Even infrequent defects leading to electric shock require severity assessment and action.
reasons: Assess frequency and severity separately.
This statement is true. Assess frequency and severity separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q06.stem: All good electrical conductors necessarily have identical magnetic properties.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish conductivity from magnetism.
Distinguish conductivity from magnetism.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q07.stem: The parallel equivalent of two positive resistances is smaller than the smaller resistance.
reasons: Parallel connection adds current paths.
This statement is true. Parallel connection adds current paths.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q08.stem: OR outputs one only when exactly one input is one; for 11 it always outputs zero.
reasons: This statement is false. OR is satisfied when at least one input is one.
OR is satisfied when at least one input is one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q09.stem: BJTs with the same external shape have a fixed B/C/E order across all manufacturers.
reasons: This statement is false. Shape alone does not establish terminal order.
Shape alone does not establish terminal order.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q10.stem: The film protecting a wiring pattern differs in role from the unwanted copper to remove.
reasons: Retain required copper and remove unwanted copper.
This statement is true. Retain required copper and remove unwanted copper.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q11.stem: At the same marked voltage, all DC and AC motor connections are interchangeable.
reasons: This statement is false. Several ratings and operating types must be checked.
Several ratings and operating types must be checked.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q12.stem: Flow control mainly relates to hydraulic-actuator speed.
reasons: Inspect speed, force and direction separately.
This statement is true. Inspect speed, force and direction separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q13.stem: If flat washers are missing, state the part number and shortage quantity when asking for verification.
reasons: Fastener configuration and torque are separate specifications.
This statement is true. Fastener configuration and torque are separate specifications.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q14.stem: An illuminance-meter reading always also determines magnetic flux density at the same value.
reasons: This statement is false. Light and magnetic field are different quantities.
Light and magnetic field are different quantities.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q15.stem: Apply theory and practical percentage thresholds independently to their respective sections.
reasons: Do not combine the sections into one total-based judgment.
This statement is true. Do not combine the sections into one total-based judgment.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q16.stem: Safety glasses and safety footwear address different hazards.
reasons: Choose PPE for the body area and hazard.
This statement is true. Choose PPE for the body area and hazard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q17.stem: Implementing one measure absolutely eliminates every fault and human error.
reasons: This statement is false. A measure does not guarantee zero risk.
A measure does not guarantee zero risk.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q18.stem: Before collecting data with a check sheet, define the items and counting rules.
reasons: Collect comparable data.
This statement is true. Collect comparable data.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q19.stem: In an electron-transfer description, oxidation is a change in which a substance loses electrons.
reasons: The electron-accepting side undergoes reduction.
This statement is true. The electron-accepting side undergoes reduction.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q20.stem: Similar initial letters in standard numbers establish identical revisions and requirements.
reasons: This statement is false. The complete number, revision and scope are needed.
The complete number, revision and scope are needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q21.stem: Hard and annealed copper differ only in name; processing condition and every property are identical.
reasons: This statement is false. Annealing and other treatment change the material condition.
Annealing and other treatment change the material condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q22.stem: A quartz resonator uses properties such as stable vibration.
reasons: It concerns signal oscillation characteristics.
This statement is true. It concerns signal oscillation characteristics.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q23.stem: DC circuits have no transient states, so capacitors are never used in them.
reasons: This statement is false. DC circuits also involve time changes and energy-storing components.
DC circuits also involve time changes and energy-storing components.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q24.stem: Every resistance-scale spacing is equal, and multipliers must never be applied.
reasons: This statement is false. Read the appropriate scale and multiplier.
Read the appropriate scale and multiplier.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q25.stem: An electromagnetic relay uses coil magnetism to move contacts.
reasons: Compare coil and contact ratings.
This statement is true. Compare coil and contact ratings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q26.stem: If a textbook says a method is seldom used now, existing examples need not be identified.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not turn an overview into a guarantee that no equipment of that type exists.
Do not turn an overview into a guarantee that no equipment of that type exists.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q27.stem: Sprues, runners and gates are different parts of the resin path into the product cavity.
reasons: Distinguish the inlet from ejection components.
This statement is true. Distinguish the inlet from ejection components.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q28.stem: Oscilloscope bandwidth and sample rate are different performance specifications.
reasons: Check multiple performance conditions.
This statement is true. Check multiple performance conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q29.stem: All products called biodegradable immediately disappear harmlessly wherever discarded.
reasons: This statement is false. Material names alone do not determine disposal.
Material names alone do not determine disposal.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-theory-q30.stem: Every aqueous solution always has pH only from 0 to 14, regardless of temperature and concentration.
reasons: This statement is false. The textbook’s basic range has assumptions for applicability.
The textbook’s basic range has assumptions for applicability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q01.stem: A “No entry” sign marks an area where you want to retrieve a tool. What should you do?
options: Ignore meaning and consider only its color.
Remove the sign because the tool is needed.
Enter if it is only briefly.
Do not enter without authorization; verify the area and permission procedure.
reasons: Understand and observe meaning and scope as well as color.
Needing a tool does not authorize removing the sign.
Brief entry does not permit unauthorized access.
Read prohibition signs with their area and scope; work convenience does not create exceptions.
This counts the leading eight but omits the two position.
The four position is zero, so the sum is not eight plus four.
Weights are 8, 4, 2 and 1: 8+0+2+0=10.
This reads the digits as a decimal string without binary positional weights.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q03.stem: A designated box contains 37 parts against a requirement of 52. Another warehouse has not been checked. Which report is accurate?
options: The shortage is definitely the responsible person’s mistake.
The designated box is 15 short; the other warehouse remains unverified.
The entire company is definitely 15 short.
reasons: The shortage is verified, but its cause and anyone’s fault are not.
52−37=15 applies to the checked box. Do not report unverified stock or causes as facts.
Only the designated box has been checked, not company-wide stock.
Recording 15 unavailable parts creates a mismatch between actual stock and records.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q04.stem: Corresponding JIS and IEC numbers were found, but their edition years differ. What should be verified?
options: Assume all conditions match because the numbers correspond.
Compare editions, differences and contractual applicability.
Automatically treat the old edition as the latest.
reasons: Destination requirements are part of applicability checks.
Number correspondence does not guarantee identical editions or national differences.
Correspondence may still involve differences and editions; compare the product and requirements.
An older edition cannot automatically be treated as current.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q05.stem: A recovered box is checked for suitability and repeatedly used. What is this primarily?
reasons: Using a product again as it is is reuse; distinguish returning it to material resources through recycling.
The box is reused, not disposed of.
The box remains in its original form rather than being returned to material resources.
Its direct classification is reuse, not merely reducing consumption.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q06.stem: After implementing an improvement, which activity is PDCA Check?
options: Finish explaining without looking at actual items.
Declare the first idea to be the established cause.
Check effects with data using the same definitions and conditions.
reasons: Without actual items or evidence of results, effectiveness cannot be assessed.
Changing standards before verification skips evaluation in Check.
Declaring an initial idea to be a cause is not checking post-implementation effects.
Check evaluates results after implementation and connects evaluation to further improvement or standardization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q07.stem: In the negative-resist concept, what remains after exposure and development?
options: Only copper after removing all resist.
reasons: Development removes unhardened regions in this negative-resist example.
Exposed hardened film remains, and development removes unhardened film. Do not generalize to every resist process.
Development selectively removes film rather than retaining it all.
Hardened film protecting required copper remains at development; this is not complete stripping.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q08.stem: For binary inputs A=1 and B=0, what is two-input AND output?
reasons: AND outputs one only when both inputs are one; B is zero.
AND output depends on inputs, rather than always being one.
AND requires every input to be one. With B=0, the output is zero.
Binary output is zero or one, not an arithmetic total of two.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q09.stem: Which tools create an internal thread in a hole in a plate?
options: A suitable pilot drill and tap.
Only a center punch and reamer.
A suitable pilot drill and die.
reasons: Drill the correct pilot diameter, then tap the internal thread. A die makes external threads.
Marking and finishing a hole do not form internal thread ridges.
Drilling a pilot hole does not yet produce thread ridges.
A pilot hole is needed, but dies are for external threads; taps create internal threads.

mfg1-electrical-mock-07-practical-q10.stem: Which PCB step removes unwanted copper while retaining conductor patterns?
reasons: Exposure patterns photosensitive film rather than removing copper.
Assembly joins components; it does not remove unwanted PCB copper.
Applying protective film alone does not remove copper.
Subtractive etching removes unprotected unwanted copper, unlike component assembly.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q01.stem: A nut driver is used to tighten a compatible hex nut by turning the nut side.
reasons: Also called a box driver, it must fit the nut’s across-flats dimension and available workspace.
This statement is true. Also called a box driver, it must fit the nut’s across-flats dimension and available workspace.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q02.stem: Play when reversing a feed mechanism is called the machined surface’s roughness.
reasons: This statement is false. Reversal play is backlash; surface roughness is the fine unevenness of a machined surface.
Reversal play is backlash; surface roughness is the fine unevenness of a machined surface.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q03.stem: For a screw advancing 0.5 mm per turn and a thimble divided into 50, one division is 0.1 mm.
reasons: This statement is false. 0.5 mm÷50=0.01 mm; 0.1 mm is ten times too large.
0.5 mm÷50=0.01 mm; 0.1 mm is ten times too large.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q04.stem: An aluminum electrolytic capacitor uses an aluminum-oxide film as its dielectric.
reasons: It is an example of conductors separated by dielectric; check polarity and ratings for each type.
This statement is true. It is an example of conductors separated by dielectric; check polarity and ratings for each type.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q05.stem: Reducing counts by changing counting rules alone proves real improvement.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse changed aggregation conditions with improvement.
Do not confuse changed aggregation conditions with improvement.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q06.stem: Any part that looks like resin always remains safely insulating regardless of damage or temperature.
reasons: This statement is false. A material name alone does not guarantee suitability.
A material name alone does not guarantee suitability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q07.stem: Using resistance ratios for voltage division assumes a series connection carrying the same current.
reasons: Check voltage-divider applicability conditions.
This statement is true. Check voltage-divider applicability conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q08.stem: NOT passes its input through unchanged.
reasons: This statement is false. Negation inverts the input.
Negation inverts the input.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q09.stem: hFE is a universal constant for every load, temperature and current.
reasons: This statement is false. Characteristics vary with conditions.
Characteristics vary with conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q10.stem: Even flexible boards require checks of bending positions, cycle counts and other conditions.
reasons: Flexibility does not mean unlimited permission.
This statement is true. Flexibility does not mean unlimited permission.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q11.stem: The voltage ratio of an ideal transformer always depends only on the difference between its two turn counts.
reasons: This statement is false. Use V2/V1=N2/N1.
Use V2/V1=N2/N1.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q12.stem: Observing reversed motion alone does not establish a particular valve failure.
reasons: Classifying symptoms differs from establishing the cause.
This statement is true. Classifying symptoms differs from establishing the cause.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q13.stem: Check management condition for torque tools requiring calibration and pre-use checks.
reasons: Tool integrity and the specified range matter.
This statement is true. Tool integrity and the specified range matter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q14.stem: Pilot holes must equal the nominal thread diameter exactly for every material.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish pilot diameter from nominal diameter.
Distinguish pilot diameter from nominal diameter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q15.stem: Practical multiple-choice questions may test judgment and planning as well as knowledge.
reasons: Check the method and question format described in the materials.
This statement is true. Check the method and question format described in the materials.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q16.stem: Stay clear of suspended loads and follow designated handling methods.
reasons: Consider dropping and unexpected movement of the load.
This statement is true. Consider dropping and unexpected movement of the load.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q17.stem: Design quality means actual manufactured characteristics, while manufacturing quality means only the design’s intended characteristics.
reasons: This statement is false. Design quality concerns intended characteristics; manufacturing quality concerns achieved workmanship. Do not reverse them.
Design quality concerns intended characteristics; manufacturing quality concerns achieved workmanship. Do not reverse them.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q18.stem: Aligned points for two variables eliminate any need to consider other factors.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish correlation from causation.
Distinguish correlation from causation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q19.stem: Specific gravity is a ratio to a reference density and has no unit.
reasons: Distinguish density from a density ratio.
This statement is true. Distinguish density from a density ratio.
This statement is false. 210×297 mm is A4.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q21.stem: The main purpose of laminating a core from thin sheets is to increase losses caused by flux changes.
reasons: This statement is false. Thin laminations and similar measures reduce losses caused by changing flux.
Thin laminations and similar measures reduce losses caused by changing flux.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q22.stem: The passive-component classification does not imply absence of residual charge or heating.
reasons: It also includes components storing and releasing energy.
This statement is true. It also includes components storing and releasing energy.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q23.stem: At a node, total current flowing in must equal total current flowing out.
reasons: Check the current balance.
This statement is true. Check the current balance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q24.stem: Connecting a measuring instrument never affects the circuit or measured value.
reasons: This statement is false. Consider the measurement system’s influence.
Consider the measurement system’s influence.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q25.stem: Some SSR products require checking off-state leakage, heat and other conditions.
reasons: Functional off and safe isolation differ.
This statement is true. Functional off and safe isolation differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q26.stem: Environmental testing and a one-off functional check examine different conditions.
reasons: Evidence under the specified environment is needed.
This statement is true. Evidence under the specified environment is needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q27.stem: Part release is unrelated to mold design, so draft angles need not be checked.
reasons: This statement is false. Ease of removal is also controlled through mold design.
Ease of removal is also controlled through mold design.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q28.stem: Voltage-waveform rise and timing differences between signals may be observed.
reasons: These concern signal changes over time.
This statement is true. These concern signal changes over time.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q29.stem: Every FRP type has an entirely scratch-proof surface and no disposal requirements.
reasons: This statement is false. Consider constraints as well as benefits.
Consider constraints as well as benefits.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-theory-q30.stem: A chemical container may display several hazards.
reasons: Check multiple items of hazard information.
This statement is true. Check multiple items of hazard information.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q01.stem: In a sine-wave circuit containing only an ideal inductor, what is current’s phase relative to voltage?
reasons: Sine-wave voltage and current have a defined phase.
Ideal inductors produce lag; lead confuses them with ideal capacitors.
Ideal-inductor current lags voltage. Real circuits also involve resistance and other effects.
An ideal inductor alone produces a phase difference rather than equal phase.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q02.stem: Why does output continue after releasing the start button in a basic holding circuit?
options: An output-related contact creates a path retaining the start condition.
Inputs and outputs have no relationship.
Every relay remains energized forever without power.
Only because the stop button is disabled.
reasons: A contact maintains the state after operation. Trace separately whether stop conditions release it.
The input, contacts and coil form the holding relationship.
Ordinary electromagnetic relays do not remain energized forever without power.
Self-holding does not mean disabling stop; stop conditions must release it.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q03.stem: 12 mA enters a node and divides into 4 mA and an unknown branch. What is the unknown current?
reasons: Input and output totals match:12=4+I, so I=8 mA.
The ratio12/4 does not calculate the unknown branch current.
Adding outgoing4 to incoming12 violates node conservation.
The product12×4 is not a current-sum conservation equation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q04.stem: Glass-fiber and carbon-fiber boards look equally black and are mixed together. What should you do?
options: Assume all FRP is perfectly insulating.
Ignore material records if the shape fits.
Assume all properties match because colors match.
Compare material and required properties; do not substitute by appearance.
reasons: FRP containing carbon fiber cannot universally be called perfectly insulating.
Shape compatibility does not replace checking material identity and specifications.
Identical black appearance does not establish matching fiber and resin properties.
Fiber and resin affect electrical and mechanical properties. Shape and appearance alone cannot guarantee conformity.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q05.stem: For binary x=1 and y=0, what is NOT(x+y)?
reasons: Binary values are zero or one, not two.
OR gives one, but the outer NOT changes it to zero.
x+y is OR, yielding one; negating gives zero. De Morgan’s NOT x AND NOT y also gives zero.
The result depends on inputs, so the function is not constantly one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q06.stem: A basic off-delay output is on when its input turns off. With a four-second setting, when does the output turn off?
options: It stays on forever regardless of input.
reasons: Basic off-delay switches off after the set time from input-off. Check product power and holding conditions.
The setting is four seconds, not permanent holding.
Basic off-delay retains output for the set time rather than switching off immediately.
Timing starts at input-off, not before input-on.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q07.stem: A scatter plot suggests a relationship between temperature and defect rate. Which conclusion is justified?
options: Declare temperature the cause without verification.
Treat it as a candidate relationship and investigate other factors and conditions.
Delete all points to remove correlation.
reasons: Correlation alone does not prove temperature causes defects.
Correlation does not establish causation. Check conditions and other factors to verify causes.
Deleting points loses measured facts and prevents checking the relationship.
Specification changes do not verify causes and cannot be made without authorization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q08.stem: After soldering, solder has connected to an adjacent pad that was not intended to be connected. Which condition does this describe?
reasons: A solder connection may eliminate required insulation spacing.
Unwanted conductive bridging is not a normal tolerance assessment.
Flux presence differs from a metallic bridge to an adjacent pad.
An unwanted bridge joins neighboring areas. Use approved rework and reinspection.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q09.stem: A designated terminal shelf has a lower limit of 10 and upper limit of 30, but contains7. Which report follows the three fixed rules?
options: Call the 23-unit gap from the maximum a defect count.
Report that the specified item is three below the lower limit.
The shelf location means the stock is appropriate.
Add other parts to make up the number.
reasons: The gap from 30 is not a defect count; the relevant shortage is three below the lower limit.
The rules control location, item and quantity. Seven is three below ten; mixing other items does not fix it.
Correct location alone does not meet the quantity condition.
Other items do not resolve the required item’s shortage and may cause wrong use.

mfg1-electrical-mock-08-practical-q10.stem: A full-scale100 scale reads40 with a50 mA range selected. What is the measurement?
reasons: 40 is the scale indication before converting to the selected 50 mA range.
50 mA is full scale, not the 40/100 pointer position.
40/100×50 mA=20 mA. Do not use the scale number alone.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q01.stem: The 1.5 mm² marking of a stranded conductor indicates its cross-sectional area, not a diameter of 1.5 mm.
reasons: mm² is area and mm is length; check the correspondence in the application table.
This statement is true. mm² is area and mm is length; check the correspondence in the application table.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q02.stem: If the smallest graduation is 0.01 mm, the error is always within 0.01 mm under all conditions of use.
