reasons: This statement is false. Orientation, contact and condition affect actual measurements.
Orientation, contact and condition affect actual measurements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q03.stem: Even with a large measurement range, an instrument cannot be used on equipment exceeding its safety rating.
reasons: Functional range and safety rating are separate requirements.
This statement is true. Functional range and safety rating are separate requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q04.stem: Product numbers and inspection-standard revisions have no bearing on traceability.
reasons: This statement is false. It is necessary to know what was assessed and against which standard.
It is necessary to know what was assessed and against which standard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q05.stem: If the average is at the specification midpoint, every product is necessarily within specification.
reasons: This statement is false. The average and variation provide different information.
The average and variation provide different information.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q06.stem: Check line types to avoid mistaking a centerline for an outline to cut.
reasons: Different line types have different meanings.
This statement is true. Different line types have different meanings.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q07.stem: On a common four-band resistor, the third band is read as the multiplier.
reasons: Distinguish the first two bands, multiplier and tolerance.
This statement is true. Distinguish the first two bands, multiplier and tolerance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q08.stem: Passing current through one diode always immediately produces perfectly smooth, constant DC.
reasons: This statement is false. Rectification and smoothing are different.
Rectification and smoothing are different.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q09.stem: Scheduled replacement can reduce failures while also incurring the cost of replacing parts that are still usable.
reasons: Consider both preventive benefits and replacement costs.
This statement is true. Consider both preventive benefits and replacement costs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q10.stem: A voltage regulator’s supply stabilization differs from A/D conversion of a signal.
reasons: Power-supply functions and signal conversion are separate.
This statement is true. Power-supply functions and signal conversion are separate.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q11.stem: Measured grease penetration and all classification numbers always increase or decrease in the same direction.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse different indication systems.
Do not confuse different indication systems.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q12.stem: Every device that opens contacts can safely interrupt short-circuit current without checking its ratings.
reasons: This statement is false. Check breaking capacity and application.
Check breaking capacity and application.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q13.stem: Logistics quality includes the correct goods, quantity, destination and promised delivery date.
reasons: Delivery accuracy is also a customer requirement.
This statement is true. Delivery accuracy is also a customer requirement.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q14.stem: Burrs on a cut surface affect appearance only and have no effect on installation.
reasons: This statement is false. Also inspect effects on subsequent processes.
Also inspect effects on subsequent processes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q15.stem: The basic method for a common metalworking file is to apply maximum force only on the return stroke.
reasons: This statement is false. Release force on the return stroke.
Release force on the return stroke.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q16.stem: Combine company management with workers following procedures to reduce hazards.
reasons: These responsibilities do not replace one another.
This statement is true. These responsibilities do not replace one another.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q17.stem: Fire-extinguisher and AED signs help locate that equipment.
reasons: Distinguish equipment signs from evacuation signs.
This statement is true. Distinguish equipment signs from evacuation signs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q18.stem: The three actuals principle always requires touching live parts with bare hands to establish the cause.
reasons: This statement is false. Direct verification also requires safe conditions.
Direct verification also requires safe conditions.
It is a management-system standard.
This statement is true. It is a management-system standard.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q20.stem: Every used or recovered battery has no voltage and may be short-circuited.
reasons: This statement is false. Remaining energy does not automatically disappear when a battery becomes used.
Remaining energy does not automatically disappear when a battery becomes used.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q21.stem: Diameter φ and radius R indicate different dimensions of a circle.
reasons: The diameter is twice the radius.
This statement is true. The diameter is twice the radius.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q22.stem: If a terminal hole fits the screw, no conductor-side compatibility check is needed.
reasons: This statement is false. Both sides must meet their applicable ranges.
Both sides must meet their applicable ranges.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q23.stem: Choose drills and end mills after checking cutting-edge locations and applications.
reasons: Match the applications of the machine and tool.
This statement is true. Match the applications of the machine and tool.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q24.stem: The only distinction between n-type and p-type is that the entire materials carry negative and positive charge respectively.
reasons: This statement is false. Understand carriers and impurities separately.
Understand carriers and impurities separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q25.stem: If the total quantity agrees, held products may be recorded as completed products.
reasons: This statement is false. Product states must also be identified.
Product states must also be identified.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q26.stem: Basic on-delay and off-delay timers delay different transitions.
reasons: Trace the timing of the on or off transition.
This statement is true. Trace the timing of the on or off transition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q27.stem: One more failure always means a higher failure rate, regardless of operating hours.
reasons: This statement is false. A rate needs its denominator.
A rate needs its denominator.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q28.stem: In the negative-resist concept example, the protective film hardened by exposure remains.
reasons: Check which film remains for the process used.
This statement is true. Check which film remains for the process used.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q29.stem: Increasing the number of poles decreases synchronous speed at the same frequency.
reasons: Ns is inversely proportional to the number of poles.
This statement is true. Ns is inversely proportional to the number of poles.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-theory-q30.stem: Even if a ruler’s end is worn away, its reference point never changes on any design.
reasons: This statement is false. Check the reference-point design and condition.
Check the reference-point design and condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q01.stem: A resistor is marked 1 kΩ with a tolerance of ±5%. Which is its marked tolerance range?
reasons: 5% of 1000 Ω is 50 Ω, giving 950–1050 Ω. Also check ratings and inspection conditions.
This uses ±0.5%, one decimal order different from ±5%.
It omits the lower side and excludes the permitted 950–999 Ω range.
This is ±50%, rather than the specified ±5%.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q02.stem: Calculate the synchronous speed of a 50 Hz, six-pole induction machine using Ns=120 f/p.
reasons: 120×50/6=1000 min⁻¹. This is rotating-field speed, not a guarantee of actual rotor speed under load.
3000 is the synchronous speed for two poles at 50 Hz, not six poles.
Divide by six poles; do not multiply to get 36000.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q03.stem: A transformer’s secondary is unloaded while its primary receives voltage under rated conditions. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: With no load, the primary must also have no voltage.
Core loss may still occur; do not assume zero power or no hazard.
Touch the copper winding to check safety.
reasons: Supply voltage remains on the primary even when the secondary is unloaded.
Core loss due to changing flux can remain at no load. Primary voltage and hazards do not disappear.
Touching an energized winding risks electric shock and other harm.
Core flux and other conditions depend on frequency, so specified conditions cannot be ignored.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q04.stem: A component looks normal but may have been handled without ESD protection. What should you do?
options: Touch its terminals with bare hands to test performance.
Accept it unconditionally because no spark was seen.
Remove all packaging and leave it exposed.
Do not rule out damage from appearance alone; verify and identify it under the procedure.
reasons: Bare-hand contact may introduce further static electricity.
ESD damage may occur without a visible spark.
Leaving it unpackaged removes protection against ESD and other hazards.
ESD damage may be invisible. Follow the handling-history, inspection and hold procedures.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q05.stem: The number of failures is unchanged from last year, but operating hours halved. What is needed for comparison?
options: Shorten the replacement interval as far as possible without evidence.
Assume the same condition because failure counts match.
Discard records and do not compare.
Account for operating hours, production volume and other conditions.
reasons: An unsupported interval reduction does not evaluate the comparison or establish appropriate replacement.
With half the hours, the same count changes the failures-per-hour comparison.
Discarding records prevents comparison including operating conditions.
Failure counts alone cannot establish condition. Also review use conditions, downtime and repair details.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q06.stem: A wire has shifted at a terminal whose solder has not solidified. What is appropriate?
options: Pull it hard just before solidification.
Skip cooling and bend the neighboring terminal.
Keep the joint still during cooling, then check rework under the criteria.
Ship without inspection if the joint is shiny.
reasons: Pulling during solidification moves the joint and can cause a bad connection.
Bending the neighboring part before cooling transmits force to and disturbs the joint.
Movement during solidification disrupts the joint. Inspect after cooling, then use approved rework and reassessment.
Shininess alone cannot establish the joint’s condition or internal defects.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q07.stem: A relay’s coil voltage matches, but its contact capacity is below the load. What is appropriate?
options: Use it unconditionally because the coil matches.
Assume an SSR needs no heat check.
Find suitable equipment that also meets contact requirements.
Remove load protection and use it.
reasons: The contact capacity is insufficient; coil voltage alone is not enough.
SSRs also require rating checks for heating, heat dissipation and other conditions.
Coil and contacts have separate ratings. Shape and coil voltage alone do not establish load-switching suitability.
Removing protection does not resolve insufficient capacity and increases fault hazards.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q08.stem: Someone proposes adding gloves for work near a rotating drill press. How should this be assessed?
options: Grab rotating chips with cotton work gloves.
Check entanglement hazards and required PPE in the work procedure.
Assume gloves always improve safety for every job.
reasons: The gloves and hand may be pulled in by rotating chips.
Gloves can create entanglement hazards depending on the task. Match training and PPE to the specific hazards.
Gloves can be caught by rotating parts and are not universally safer.
OJT does not remove the need to check safety procedures and PPE.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q09.stem: Dimensions changed after a material lot change despite the same tool settings. What should be checked?
options: Compare 4 M changes, including material, and measurement conditions.
Decide the operator is the only cause.
Rewrite only the average to the specification midpoint.
reasons: 4 M includes people, machines, materials and methods. Investigate changes and results using actual items and records.
The material lot changed, so the cause cannot be restricted to the operator.
Rewriting data changes neither dimensions nor cause and destroys record reliability.
Discarding lot records prevents relating the change timing to dimensional changes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-01-practical-q10.stem: Five boxes contain 12 products each, but the delivery note states 54. What discrepancy needs verification?
options: Reducing cushioning will reconcile the quantity.
The actual total is 60, six more than the note’s 54.
Ignore the quantity difference if the destination matches.
reasons: Cushioning quantity does not resolve a product-count discrepancy.
12×5=60. Find the cause of the six-unit difference and reconcile goods and documents before dispatch.
A correct destination does not resolve an incorrect quantity.
12×5=60 actual products, not 54.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q01.stem: Repositioning during solder solidification has no effect on joint quality.
reasons: This statement is false. Hold the joint still and check it against criteria after cooling.
Hold the joint still and check it against criteria after cooling.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q02.stem: With 0.01 mm graduations, a thimble reading of 17 contributes 17 mm.
reasons: This statement is false. Add 17×0.01 mm.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q03.stem: A period is the time until the same state recurs in the same direction.
reasons: Choose corresponding points in the cycle correctly.
This statement is true. Choose corresponding points in the cycle correctly.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q04.stem: Do not assume zero stock at a storage location that has not been checked.
reasons: Separate verified scope from what remains unverified.
This statement is true. Separate verified scope from what remains unverified.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q05.stem: A Pareto chart only orders counts from smallest to largest and does not use cumulative percentages.
reasons: This statement is false. It helps identify the larger categories.
It helps identify the larger categories.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q06.stem: For drawings containing older symbols, check the legend and applicable standards.
reasons: Standards and revisions may differ.
This statement is true. Standards and revisions may differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q07.stem: Parallel branches connected between the same two points must have different voltages for different resistance values.
reasons: This statement is false. The potential difference between their endpoints is shared.
The potential difference between their endpoints is shared.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q08.stem: Both ESD protection and protection of people from electric shock must be satisfied.
reasons: ESD measures must also be compatible with safety conditions.
This statement is true. ESD measures must also be compatible with safety conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q09.stem: Coils and capacitors have the same construction and are interchangeable in every circuit.
reasons: This statement is false. Their construction and properties differ.
Their construction and properties differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q10.stem: The term printed wiring board means there is no need to distinguish before and after component installation.
reasons: This statement is false. Make the actual production stage clear.
Make the actual production stage clear.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q11.stem: Feedback returns the detected state to compensate for the difference from a command.
reasons: Check the relationship between detection and command.
This statement is true. Check the relationship between detection and command.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q12.stem: Usable operation during a power outage depends on equipment functions and conditions.
reasons: Check functions, capacity, wiring conditions and related requirements.
This statement is true. Check functions, capacity, wiring conditions and related requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q13.stem: A hex bolt’s nominal diameter may be used directly as the across-flats dimension for every tool.
reasons: This statement is false. These dimensions describe different features.
These dimensions describe different features.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q14.stem: Thermocouple measurement also depends on the reference junction, compensation leads and polarity.
reasons: Verify the consistency of the measurement system.
This statement is true. Verify the consistency of the measurement system.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q15.stem: Moving a conductor always produces sustained induced current even in an open circuit.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish induced voltage from current flowing in a circuit.
Distinguish induced voltage from current flowing in a circuit.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q16.stem: When work changes, reassess hazards and required training.
reasons: Check conditions appropriate to the changed work.
This statement is true. Check conditions appropriate to the changed work.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q17.stem: OSHMS means creating a plan once and never checking results after implementation.
reasons: This statement is false. It is a continuous management cycle.
It is a continuous management cycle.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q18.stem: Responding to abnormalities may include holding products, reporting and checking the affected scope.
reasons: Trace the items and scope to prevent unintended release.
This statement is true. Trace the items and scope to prevent unintended release.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q19.stem: pH has the same dimension as density and is expressed in kg/m³.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse physical quantities and indicators.
Do not confuse physical quantities and indicators.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q20.stem: For exports, compare the standards required by the destination country and contract.
reasons: Check the requesting destination and differences in corresponding standards.
This statement is true. Check the requesting destination and differences in corresponding standards.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q21.stem: Every ladder-instruction symbol unconditionally equals the physical state of a real switch.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish input, logic and output roles.
Distinguish input, logic and output roles.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q22.stem: A thermistor is merely a zero-resistance wire under all conditions regardless of temperature.
reasons: This statement is false. Its temperature characteristics are used in its application.
Its temperature characteristics are used in its application.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q23.stem: In a sine-wave circuit containing only an ideal capacitor, current leads voltage.
reasons: Distinguish the phase relationships of ideal inductors and capacitors.
This statement is true. Distinguish the phase relationships of ideal inductors and capacitors.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q24.stem: Memory ICs and power regulators are functionally interchangeable in every application.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish storage from supply stabilization.
Distinguish storage from supply stabilization.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q25.stem: Pushbuttons include automatic-return and maintained-state designs.
reasons: Check the component type.
This statement is true. Check the component type.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q26.stem: Because SF6 is colorless and odorless, it may be released into the atmosphere without authorization.
reasons: This statement is false. Smell alone does not determine safety or environmental impact.
Smell alone does not determine safety or environmental impact.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q27.stem: A warehouse-method name alone does not determine acceptable PPM for every shipment.
reasons: Check scope, period and contractual conditions.
This statement is true. Check scope, period and contractual conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q28.stem: LCR readings never depend on measurement frequency, so settings need not be recorded.
reasons: This statement is false. Align component and instrument conditions.
Align component and instrument conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q29.stem: Reducing industrial packaging materials still requires meeting necessary protection requirements.
reasons: Do not sacrifice protection for cost alone.
This statement is true. Do not sacrifice protection for cost alone.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-theory-q30.stem: A permanent magnet’s remanence and coercivity are different properties.
reasons: Check each according to the application.
This statement is true. Check each according to the application.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q01.stem: Match a solar cell, storage battery and power conditioner to their roles.
options: All only store electricity in the same way.
Generation, storage, and DC/AC conversion or related functions.
Drawing wiring diagrams, packaging and generation.
reasons: These are not identical storage devices; they generate, store and convert respectively.
Generation, storage and conversion differ. Outage use depends on system functions and conditions.
Solar cells generate and storage batteries store; these assignments are reversed.
This confuses energy functions with drawing and packaging activities.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q02.stem: For binary inputs x=0 and y=1, what is NOT(x·y)?
reasons: This leaves the AND result unchanged and omits the outer NOT.
Binary results are zero or one, not two.
AND gives zero, and its negation is one. NOT x OR NOT y also gives one.
Applying NOT means the result is not zero like x in this case.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q03.stem: A hydraulic cylinder moves in the correct direction but slowly. Which way of organizing information is appropriate?
options: Raise pressure to maximum without authorization.
Record force, direction and speed as the same quantity.
Record flow and other speed-related factors as checks.
reasons: Unauthorized pressure increases risk exceeding ratings and do not substitute for checking flow.
Force relates to pressure, speed to flow and other factors; direction is separate information.
Flow affects speed but does not alone establish the fault location. Separate observations and verify through approved checks.
Correct direction and low speed alone do not establish a directional-valve fault.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q04.stem: Under identical conditions, defects are 12 label cases, six scratches and two missing items. What cumulative percentage is represented by the two largest categories?
reasons: 60% covers only the largest label category of 12 cases.
The two categories total 18, not 16 of 20.
18 is the count; the percentage is 18/20×100.
There are 20 cases overall and 18 in the top two, so 90%. Assess safety-critical small categories separately.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q05.stem: After assembly, leftover screws do not match the recorded count. What should you do?
options: Discard extras where they cannot be seen.
Check the remainder and inside the enclosure, and report possible missing or foreign items.
Pass them silently to the next worker.
reasons: Hiding and discarding extras obstructs reconciliation and cause investigation.
A count mismatch can indicate foreign or missing items. Reconcile actual items and records without concealing unverified conditions.
Changing records alone conceals possible missing or foreign items.
A silent handover fails to communicate the count difference or foreign-item concern.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q06.stem: Hand tapping suddenly becomes difficult. What should you do?
options: Do not force it; check pilot hole, tool, chips and other conditions under the procedure.
Remove PPE and clear chips by hand.
Add an extension pipe for more force.
reasons: Forcing increased resistance can break the tap or damage threads. Verify conditions and use the specified treatment.
Releasing the clamp lets the workpiece move, compromising accuracy and safety.
Bare-hand chip removal risks cuts and violates the specified method.
Excessive force using an extension may break the tap.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q07.stem: A small round hole needs internal hand finishing. How should the tool be selected?
options: Force the largest flat file into the hole.
Pull hard only on the return stroke.
Choose a file section and size matching the curve, while checking surfaces to retain.
Remove material without ever checking dimensions.
reasons: A large flat file does not fit the curved hole and may damage its shape.
Pulling hard against the normal cutting direction does not produce the intended cut.
Match section, size and cutting direction to the purpose; assess effects on retained geometry, not just whether it fits.
Without dimensional checks, overcutting and shape defects go undetected.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q08.stem: You want to connect PSE-marked equipment to a system with another voltage. What is appropriate?
options: PSE alone proves suitability for every voltage.
Separately verify ratings, application and connection conditions.
The marking shape grants the worker a qualification.
Removing earth always makes it usable.
reasons: PSE alone does not establish suitability for another voltage; check ratings.
PSE does not guarantee every application, voltage or work qualification.
A product marking is separate from worker qualifications.
Removing earth does not resolve voltage mismatch and undermines shock protection.
1 mm=1000 μm, so 0.25×1000=250 μm. Use consistent prefix factors.
25 μm is ten times too small.
Multiply by 1000 from mm to μm, rather than dividing.

mfg1-electrical-mock-06-practical-q10.stem: A symmetric, zero-centered waveform spans six divisions peak to trough at 2 V/div. What is its amplitude?
reasons: This doubles the 12 V peak-to-peak value, opposite to the amplitude conversion.
12 V is peak-to-peak; amplitude is half.
Half of six divisions is three, which still must be multiplied by 2 V/div.
Peak-to-peak is 6×2=12 V. Symmetry about zero makes amplitude half, 6 V.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q01.stem: For a proportional straight line with voltage V horizontally and current I vertically, its slope equals resistance R.
reasons: This statement is false. Its slope is I/V=1/R; resistance is the reciprocal of the slope.
Its slope is I/V=1/R; resistance is the reciprocal of the slope.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q02.stem: In a magnetic starter combining a contactor and thermal overload relay, distinguish load switching from overload detection.
reasons: The contactor switches the load and the thermal relay detects overload; the thermal relay alone is not the main-circuit interrupter.
This statement is true. The contactor switches the load and the thermal relay detects overload; the thermal relay alone is not the main-circuit interrupter.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q03.stem: Because star-delta starting reduces current, it suits every motor regardless of winding and load torque.
reasons: This statement is false. Compatible windings and ratings are prerequisites. Starting torque also changes, so check load and protection.
Compatible windings and ratings are prerequisites. Starting torque also changes, so check load and protection.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q04.stem: Workers may change risk scores and acceptance limits according to their mood each time.
reasons: This statement is false. Use consistent assessment criteria.
Use consistent assessment criteria.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q05.stem: Even at scale 2:1, written dimensions state the required real dimensions.
reasons: Image size and written dimensions are separate.
This statement is true. Image size and written dimensions are separate.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q06.stem: Mica and ceramics are examples of inorganic insulation after applying the correction.
reasons: Apply the correction excluding natural rubber from inorganic materials.
This statement is true. Apply the correction excluding natural rubber from inorganic materials.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q07.stem: A two-terminal diode works identically in every condition even when reversed.
reasons: This statement is false. It is a directional device.
It is a directional device.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q08.stem: Two-input AND gives zero for 00,01 and 10, and one for 11.
reasons: Output occurs only when every required condition is met.
This statement is true. Output occurs only when every required condition is met.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q09.stem: High gain permits use beyond maximum allowable power dissipation.
reasons: This statement is false. Signal characteristics do not authorize exceeding limits.
Signal characteristics do not authorize exceeding limits.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q10.stem: Lubricate using the specified material, locations, quantities and intervals.
reasons: Appearance alone does not establish suitability.
This statement is true. Appearance alone does not establish suitability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q11.stem: Every step-up transformer has higher primary voltage than secondary voltage.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish the power-receiving side from relative voltage magnitude.
Distinguish the power-receiving side from relative voltage magnitude.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q12.stem: Turning off a hydraulic pump allows every pipe to be loosened freely immediately.
reasons: This statement is false. Address residual pressure and load-induced movement.
Address residual pressure and load-induced movement.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q13.stem: Taps make internal threads; dies make external threads.
reasons: Distinguish the machining target of each tool.
This statement is true. Distinguish the machining target of each tool.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q14.stem: If a tap suddenly becomes difficult, always finish by using an extension bar.
reasons: This statement is false. Prevent breakage and defective threads.
Prevent breakage and defective threads.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q15.stem: Deepen skills understanding through new practice rather than removing examination questions.
reasons: Do not remove or share actual examination content.
This statement is true. Do not remove or share actual examination content.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q16.stem: Do not use a liquid marked non-potable for drinking.
reasons: Observe the prohibited use identified by the marking.
This statement is true. Observe the prohibited use identified by the marking.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q17.stem: In QCD, C means delivery date and D means cost.
reasons: This statement is false. C means Cost and D means Delivery.
C means Cost and D means Delivery.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q18.stem: Treat factors written in a cause-and-effect diagram as candidates to verify with evidence.
reasons: Organizing and verifying are separate stages.
This statement is true. Organizing and verifying are separate stages.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q19.stem: Reduce concerns preventing waste, while Reuse concerns repeated use.
reasons: Distinguish the roles within3 R correctly.
This statement is true. Distinguish the roles within3 R correctly.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q20.stem: If drawing shapes look similar, skip the drawing number and revision.
reasons: This statement is false. Identify the correct item.
Identify the correct item.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q21.stem: Thermal class F155 unconditionally permits every product to operate at 155°C ambient.
reasons: This statement is false. Check the insulation system and operating conditions.
Check the insulation system and operating conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q22.stem: A lathe and milling machine normally rotate different items.
reasons: Distinguish workpiece rotation from tool rotation.
This statement is true. Distinguish workpiece rotation from tool rotation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q23.stem: The loop law requires adding all source and resistor voltages without signs.
reasons: This statement is false. Define traversal direction and polarities.
Define traversal direction and polarities.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q24.stem: Every DMM without exception lacks an AC current range.
reasons: This statement is false. Check functions for each model.
Check functions for each model.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q25.stem: Bimetal combines metals with different thermal expansion coefficients.
reasons: It uses deformation caused by unequal expansion.
This statement is true. It uses deformation caused by unequal expansion.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q26.stem: Insulation resistance and withstand voltage are not two names for one identical test.
reasons: Purposes, equipment and methods differ.
This statement is true. Purposes, equipment and methods differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q27.stem: Because molds are rigid, humidity and rust have no relation to their quality or storage.
reasons: This statement is false. Storage conditions affect the next production run.
Storage conditions affect the next production run.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q28.stem: Photoelectric sensors and mechanical switches use different detection principles.
reasons: Check sensing principle and output.
This statement is true. Check sensing principle and output.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q29.stem: A metal-base board always directly shorts every wiring pattern to the same metal.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish heat dissipation from electrical insulation.
Distinguish heat dissipation from electrical insulation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-theory-q30.stem: Careful tool handling and returning tools to designated locations are safety behaviors.
reasons: Follow handling practices preventing drops and injuries.
This statement is true. Follow handling practices preventing drops and injuries.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q01.stem: A part fell but did not strike anyone. What response supports improvement?
options: Erase the event because nobody was injured.
Drop it again under the same conditions.
Record conditions and measures as a near miss.
Decide it was only operator inattention.
reasons: Even without injury, it is hazard information needed for prevention.
Repeating the drop may cause another accident.
Events without injury still reveal hazards. Check possible causes and review effectiveness.
Blaming inattention without examining placement or equipment misses possible causes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q02.stem: You need physical mounting positions but have only an electrical connection diagram. Which additional drawing is needed?
options: Only the colors of lines in the same diagram.
reasons: A developed diagram shows functional connections rather than physical mounting positions.
Line colors may aid circuit identification but do not establish physical layout.
Terminal correspondence does not replace a layout showing locations and dimensions.
Connection and physical arrangement are different information. Use an appropriate layout and verify drawing number and revision.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q03.stem: For ideal point charges with unchanged charges and medium, separation triples. What happens to force magnitude?
reasons: Increasing separation weakens force rather than tripling it.
Coulomb force is inversely proportional to separation squared:1/3²=1/9.
It is inverse-square, not simply inverse-distance.
Ninefold force corresponds to reducing separation to one third.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q04.stem: A constant DC power of 8 W is consumed for 45 minutes. What is the energy?
reasons: This divides power by time instead of using P×t.
8 Wh corresponds to one hour, not45 minutes.
45 minutes=0.75 h, so 8×0.75=6 Wh. Convert minutes to hours.
This treats45 minutes as45 hours without conversion.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q05.stem: A breaker operated and there is a burning smell. What should you do?
options: Replace it with a higher rating without authorization.
Follow safety procedures, report the abnormality and await cause verification.
Repeatedly reclose it to see whether the smell disappears.
Use a disconnector to substitute for fault-current interruption.
reasons: Raising the rating may leave wiring and other intended items unprotected.
Repeated reclosing increases fault and restart hazards. Respect device roles and use approved action.
Reclosing before checking the cause may cause short circuits, fire or unexpected restart.
A disconnector does not substitute for a breaker’s fault-current interruption role.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q06.stem: A scheduled pre-failure inspection records a wear trend. What is the appropriate purpose?
options: Use it to decide how to prevent failures or stoppages.
Guarantee unlimited life because it was inspected.
reasons: Preventive maintenance includes understanding condition and acting before failure; records and specification checks remain necessary.
Actual failure and repair records still support improvement.
Inspection establishes condition at that time, not unlimited lifetime.
Preventive replacements still require matching part specifications to equipment.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q07.stem: A copper part barely attracts a magnet. What judgment is appropriate?
options: Verify conductivity and application specifications separately from magnetism.
Adopt it as insulation because it does not attract a magnet.
Replace a core with it without checking material.
Assume a conductor works at every temperature.
reasons: Magnetism and conductivity differ; magnetic response alone does not determine electrical use.
Copper conducts even if weakly attracted, so this does not make it insulation.
Do not substitute core material without comparing magnetic and material requirements.
Conductors also have temperature and rating limits.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q08.stem: Before voltage measurement, the red lead remains in the current input. What should be done first?
options: Select maximum current range and connect in parallel.
Keep it disconnected and verify the specified terminals, function and range.
Apply it directly across the supply.
reasons: Removing a fuse does not resolve the terminal/function mismatch.
Increasing current range does not make it a voltage-measurement connection.
A current input connected across a source may short it. Match quantity, terminals and function before connecting.
A current input placed across the source risks a short circuit.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q09.stem: The actual measurement location differs from the QC process chart control point. What should you do?
options: Modify the chart from old memory.
Choose the convenient one without approval.
Check revisions and instructions, then ask the responsible person about the discrepancy.
reasons: Memory-based modifications compromise approved control conditions.
Unauthorized selection does not verify current required controls.
The discrepancy requires checking, not abandoning measurement control.
Check the latest revision and approved conditions; do not remove control points independently.

mfg1-electrical-mock-09-practical-q10.stem: Which instrument measures magnetic flux density?
reasons: A gaussmeter measures magnetic flux density. Illuminance concerns light; calipers and height gauges concern dimensions.
A height gauge measures height and related dimensions, not flux density.
An illuminance meter measures illumination, not magnetic flux density.
A caliper measures dimensions rather than magnetic flux density.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q01.stem: Passing a finished product’s dimensional inspection automatically passes separately specified weight and strength checks.
reasons: This statement is false. Dimensions, weight and strength are separate checks; independently meet structural-inspection and other requirements.
Dimensions, weight and strength are separate checks; independently meet structural-inspection and other requirements.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q02.stem: When comparing injection molding for small batches and mass production, assess initial tooling cost separately from processing time per item.
reasons: Quantity changes the per-item share of initial cost, so processing time alone does not determine total cost.
This statement is true. Quantity changes the per-item share of initial cost, so processing time alone does not determine total cost.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q03.stem: In PCB manufacture, circuit-pattern photosensitive film and solder resist always mean the same material and process.
reasons: This statement is false. Circuit-forming photosensitive film differs in purpose and process from solder resist covering areas where solder is not wanted.
Circuit-forming photosensitive film differs in purpose and process from solder resist covering areas where solder is not wanted.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q04.stem: For an unstable stand, consider placement and support as well as warnings.
reasons: Measures changing the hazardous physical condition are also necessary.
This statement is true. Measures changing the hazardous physical condition are also necessary.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q05.stem: Enlarging or reducing a copy does not change the required dimensions written on the drawing.
reasons: Check dimension annotations and units.
This statement is true. Check dimension annotations and units.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q06.stem: Every internal part of a transformer should use the same conducting material.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish conducting, magnetic and insulating roles.
Distinguish conducting, magnetic and insulating roles.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q07.stem: Because reverse leakage and breakdown exist, do not assume reverse current is always zero.
reasons: Use real devices within their specified conditions.
This statement is true. Use real devices within their specified conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q08.stem: Matching logic truth tables does not necessarily establish an adequate safety circuit.
reasons: Functional logic and safety validity are separate.
This statement is true. Functional logic and safety validity are separate.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q09.stem: A/D conversion only means changing digital values into analog quantities.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish conversion direction from D/A.
Distinguish conversion direction from D/A.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q10.stem: Any product called grease may be thickly applied to electronic components.
reasons: This statement is false. Applications and performance requirements differ.
Applications and performance requirements differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q11.stem: Losses occur with an energized primary even when the secondary has no load.
reasons: Core losses and remaining hazards exist.
This statement is true. Core losses and remaining hazards exist.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q12.stem: A large outer box eliminates any need for internal restraint or cushioning.
reasons: This statement is false. Prevent internal movement and shock as well.
Prevent internal movement and shock as well.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q13.stem: Consider whether components fit only after all holes have been drilled.
reasons: This statement is false. Prevent positioning errors before machining.
Prevent positioning errors before machining.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q14.stem: Remove chips after stopping rotation, using the specified safe method.
reasons: Prevent entanglement and flying chips.
This statement is true. Prevent entanglement and flying chips.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q15.stem: Occupational safety and health covers only machine appearance, excluding illness and health.
reasons: This statement is false. Protect both safety and health.
Protect both safety and health.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q16.stem: Because a warning is not a prohibition, people may freely enter dangerous areas without checking other conditions.
reasons: This statement is false. Also verify the area and accompanying instructions.
Also verify the area and accompanying instructions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q17.stem: Material in 4 M includes materials and components.
reasons: Consider people, equipment, materials and methods.
This statement is true. Consider people, equipment, materials and methods.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q18.stem: ISO9001 certification permanently passes every product from that organization without inspection.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish certification scope from product evidence.
Distinguish certification scope from product evidence.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q19.stem: A circular economy only aims to make repairs difficult and discard materials after one use.
reasons: This statement is false. Keep resources circulating for longer.
Keep resources circulating for longer.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q20.stem: The basic third-angle arrangement places the plan view above the front view.
reasons: Match projection method to view direction.
This statement is true. Match projection method to view direction.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q21.stem: A cable sheath and individual conductor insulation cover different things.
reasons: Check construction and the layer being removed.
This statement is true. Check construction and the layer being removed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q22.stem: Automatic tool changing is unrelated to NC and removes any need to check the origin.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish control method from setup verification.
Distinguish control method from setup verification.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q23.stem: After calculating branch currents, check their sum against total current.
reasons: Branches share voltage, with current varying by resistance.
This statement is true. Branches share voltage, with current varying by resistance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q24.stem: Cleaning concerns appearance only and has no relation to foreign matter in products.
reasons: This statement is false. Maintain both safety and quality.
Maintain both safety and quality.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q25.stem: A thermal relay provides overload protection through contacts and other mechanisms linked to detection.
reasons: Check combinations with contactors and the protection scope.
This statement is true. Check combinations with contactors and the protection scope.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q26.stem: Keep prescribed conditions and assessment grounds for reliability tests such as accelerated-life tests.
reasons: Evaluation requires reproducible conditions and results.
This statement is true. Evaluation requires reproducible conditions and results.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q27.stem: Multilayer only means flexible and has no relation to conductor layers.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish layer structure from physical form.
Distinguish layer structure from physical form.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q28.stem: Delayed action and instantaneous return of an on-delay contact describe different transitions.
reasons: Trace timing for both operation and return.
This statement is true. Trace timing for both operation and return.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q29.stem: A mask for copper patterns eliminates every component part-number and polarity check during assembly.
reasons: This statement is false. Conductor formation and component mounting are separately controlled.
Conductor formation and component mounting are separately controlled.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-theory-q30.stem: Reading negative wording through the end of a question is important for true/false judgment.
reasons: Negation may reverse the meaning.
This statement is true. Negation may reverse the meaning.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q01.stem: Ideal100Ω and 300Ω resistors are in series. What is the equivalent resistance?
reasons: The product alone is not series resistance and has inconsistent units.
75Ω is the parallel value.
Series resistance is the sum, not the average.
100+300=400Ω; do not confuse this with the parallel formula.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q02.stem: The length of a wire halves while material, temperature and area remain unchanged. What is its resistance ratio?
reasons: R=ρℓ/S is proportional to length, so resistance halves. Retain the same-area and material conditions.
Resistance changes with length even when material and area match.
The relationship is not proportional to length squared.
Proportionality to length means half the length does not double resistance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q03.stem: Which improvement addresses falling hazards from an unstable temporary stand?
options: Push it into the passage just to clear the workbench.
Keep people clear, then adopt an approved stable location and transport method.
Shake it to test whether items fall.
reasons: The passage creates new obstruction and collision hazards.
Warnings alone do not remove the hazard. Specify placement and transport and check new hazards such as obstructed passages.
Shaking may cause the actual fall.
Calling out alone removes neither instability nor its cause.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q04.stem: For an ideal 3.0 kΩ resistor at 9 VDC, what current is calculated?
reasons: Convert0.003 A to mA by multiplying1000, yielding3 mA.
Multiplying9 and 3 does not apply Ohm’s-law division.
3.0 kΩ=3000Ω;I=9/3000=0.003 A=3 mA. Check ratings separately for actual use.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q05.stem: When replacing a rectifier diode, what must be checked besides matching shape?
reasons: Direction affects operation, and matching shape does not establish polarity or rating compatibility.
Shape alone does not guarantee polarity or rating compatibility.
Correct polarity still allows insufficient reverse-voltage or current ratings.
Current capacity alone does not prevent reversed fitting or terminal mismatch.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q06.stem: Wire insulation colors match when selecting a wire and terminal. What additional checks are needed?
options: No further checks because colors match.
Conductor area, voltage/temperature ratings and terminal/tool compatibility.
reasons: Box order cannot establish wire/terminal suitability.
Matching color does not guarantee matching conductor size or ratings.
Color is only one identification feature and does not guarantee electrical or mechanical compatibility.
Preferred color is not a criterion for ratings or crimp suitability.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q07.stem: Which injection-mold component pushes the product out?
reasons: The gate is the cavity inlet, not the component ejecting the solid product.
The ejector pin pushes the part out during release; distinguish it from gate and sprue flow paths.
The sprue carries molten material rather than ejecting the solid part.
The runner is a material channel, unlike an ejection pin.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q08.stem: A board marked inspected has a suspected solder bridge between adjacent terminals. What should be done?
options: Ignore the concern because it has a label.
Apply high voltage without responsibility or authorization.
Identify and hold the item; report the observed location and inspection history.
Rewrite records to pass the appearance inspection.
reasons: Suspected actual abnormalities require checking despite an inspected label.
High-voltage testing without authority and safe conditions is hazardous.
Prevent release when labeling and actual condition conflict. Use authorized inspection and rework procedures.
Changing records resolves neither the suspected bridge nor the actual condition.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q09.stem: Which IC primarily amplifies analog signals?
reasons: Basic gates perform binary logic rather than linear amplification of continuous signals.
An op amp is an amplifier for analog processing; its primary function differs from memory, logic and processing/control ICs.
Memory primarily stores information, rather than amplifying analog signals.
A microprocessor primarily executes computational/control instructions; it is not the name of an amplifier.

mfg1-electrical-mock-10-practical-q10.stem: A loop has an 18 V source and resistor drops of 7 V and an unknown value. What is the unknown drop?
reasons: The product18×7 does not satisfy the loop voltage-sum relationship.
The drops are not given as equal; the remainder is 11 V.
Subtract7 V from 18 V instead of adding.
With consistent rises and drops,18−7−V=0, soV=11 V.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-01.stem: The fish-and-tree pictogram on a chemical label indicates hazards to the aquatic environment. Also check the label and SDS for substance identification, hazards and handling conditions.
reasons: True. The picture provides a clue to harm to aquatic organisms or the environment. Check the label and SDS for the substance’s identity and detailed control measures.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Interpreting the fish picture as indicating drinking or washing use is wrong; treat it as notification of environmental hazards.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-02.stem: The harder you strike the head of a bolt that is difficult to insert, the more its thread compatibility is guaranteed.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Striking may crush the threads. Check the part number, alignment, foreign matter and damage as possible causes of difficult insertion; do not force the bolt tight.
False. Striking may crush the threads. Check the part number, alignment, foreign matter and damage as possible causes of difficult insertion; do not force the bolt tight.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-03.stem: High electrical conductivity alone does not establish suitability as a component; the required cross section, temperature, connections and specifications must also be checked.
reasons: True. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-04.stem: Preventive maintenance means checking conditions to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing equipment after it breaks down.
reasons: True. Preventive maintenance is an approach to checking equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing it after a breakdown. Daily checks cover specified items before work and at other designated times to detect small changes early. Periodic inspections follow a plan and examine details that daily checks alone may not reveal. Performing one does not permit omission of the other.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Preventive maintenance is an approach to checking equipment condition to prevent failures and accidents, rather than only repairing it after a breakdown. Daily checks cover specified items before work and at other designated times to detect small changes early. Periodic inspections follow a plan and examine details that daily checks alone may not reveal. Performing one does not permit omission of the other.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-05.stem: Passing a mock exam makes all required workplace training and work permits unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A mock exam checks learning and does not grant qualifications, training or work permits for actual equipment. Confirm the necessary requirements and assigned responsibilities at the workplace.
False. A mock exam checks learning and does not grant qualifications, training or work permits for actual equipment. Confirm the necessary requirements and assigned responsibilities at the workplace.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-06.stem: If visual inspection finds no cracks, it can also guarantee the absence of internal defects.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The surface visible in visual inspection differs from the interior. Internal defects require an inspection method appropriate to the material, location and requirements.
False. The surface visible in visual inspection differs from the interior. Internal defects require an inspection method appropriate to the material, location and requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-07.stem: Geometrical tolerances specify straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity, position and other characteristics.
reasons: True. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-08.stem: Calculating the thickness reduction percentage automatically determines the permissible amount of processing in one pass on the actual workpiece.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The reduction percentage is a geometric ratio relative to the original thickness. The permissible amount of processing in one pass depends on the material, equipment capability and approved process.

False. The reduction percentage is a geometric ratio relative to the original thickness. The permissible amount of processing in one pass depends on the material, equipment capability and approved process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-09.stem: If a marking is readable, checking whether its content matches the product is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even a readable marking may show a different part number or incorrect quantity. Separately check that the marking matches the actual product.
False. Even a readable marking may show a different part number or incorrect quantity. Separately check that the marking matches the actual product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-10.stem: Dimensions provide information needed for a component’s function and manufacture and generally indicate finished dimensions.
reasons: True. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-11.stem: Ra and Rz can be standardized to the largest value, disregarding which surface each requirement concerns.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Ra and Rz are roughness parameters with different definitions. Retain the parameter and value specified for each surface; do not standardize them to the maximum value.
False. Ra and Rz are roughness parameters with different definitions. Retain the parameter and value specified for each surface; do not standardize them to the maximum value.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-12.stem: Use the type of protective equipment specified for your work and check for damage, dirt and proper fit before use.
reasons:
True. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.

Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.

If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-13.stem: Before work, confirm the equipment assigned to you, work procedure, stopping method and contact person.
reasons:
True. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.
When reporting, state the equipment name, when you noticed the condition, the facts observed, and the action already taken. Saying only “I think it is broken” makes it difficult for the listener to assess the situation. Separate assumptions from facts if the cause is not yet confirmed. Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.

Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-14.stem: If a container is the same color as the adjacent liquid, its contents can be identified definitively even if its label is unknown.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Color does not establish a substance’s identity. Do not use a liquid whose identification is unclear; ask the responsible person to check the container and original records.
False. Color does not establish a substance’s identity. Do not use a liquid whose identification is unclear; ask the responsible person to check the container and original records.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-15.stem: First check the front view and projection-method instructions to avoid confusing left and right on the paper with the direction from which the actual object is viewed.
reasons: True. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-16.stem: The nonconforming-unit rate of an inspected sample guarantees conformity of every uninspected item.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The sample rate is a result for the inspected items, not a result from checking every uninspected item. Lot acceptance also requires the specified sampling criteria.
False. The sample rate is a result for the inspected items, not a result from checking every uninspected item. Lot acceptance also requires the specified sampling criteria.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-17.stem: A QC process chart organizes what is controlled at each process, by what method, at what frequency, and what action is taken when an abnormality occurs.
reasons: True. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A work standard specifies the work content, sequence, equipment, tools, and important conditions to maintain required quality despite changes in people or time. A QC process chart organizes what is controlled in each process, how often and by what method, and how abnormalities are handled. The working method and the control system play different roles even in the same process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-18.stem: If the items are the correct type, the three fixed principles are maintained even when the shelf’s quantity limit is exceeded.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The three fixed principles include quantity as well as location and item type. Exceeding the quantity limit violates the fixed-quantity principle even for the correct items.
False. The three fixed principles include quantity as well as location and item type. Exceeding the quantity limit violates the fixed-quantity principle even for the correct items.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-19.stem: A dial indicator comparison reading of 0.03 mm always indicates the workpiece’s full dimension.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A comparison reading is the difference from a reference. Obtain the full dimension by adding the signed difference to the reference dimension.
False. A comparison reading is the difference from a reference. Obtain the full dimension by adding the signed difference to the reference dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-20.stem: Use the workplace’s prescribed assessment method to prioritize risks; do not decide solely by personal impressions.
reasons:
True. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
First consider whether the hazard can be eliminated or reduced. If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When considering risk, look not only at whether a hazard exists but also at the severity of an accident, its likelihood, and opportunities for exposure. Use the workplace’s assessment method rather than deciding priorities solely by personal intuition.
