If equipment or process changes are needed, consult the responsible person or department instead of modifying equipment without authorization. After implementation, check whether the measure works and whether a new hazard has been created.
Maintaining safety requires repeating a cycle of planning, implementation, evaluation, and necessary improvement. Inspection records and near misses provide information for the next improvement.
Do not assume that countermeasures completely eliminate the possibility of an accident. Machines can fail, misunderstandings can occur, and surroundings can change. Share the remaining hazards and maintain the ability to stop when something abnormal occurs.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-21.stem: A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.
reasons: True. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-22.stem: If polishing makes a surface shiny, an out-of-specification outside diameter also becomes acceptable.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Gloss does not guarantee conformity of the outside diameter. Check dimensions and surface condition as separate requirements.
False. Gloss does not guarantee conformity of the outside diameter. Check dimensions and surface condition as separate requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-23.stem: If one person knows about the new revision, informing the next person in charge is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Unless the next person in charge is also informed of when the new revision takes effect, its scope and how it is distinguished from the old revision, work may be performed under different conditions.

False. Unless the next person in charge is also informed of when the new revision takes effect, its scope and how it is distinguished from the old revision, work may be performed under different conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-24.stem: Safety signs include those prohibiting actions, warning of hazards, and identifying places or equipment needed in an emergency.
reasons:
True. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Safety signs include those that prohibit actions, warn of a hazard, and indicate locations or equipment needed in an emergency. Do not only memorize the picture; consider what action is required at that location.
“No entry” does not mean you may enter if you are careful. An electric-shock warning indicates the presence of an electrical hazard. Follow the sign and confirm the equipment procedure and your authorization to enter the area.
For chemicals, check the container label and safety data sheet. Hazards such as ignition, corrosion, and health effects differ by substance. Do not identify contents solely by color or smell, or use liquid from an unlabeled container.
Check the locations and routes to fire extinguishers, AEDs, and evacuation areas during normal conditions instead of starting to search in an emergency. If an escape route is obstructed, request improvement according to workplace rules.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-25.stem: After periodic inspection is completed, the next day’s daily inspection is unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Daily and periodic inspections differ in scope and purpose. Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not replace this morning’s check for leaks and other conditions.
False. Daily and periodic inspections differ in scope and purpose. Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not replace this morning’s check for leaks and other conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-26.stem: If a hole diameter becomes out of specification after the tool and operator are changed simultaneously, investigate both changes and other 4M conditions rather than declaring only one the cause.
reasons: True. When the operator and tool change simultaneously, the sequence of events alone cannot identify one as the cause. Check the facts for the 4Ms, including mounting, materials, settings and methods.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When the operator and tool change simultaneously, the sequence of events alone cannot identify one as the cause. Check the facts for the 4Ms, including mounting, materials, settings and methods.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-27.stem: Knowing the numerical setting makes checking its unit unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The same numerical value represents a different quantity when the unit differs. Check a setting’s number together with its displayed unit.
False. The same numerical value represents a different quantity when the unit differs. Check a setting’s number together with its displayed unit.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-28.stem: For slinging and operation, verify required qualifications, training and assigned responsibilities; someone merely nearby must not start assisting on their own initiative.
reasons: True. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-29.stem: Read prohibition and warning signs separately: prohibition signs identify actions that must not be performed, while warning signs identify existing hazards.
reasons: True. Prohibition communicates a restriction on behavior, while a warning communicates the presence of a hazard. It does not mean that acting carefully removes a prohibition.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Treating a warning sign as permission to act confuses the roles of prohibitions and hazard notifications.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-theory-30.stem: For every threaded NO-GO gauge, judgment is based solely on the same insertion behavior as a plain hole.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Threaded NO-GO gauges are judged under specified conditions such as insertion behavior and number of turns. Do not unconditionally apply the passage criteria for a plain hole.
False. Threaded NO-GO gauges are judged under specified conditions such as insertion behavior and number of turns. Do not unconditionally apply the passage criteria for a plain hole.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-01.stem: The cutting sound changes suddenly, but no scratches are yet visible on the product. Which action is appropriate, including the decision to restart?
options: Stop safely and report; obtain separate instructions for checking the product and restarting the equipment.
Restart immediately on your own judgment after stopping.
Record the cause definitively as a breakdown.
reasons: Continuing until scratches appear can allow an equipment abnormality to increase hazards and defects.
Stop safely, report the facts, and separately check the product impact and whether equipment restart is permitted.
Do not restart without authorization until the cause and safety have been checked, even after stopping.
A breakdown is a suspected cause; record it separately from the observed fact of an abnormal sound.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-02.stem: The new work standard is available, but it is unclear whether the QC process chart is an old revision. How should you proceed?
options: Follow only the work standard and omit measurement.
Set control values from old memories.
Check the scope and revision of both documents and the applicability of their control conditions.
Treat the fixing method as unnecessary because measurement was performed.
reasons: Following the work method does not allow omission of measurements specified in the QC process chart.
Old memories do not verify the control conditions for the current product and revision.
The work standard and QC process chart have different roles; cross-check the scope, revision and applicable conditions of both.
A measurement result does not eliminate the work-method requirement to secure the material.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-03.stem: The basic size is 12 mm, the upper deviation is +0.03 mm, and the lower deviation is −0.01 mm. What is the tolerance?
reasons: Subtracting the lower limit, 11.99 mm, from the upper limit, 12.03 mm, gives 0.04 mm.
This treats the positive and negative deviations like a sum rather than a difference and differs from the tolerance of 0.04 mm.
Tolerance is the difference between the limit sizes, not a value obtained by adding the basic size of 12 mm.
Adding the upper and lower limits gives 24.02 mm, which is not the tolerance.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-04.stem: There is an uncoated area on the back of an outdoor component. Its front is uniform. How should you judge it?
options: If only the front looks clean, all requirements pass.
Check the surfaces requiring corrosion protection, coating condition and required inspections against the requirements.
Use any paint if its color is the same.
reasons: The attractive front cannot compensate for missing coating on a back surface that requires corrosion protection.
Compare the target surfaces, coating condition, thickness and other items with requirements; confirm required inspections and approved disposition.
Unapproved recoating may violate specified film thickness or curing conditions.
Paints of the same color may differ in composition and performance, so compatibility with the specified paint must be checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-05.stem: The inside diameter at the entrance was measured, but the contact tip cannot reach a groove farther inside. How should this be recorded?
options: Copy the entrance diameter as the groove diameter.
Record measurement as complete because the pointer moved.
Force the contact tip to bend.
Record the groove as unverified and consult about a suitable contact shape and reference.
reasons: The entrance and groove are different locations; do not copy the entrance diameter as the groove diameter.
Pointer movement alone does not establish contact with the groove’s measuring surface.
Bending the contact tip damages its geometry, function or measurement conditions; do not modify it without authorization.
Record the unreachable groove as unverified and consult about a tip shape that can make contact, its range and the reference.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-06.stem: The angle of an inclined surface was readable, but the protractor’s base was not contacting the intended surface. What should you do?
options: Use only the number that was readable.
Correct contact with both surfaces and verify using the specified method.
Convert it to a length as a substitute.
Replace it with the angle of an easier-to-view surface.
reasons: A reading taken without base contact does not guarantee the angle between the two specified surfaces.
Place the base and blade correctly against the two intended surfaces and verify the angle using the specified method.
Angle and length are different quantities; conversion does not correct poor contact.
The angle of another surface does not replace the requested target angle.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-07.stem: Incorrect labels on purchased items are repeatedly found during inspection. Which approach should a small group use?
options: Declare inspection alone to be the cause.
Determine the cause by majority vote alone.
Collect facts from procurement through shipment and check the effectiveness of countermeasures.
reasons: Even when inspection discovers the issue, investigate possible causes in procurement, labeling, handover and other stages.
A majority vote selects an opinion; it does not prove a cause as fact.
Investigate facts and handovers from procurement through shipment, and check whether identification is maintained after countermeasures.
Changing labeling conditions also requires formal checking and approval.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-08.stem: Defects are classified as A: 8 cases, B: 7 cases, and C: 5 cases. What percentage is A alone?
reasons: 8 is a count; obtain its percentage of all 20 cases using 8 ÷ 20 × 100.
75% represents the combined 15 cases of A and B, not A alone.
The 8 cases of A represent 40%; 60% represents the remaining 12 cases.
A accounts for 8 of the total 20 cases, so 8 ÷ 20 × 100 = 40%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-09.stem: Thickness decreases from 4.0 mm to 3.0 mm. What is the reduction percentage relative to the original thickness?
reasons: Dividing the reduction of 1.0 mm by the original thickness of 4.0 mm gives 25%.
33.3% uses the final thickness of 3.0 mm as the denominator, rather than the original thickness.
75% represents the remaining 3.0 mm, not the reduction percentage.
A reduction of 1 mm cannot simply be treated as 1%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-01-practical-10.stem: You are selecting a fiber-reinforced resin component. How should you assess the material?
options: Check the combination of resin and reinforcement and the specified conditions.
Remove all fibers as foreign matter.
The resin name alone guarantees all performance.
reasons: Properties are obtained through the combination of resin and reinforcement such as fibers; check the composition and specified conditions.
Fibers added for reinforcement are not foreign matter; removing them without authorization changes the material’s composition.
Reinforcements also include glass fibers and other materials; they are not limited to metals.
Even with the same resin name, performance differs with reinforcement, molding conditions and other factors, so the name does not guarantee all requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-01.stem: Distinguish shaft-diameter measurements as continuous variable data from counts of out-of-specification products as attribute data.
reasons: True. Measurements such as length and count data such as case numbers have different meanings and recording fields.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. This distinction is necessary because copying a hole-diameter value directly into a count field confuses quantities and counts.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-02.stem: When document revisions differ, freely adopt whichever has a newer-looking cover.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A cover’s appearance cannot determine the applicable revision. Cross-check the document number, revision and target product, and ask the responsible person which specified revision applies.
False. A cover’s appearance cannot determine the applicable revision. Cross-check the document number, revision and target product, and ask the responsible person which specified revision applies.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-03.stem: A length of 24 and an angle of 24° are the same quantity because their numerical values are the same.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. 24 mm is a length and 24° is an angle; they are different quantities. Do not treat them as identical from the numbers alone.
False. 24 mm is a length and 24° is an angle; they are different quantities. Do not treat them as identical from the numbers alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-04.stem: Dimension values entered on a drawing indicate the object’s actual dimensions regardless of scale.
reasons: True. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-05.stem: Grinding removes material gradually with abrasive grains in a grinding wheel and is used to finish hard materials and surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy.
reasons: True. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Grinding removes small amounts of material using abrasive grains in a wheel and is used for hard materials or surfaces requiring high dimensional accuracy. Polishing conditions a surface with abrasives and similar media. Its purposes include appearance, roughness, and friction, but a shinier surface is not necessarily better for every application. Check drawing requirements for size and surface condition separately.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-06.stem: A straight ruler is always suitable for inspecting any precision tolerance.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Instruments have limits to their reading capability and application range. A straight ruler may provide a reading without being capable of judging the specified precision tolerance.
False. Instruments have limits to their reading capability and application range. A straight ruler may provide a reading without being capable of judging the specified precision tolerance.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-07.stem: In OSHMS, conditions and results are evaluated after implementing measures and the review is reflected in the next plan; merely entering a measure once does not complete management.
reasons: True. Manage occupational safety and health by repeating planning, implementation, evaluation and improvement, checking effectiveness and remaining hazards after implementation.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Implementation does not remove the need for evaluation or improvement; ongoing management leads to the next check.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-08.stem: If the power-supply marking on relocated equipment is unreadable and only an old note is available, hold off on connecting it.
reasons: True. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-09.stem: If the zero point is correct, correctness across the measuring instrument’s full range is guaranteed.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The zero point checks one position. Also check calibration and inspection records for the condition across the full range.
False. The zero point checks one position. Also check calibration and inspection records for the condition across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-10.stem: If a decimal point or part of a numeral on paper is obscured, do not guess and proceed; request a readable approved drawing.
reasons: True. The size of lettering on a drawing is specified by its character height. The textbook lists 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kanji, and 2.5, 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kana, letters and numbers. If a decimal point or part of a digit is illegible, do not guess and start work; request a legible approved drawing. Do not confuse enlargement or reduction during printing with a change to the stated dimension values.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The size of lettering on a drawing is specified by its character height. The textbook lists 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kanji, and 2.5, 3.5, 5, 7 and 10 mm for kana, letters and numbers. If a decimal point or part of a digit is illegible, do not guess and start work; request a legible approved drawing. Do not confuse enlargement or reduction during printing with a change to the stated dimension values.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-11.stem: If no depth indication can be found for a hole, it is invariably a through hole.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Some through-hole indications omit depth, but failing to find a depth indication alone does not establish that a hole is through. Cross-check other views and instructions.
False. Some through-hole indications omit depth, but failing to find a depth indication alone does not establish that a hole is through. Cross-check other views and instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-12.stem: If adding cutting fluid changes the appearance, investigating the cause of an abnormal sound becomes unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even if adding fluid changes the appearance, abnormalities in the tool, mounting, conditions or other factors may remain. Check records and equipment condition.
False. Even if adding fluid changes the appearance, abnormalities in the tool, mounting, conditions or other factors may remain. Check records and equipment condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-13.stem: A sectional view shows the interior by imagining the object cut and the nearer portion removed.
reasons: True. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A sectional view represents the inside of an object by imagining a cut and removing the portion in front. It can make internal holes and steps easier to understand than using many hidden lines. It is a way of communicating shape, not a machining instruction to cut the actual product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-14.stem: Applying water to a fire where live electrical parts may be present extinguishes it safely without electric-shock risk.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Water may cause electric shock at live parts. Report and evacuate from a safe position, and check extinguisher suitability and safety conditions.
False. Water may cause electric shock at live parts. Report and evacuate from a safe position, and check extinguisher suitability and safety conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-15.stem: The material’s mechanical and metal processing category lists many examples of work, including casting, forging, cutting, sheet-metal work, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion.
reasons: True. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The source lists many examples in the machining and metalworking category: casting, forging, cutting, sheet metal, maintenance, inspection, assembly, molding, painting, packaging, heat treatment, rolling and extrusion. Experience in one process does not authorize every type of work. Check the assigned job and required training.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-16.stem: Control conditions for another product can be applied unconditionally if the process names are similar.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with the same process name, specifications and control conditions may differ by product. Check applicability to the product, process and document revision.
False. Even with the same process name, specifications and control conditions may differ by product. Check applicability to the product, process and document revision.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-17.stem: In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner performs within the prescribed scope, and the instructor checks.
reasons:
True. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.
In OJT, the instructor explains and demonstrates, the learner practices within the specified scope, and the instructor checks the result. Having seen a task is not the same as being able to perform it safely alone. If an operation is unclear, stop and ask before attempting it.
After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When learning new work, understand why the steps follow that order rather than only memorizing the sequence. Before practice, confirm the pre-work inspection, prohibited actions, and response to abnormalities.

After listening, explaining the procedure back in your own words helps reveal misunderstandings. In particular, do not rely on a vague acknowledgment when confirming values, units, part orientation, and stopping conditions.
Reading this material does not replace the training or qualifications required at the workplace. Confirm the work you may perform and the required training with the responsible person according to the equipment and working conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-18.stem: Even when diameter and length are within specified ranges, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation, position and other characteristics are not necessarily met.
reasons: True. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Even if a diameter or length is within its specified range, requirements for surface flatness, axis orientation or position may not be met. Geometrical tolerances indicate characteristics such as straightness, flatness, roundness, parallelism, perpendicularity and position. Different types evaluate different properties, so one dimensional measurement does not mean everything has been checked.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-19.stem: Direct current flows in a constant direction, so it presents no hazard to the human body.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Direct current also presents electric-shock and other hazards. Constant flow direction does not guarantee safety for the human body.
False. Direct current also presents electric-shock and other hazards. Constant flow direction does not guarantee safety for the human body.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-20.stem: Aqueous solutions invariably have a pH between 0 and 14 regardless of conditions.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The introductory example’s conditions of room temperature and dilute aqueous solutions cannot be generalized to every liquid. Retain the temperature, solution conditions and measurement method.

False. The introductory example’s conditions of room temperature and dilute aqueous solutions cannot be generalized to every liquid. Retain the temperature, solution conditions and measurement method.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-21.stem: Design quality concerns intended performance and specifications; manufacturing quality concerns their realization in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivery of the correct items in the correct quantity, on time and in the correct condition.
reasons: True. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-22.stem: For copied or reduced-size drawings, check that lines and lettering remain sufficiently readable.
reasons: True. For the mechanical drawings covered in this textbook, A-series paper is preferred, in a size that clearly shows the object. Normally the long edge is horizontal; A4 may also be used in portrait orientation. A larger sheet does not make the information more accurate. On copied or reduced drawings, check that the lines and lettering remain clearly readable.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. For the mechanical drawings covered in this textbook, A-series paper is preferred, in a size that clearly shows the object. Normally the long edge is horizontal; A4 may also be used in portrait orientation. A larger sheet does not make the information more accurate. On copied or reduced drawings, check that the lines and lettering remain clearly readable.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-23.stem: A resistor can be replaced without checking required ratings if its resistance value is the same.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with the same resistance, required ratings such as power and operating conditions may differ. Do not replace a resistor without checking the specified requirements.
False. Even with the same resistance, required ratings such as power and operating conditions may differ. Do not replace a resistor without checking the specified requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-24.stem: A single description such as “light” or “hard” is insufficient to judge suitability for an application.
reasons: True. Density is mass per unit volume. Objects of the same volume can have different masses when their materials differ. Elasticity means deformation recovers after force is removed; plasticity means deformation remains. Hardness and toughness—the ability to resist fracture under impact and similar loading—are also different properties. “Light” or “hard” alone does not establish suitability for an application.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Density is mass per unit volume. Objects of the same volume can have different masses when their materials differ. Elasticity means deformation recovers after force is removed; plasticity means deformation remains. Hardness and toughness—the ability to resist fracture under impact and similar loading—are also different properties. “Light” or “hard” alone does not establish suitability for an application.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-25.stem: All extinguishers can be used in the same way regardless of the type of fire.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Extinguishers have suitability requirements for different fires. Inappropriate methods, such as water on oil or live electrical parts, are dangerous.
False. Extinguishers have suitability requirements for different fires. Inappropriate methods, such as water on oil or live electrical parts, are dangerous.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-26.stem: Surface roughness describes fine surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, appearance and other characteristics.
reasons: True. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Surface roughness describes small surface irregularities and relates to friction, wear, lubrication, and appearance. Ra is arithmetic mean roughness and Rz is maximum-height roughness. Check the parameter, unit, and measurement conditions against the drawing requirement. A smaller roughness value is not unconditionally better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-27.stem: If a scatter diagram shows a relationship, causation between the two quantities has been proven.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A scatter diagram gives a clue to a relationship between two quantities. A cause cannot be established without investigating other conditions and facts.
False. A scatter diagram gives a clue to a relationship between two quantities. A cause cannot be established without investigating other conditions and facts.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-28.stem: Having ISO 9001 information allows dimensional inspection of individual components to be omitted.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. ISO 9001 concerns quality management systems. Whether the actual product meets specified dimensions must be checked through the necessary inspection.
False. ISO 9001 concerns quality management systems. Whether the actual product meets specified dimensions must be checked through the necessary inspection.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-29.stem: Merely having a work procedure document is insufficient unless it can be read at the workplace when needed.
reasons: True. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-theory-30.stem: For a flatness specification, the operator must always add an independently chosen datum.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Flatness concerns a feature’s own form and does not call for an operator to add an unnecessary datum. Follow the drawing’s formal instructions.
False. Flatness concerns a feature’s own form and does not call for an operator to add an unnecessary datum. Follow the drawing’s formal instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-01.stem: Usable and chipped tools are mixed together in a toolbox. Which improvement also prevents reuse of damaged tools?
options: Put everything together in one box.
Return damaged tools if they look similar.
Identify and segregate damaged tools, and define fixed locations and checking methods for needed tools.
Discard even needed tools without authorization.
reasons: Simply putting them together does not remove the situation in which a damaged tool can be selected again.
Do not return a chipped tool as usable even if it looks similar.
Combining identification and segregation of damaged tools with storage locations and condition checks for needed tools helps prevent reuse.
Sorting means distinguishing needed from unneeded items, not discarding needed tools without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-02.stem: Defects were recorded as 12 faint-print cases, 6 dirt cases and 2 irregular-shape cases. What is the cumulative percentage through dirt?
reasons: Of all 20 cases, faint print 12 + dirt 6 = 18 cases, giving a cumulative percentage of 90%.
60% represents only the 12 faint-print cases, not the cumulative total through dirt.
30% represents only the 6 dirt cases and does not include faint print.
20% is not the result of dividing the cumulative 18 cases by all 20 cases.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-03.stem: A failed light prevents viewing one item on an inspection checklist. Which recording and start decision is appropriate?
options: Mark it normal because it was normal yesterday.
Record why it is unverified and consult about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.
Record it as seen and view it later.
reasons: Yesterday’s normal condition does not prove today’s condition at the location that could not be checked.
Deleting a specified item does not resolve the unverified condition; an operating decision is also needed.
Retain the reason it is unverified and consult the responsible person about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.
Recording something as checked when it was not viewed does not match what was actually done.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-04.stem: Finished components touch and become scratched when placed together in a box. Which packaging consideration is appropriate?
options: Improve only the appearance of the outer box.
Check individual protection such as dividers, movement, identification and quantity.
reasons: Improving only the outer box’s appearance does not prevent components touching inside.
Do not combine counts for similar part numbers with different specifications; maintain identification and quantities.
Removing labels loses identification information and increases mix-up risk.
Consider individual protection and methods to restrain movement inside the box, and also check identification and quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-05.stem: What information should be checked when judging a threaded NO-GO gauge?
options: Only the explanation for plain holes.
Only the final position after forceful tightening.
The specified insertion behavior, number of turns and other conditions for that gauge.
Only whether the GO gauge entered.
reasons: Threads have their own insertion, turn-count and other conditions; a plain-hole explanation alone is insufficient.
Forceful tightening risks damage and misjudgment; do not change acceptance conditions by force.
Check the GO and NO-GO sides under the conditions specified for that thread and gauge.
The GO-side result alone does not replace the required NO-GO-side check.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-06.stem: There is foreign matter on a depth gauge’s reference surface. Which measurement plan is appropriate?
options: Subtract a convenient number from the reading.
Guarantee the depth with the foreign matter still present.
Prepare the reference surface and instrument by the specified method and check contact and the starting reference.
reasons: Subtracting an unsupported allowance for foreign matter does not constitute correct measurement.
Foreign matter changes contact with the reference surface and causes an erroneous depth reading.
Height and depth have different references and targets; do not copy one to the other.
Prepare the reference surface and instrument condition, then measure depth with correct contact and reference.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-07.stem: Someone is about to enter the previous reading even though inspection was not performed. What should be done?
options: Enter it if the trend is similar.
Change the criteria to meet the target.
Erase the unverified field and ship.
Match records to actual work, retain the unverified status and report.
reasons: Expecting the same trend as before is not an actual measurement result for this inspection.
A target does not justify changing approved criteria.
Erasing an unverified field does not complete inspection and can release unjudged items.
Retain and report the fact that inspection was not performed, and record only results actually obtained.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-08.stem: Which record correctly converts a measurement time of 1250 ms to seconds?
reasons: Changing only the unit to seconds without changing the number makes it 1000 times larger.
0.125 s is one tenth of the correct 1.25 s.
12.5 s is ten times the correct 1.25 s.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-09.stem: The reference is 32.00 mm and the difference is −0.03 mm. Which calculation and record are appropriate?
options: 32.03 mm, recorded as a positive difference.
31.97 mm, with the negative difference recorded.
Record 0.03 mm as the full dimension.
reasons: This adds a negative difference as positive, reversing the specified sign.
32.00 + (−0.03) = 31.97 mm. Record the corresponding reference and negative difference as well.
0.03 mm is the magnitude of the difference, not the full dimension.
Since the difference is not zero, the dimension cannot remain at the reference value of 32.00 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-02-practical-10.stem: You want to apply a new functional coating at a thickness different from its specified conditions. Which check is appropriate?
options: If it is named functional, it performs under all conditions.
Cross-check the coating, substrate, film thickness, drying and curing against requirements.
Mix freely if the color is the same.
Omit grounding or ventilation without authorization.
reasons: The name functional alone does not establish performance at unspecified film thicknesses or conditions.
Check how the coating, substrate, film thickness, drying and curing conditions correspond to requirements.
The same color does not mean the same composition; unauthorized mixing compromises conformity and safety.
Grounding and ventilation are safety conditions for the painting method; do not omit them without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-01.stem: Even when dimensions conform, the overall requirements are not met if the required quantity is not delivered.
reasons: True. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is not determined solely by the convenience of the manufacturer. The starting point is meeting users’ requirements. Design quality concerns the intended performance and specification; manufacturing quality concerns how these are achieved in actual products; logistics quality concerns delivering the correct items in the correct quantity, on time, and in the required condition. Meeting dimensional requirements alone does not meet the entire requirement if the necessary quantity is not delivered.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-02.stem: Eddy-current testing uses electrical changes involving a coil and the object; applying it requires checking the object’s conductivity, shape and other conditions.
reasons: True. The method uses electrical changes related to eddy currents induced in a conductor by an AC coil; material and shape affect applicability.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The method cannot be used on every material under identical conditions, so the statement that applicability conditions must be checked is not false.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-03.stem: If a pressed product appears to have the specified shape, inspection of all other requirements becomes unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Visible shape alone does not verify all internal, dimensional, functional and other requirements. Perform the inspections appropriate to the pressing process.
False. Visible shape alone does not verify all internal, dimensional, functional and other requirements. Perform the inspections appropriate to the pressing process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-04.stem: If you can read the position of a welding symbol, work qualifications and safety procedures become unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Reading a symbol does not waive work qualifications, training or safety conditions. Meet the actual work requirements separately.
False. Reading a symbol does not waive work qualifications, training or safety conditions. Meet the actual work requirements separately.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-05.stem: If an equipment power-supply marking is unreadable, tell the responsible person its equipment number and the marking’s condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection method.
reasons: True. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. If a relocated machine’s supply marking is unreadable and only an old note remains, withhold connection. Report the machine number and marking condition, and confirm the appropriate ratings and connection. Keep actual energizing and wiring within the authorized work scope.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-06.stem: If only the GO side enters a plain hole, every NO-GO-side check becomes unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Limit acceptance for a plain hole requires checking both that the GO side passes and that the NO-GO side does not pass. One side alone is insufficient.
False. Limit acceptance for a plain hole requires checking both that the GO side passes and that the NO-GO side does not pass. One side alone is insufficient.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-07.stem: Foreign matter underneath a height gauge has absolutely no effect on readings.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Foreign matter underneath changes contact and orientation against the surface plate, affecting height readings. Check the base and plate using the specified procedure.
False. Foreign matter underneath changes contact and orientation against the surface plate, affecting height readings. Check the base and plate using the specified procedure.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-08.stem: Packaging protects products from scratches, dirt, moisture and other damage, communicates identification information, and facilitates transport and storage.
reasons: True. Packaging protects products from scratches, dirt, moisture, and other hazards, communicates identification, and facilitates transport and storage. Individual wrapping supports separate protection and control; corrugated boxes group items together. Shrink film contracts under heat, but wrapping alone does not guarantee complete impact or moisture protection.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Packaging protects products from scratches, dirt, moisture, and other hazards, communicates identification, and facilitates transport and storage. Individual wrapping supports separate protection and control; corrugated boxes group items together. Shrink film contracts under heat, but wrapping alone does not guarantee complete impact or moisture protection.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-09.stem: Dividing the masses of two objects of different volumes directly always gives specific gravity.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Specific gravity is a density ratio relative to a reference substance. It corresponds to a mass ratio for equal volumes, but cannot be found by directly dividing masses of different volumes.
False. Specific gravity is a density ratio relative to a reference substance. It corresponds to a mass ratio for equal volumes, but cannot be found by directly dividing masses of different volumes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-10.stem: Not every metal hardens in the same way under the same heating and cooling.
reasons: True. Heat treatment changes metal structure and properties through heating and cooling conditions. In typical steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness, and other properties after quenching. Annealing may soften the material to improve machinability. Not every metal hardens in the same way under identical heating and cooling.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Heat treatment changes metal structure and properties through heating and cooling conditions. In typical steel treatments, quenching is used to increase hardness, while tempering adjusts hardness, toughness, and other properties after quenching. Annealing may soften the material to improve machinability. Not every metal hardens in the same way under identical heating and cooling.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-11.stem: When connecting a motor or transformer, do not regard wiring connections alone as establishing conformity; check the equipment ratings and facility specifications.
reasons: True. Motors convert motive power and transformers change voltage in applicable circuits, but use also requires compatibility with the power supply, equipment ratings and facility conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Motors convert motive power and transformers change voltage in applicable circuits, but use also requires compatibility with the power supply, equipment ratings and facility conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-12.stem: Reading only part of “must not do” makes it mean the same as “may do”.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. “Must not do” expresses prohibition, while “may do” expresses permission; their meanings are opposite. Read the negation and the sentence ending.
False. “Must not do” expresses prohibition, while “may do” expresses permission; their meanings are opposite. Read the negation and the sentence ending.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-13.stem: Welding is a candidate for joining two thin sheets; casting for making a body with complex internal spaces in a mold; and pressing for pushing and bending a sheet.
reasons: True. Compare three objectives: joining two sheets, making a body with complex spaces in a mold, and pressing a sheet into a bend. Welding, casting, and press work are possible choices respectively. However, do not select a method from shape alone; check material, required strength, production quantity, and later processes. Several methods can be combined, such as machining after casting.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Compare three objectives: joining two sheets, making a body with complex spaces in a mold, and pressing a sheet into a bend. Welding, casting, and press work are possible choices respectively. However, do not select a method from shape alone; check material, required strength, production quantity, and later processes. Several methods can be combined, such as machining after casting.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-14.stem: When reporting an abnormality, there is no need to distinguish verified facts from speculation about the cause.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Reporting an unverified suspected cause as fact can mislead decisions. Separately report observations, responses and unverified matters.
False. Reporting an unverified suspected cause as fact can mislead decisions. Separately report observations, responses and unverified matters.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-15.stem: Screen magnification or print size can change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely from lengths measured on a screen or paper with a ruler.
reasons: True. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A 1:1 scale is full size, 2:1 is an enlargement to twice the actual size, and 1:2 is a reduction to half size. Written dimensions indicate the object’s actual size regardless of scale. Screen magnification or print size may also change, so do not determine machining dimensions solely by measuring the screen or paper with a ruler.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-16.stem: Control-chart limits and product specification limits always describe the same boundary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Control limits monitor process changes, while specification limits define product requirements; they have different purposes.
False. Control limits monitor process changes, while specification limits define product requirements; they have different purposes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-17.stem: As the number of displayed digits on a caliper increases, errors caused by foreign matter automatically disappear.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Display digits do not remove foreign matter or poor contact. Check measuring-face and workpiece cleanliness, contact, and suitability of the specified instrument.
False. Display digits do not remove foreign matter or poor contact. Check measuring-face and workpiece cleanliness, contact, and suitability of the specified instrument.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-18.stem: A dial caliper gauge uses contact tips resembling inside or outside calipers to reach difficult-to-measure locations such as grooves.
reasons: True. A lever-type indicator has a contact point that pivots like a lever. A cylinder gauge has a shape for comparative bore measurement. A dial caliper gauge has inside/outside-caliper-like contacts for hard-to-reach locations such as grooves. Check correct contact with the target surface as well as suitable range and resolution.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A lever-type indicator has a contact point that pivots like a lever. A cylinder gauge has a shape for comparative bore measurement. A dial caliper gauge has inside/outside-caliper-like contacts for hard-to-reach locations such as grooves. Check correct contact with the target surface as well as suitable range and resolution.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-19.stem: When recording specific gravity, also check the reference substance and temperature; do not treat different conditions as identical merely because numbers are similar.
reasons: True. Specific gravity is treated as the ratio to the density of a reference substance. This source uses water at 4°C, with specific gravity 1, as the reference for solids and liquids. Distinguish this ratio from density values carrying units such as g/cm³. Records with different references or temperatures are not identical merely because their numbers look alike.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Specific gravity is treated as the ratio to the density of a reference substance. This source uses water at 4°C, with specific gravity 1, as the reference for solids and liquids. Distinguish this ratio from density values carrying units such as g/cm³. Records with different references or temperatures are not identical merely because their numbers look alike.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-20.stem: If an improvement proposal seems good, you may change only your own procedure document and implement it before approval.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Improvement proposals can also affect quality and safety. Obtain formal checking and approval before implementation, and coordinate applicability and communication.
False. Improvement proposals can also affect quality and safety. Obtain formal checking and approval before implementation, and coordinate applicability and communication.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-21.stem: A location that could not be viewed because of insufficient lighting may be recorded as normal.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An item that could not be seen is unverified. Record the reason and consult the responsible person about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.
False. An item that could not be seen is unverified. Record the reason and consult the responsible person about the checking method and whether operation is permitted.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-22.stem: Measurement results include the effects of the instrument, person measuring, temperature, mounting condition and other factors.
reasons: True. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-23.stem: A histogram directly shows the original measurement data’s chronological order.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A histogram is a frequency distribution grouped into intervals. Aggregating the data means it does not directly show the original chronological order.
False. A histogram is a frequency distribution grouped into intervals. Aggregating the data means it does not directly show the original chronological order.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-24.stem: Knoop hardness HK uses the long diagonal of an elongated diamond-shaped indentation, unlike the rebound height read for Shore hardness.
reasons: True. Knoop uses the indentation diagonal, whereas Shore as described in the material uses the hammer’s rebound height.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The two cannot be treated as having the same readout target; distinguish the hardness methods and scales.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-25.stem: One conforming item after improvement proves stability of the entire process.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. One conforming item is a result at one point in time and does not prove variation or continued stability across the entire process.
False. One conforming item is a result at one point in time and does not prove variation or continued stability across the entire process.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-26.stem: A limit gauge checks whether a hole or shaft lies within the specified permissible range, generally using a GO and NO-GO pair.
reasons: True. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-27.stem: Blow molding uses air to form hollow shapes; extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products with a constant cross section.
reasons: True. Injection molding shapes flowing resin in a mold. Blow molding uses air to produce hollow forms, while extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products of constant cross-section. Compression molding shapes material by pressure within a mold. Reinforced plastic combines resin with reinforcement such as fibers. Materials and solidification mechanisms differ between methods.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Injection molding shapes flowing resin in a mold. Blow molding uses air to produce hollow forms, while extrusion continuously pushes material through a die to make long products of constant cross-section. Compression molding shapes material by pressure within a mold. Reinforced plastic combines resin with reinforcement such as fibers. Materials and solidification mechanisms differ between methods.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-28.stem: Components of another specification may be added to the needed-item stock count if they are on the same shelf.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Only needed items of the specified specification count as stock. Identify and segregate other-specification items as mixed-in items; do not add them to the needed-item count.
False. Only needed items of the specified specification count as stock. Identify and segregate other-specification items as mixed-in items; do not add them to the needed-item count.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-29.stem: 5S activities maintain a workplace where needed items can be found, items are not confused, and hazards or abnormalities can be noticed.
reasons:
True. 5S is not merely about making a workplace look tidy. It is a way to maintain a workplace where necessary items are easy to find, incorrect items are not used, and hazards and abnormalities are easier to notice.
Sorting means separating necessary and unnecessary items. However, do not discard drawings, inspection records, or entrusted items at your own discretion. Confirm the disposal criteria and who has authority. Setting in order means deciding where necessary items belong and how to return them so they can be retrieved without searching.
When cleaning, remove dirt while also looking for abnormalities such as leaks or damage. Cleaning inside machinery must follow the specified stopping and safety confirmation procedure. Maintaining cleanliness means sustaining the results of sorting, organizing, and cleaning. Discipline means understanding the agreed methods and following them as a habit.
An improvement will not last if a one-time cleanup cannot be maintained by the next person. Defining responsibility, when checks are performed, and whom to notify of abnormalities creates an activity that does not rely solely on individual effort.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. 5S is not merely about making a workplace look tidy. It is a way to maintain a workplace where necessary items are easy to find, incorrect items are not used, and hazards and abnormalities are easier to notice.
Sorting means separating necessary and unnecessary items. However, do not discard drawings, inspection records, or entrusted items at your own discretion. Confirm the disposal criteria and who has authority. Setting in order means deciding where necessary items belong and how to return them so they can be retrieved without searching.
When cleaning, remove dirt while also looking for abnormalities such as leaks or damage. Cleaning inside machinery must follow the specified stopping and safety confirmation procedure. Maintaining cleanliness means sustaining the results of sorting, organizing, and cleaning. Discipline means understanding the agreed methods and following them as a habit.
An improvement will not last if a one-time cleanup cannot be maintained by the next person. Defining responsibility, when checks are performed, and whom to notify of abnormalities creates an activity that does not rely solely on individual effort.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-theory-30.stem: If its pH is near neutral, a liquid is harmless water even if its composition is unknown.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. pH alone does not identify composition or hazards. Even near neutrality, withhold use of an unknown liquid and verify its identity.
False. pH alone does not identify composition or hazards. Even near neutrality, withhold use of an unknown liquid and verify its identity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-01.stem: The designated-part shelf has a lower limit of 15 items and currently holds 12 correct items and 3 different items. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: The total is 15, so there is no shortage.
Correct parts are 3 below the lower limit; segregate the different items.
Relabel the different items as designated parts.
Stack stock up to the upper limit without replenishment instructions.
reasons: The 3 different items are not the required designated parts and cannot be added to stock.
There are 12 needed items, 3 below the lower limit of 15; identify and segregate the different items.
Changing a different item’s label does not change its specification and conceals a mix-up.
Follow instructions for the replenishment quantity as well; do not stack stock up to the upper limit without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-02.stem: A length of 0.45 mm must be entered in a field recorded in meters. Which value is correct?
reasons: 0.0045 m equals 4.5 mm, ten times the original 0.45 mm.
Changing only the unit to meters makes it 1000 times 0.45 mm.
450 m is one million times the correct value of 0.00045 m.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-03.stem: You want to reduce weight while keeping the material volume the same. What is needed after comparing density?
options: Regard weight reduction alone as suitability for all applications.
Replace it with a similar-looking material.
Check strength, deformation, temperature conditions and design approval.
reasons: Reduced weight is one benefit; it does not guarantee suitability for strength, temperature and other requirements in every application.
Similar-looking materials may differ in composition and properties; do not replace them without authorization.
Omitting material-grade records prevents checking compatibility with required properties and tracing history.
In addition to the density-related mass change, check strength, deformation, temperature and design approval.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-04.stem: Calculate on paper the reduction percentage from a plate thickness of 10 mm to 8 mm. Which value is correct?
reasons: 25% uses the final thickness of 8 mm as the denominator.
Reduction 2 mm ÷ original thickness 10 mm × 100 = 20%.
80% represents the remaining thickness, not the reduction percentage.
A reduction of 2 mm is not the same as a percentage of 2%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-05.stem: A decimal point on a copied drawing is unreadable, while another component’s drawing is clear. Which response is appropriate?
options: Withhold the affected work and request a readable approved drawing for the actual component.
Determine the official value by measuring the line on paper.
reasons: Do not guess the component’s requirements; withhold related work until they can be checked on a readable approved drawing.
Another component’s drawing cannot establish the dimensional requirements for this component.
Choosing a seemingly larger value is a guess, not formal verification of requirements.
Print scale and magnification can vary; do not substitute paper line length for the written dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-06.stem: A health consultation and equipment-failure report were both reduced to one greeting. What improvement is needed?
options: A loud voice removes the need for content.
Knowing the responsible person’s name removes the need to communicate.
Convey specific information to the respective contact points.
Complete everything using only a coworker’s speculation.
reasons: Even a loud voice does not constitute consultation if the health problem or failure details are not conveyed.
Knowing the responsible person’s name alone does not deliver information.
Convey the specific subject and facts for health consultation and failure reporting to the appropriate respective contacts.
Do not omit checking with specialist contacts based only on a coworker’s speculation.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-07.stem: You want to try a DC supply on equipment for which only an AC marking is known. Which response is appropriate?
options: Ask the responsible person about ratings and the specified supply; do not make an unverified connection.
The supply type is unnecessary if the numbers match.
Matching connector shapes always guarantee compatibility.
Try it because DC is not dangerous.
reasons: Cross-check the supply type and required ratings against specifications; do not connect while information remains unknown.
Even with the same voltage, differences in AC/DC type, frequency or other conditions may make the equipment incompatible.
Connector shape does not guarantee suitability for supply type or ratings.
DC also presents electric-shock and other hazards; do not justify a trial connection on assumed safety.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-08.stem: Of 200 inspected items, 5 are nonconforming. Which percentage and denominator combination is correct?
reasons: The inspected group is 200 items; using 100 as the denominator changes the target group.
2000 is not the inspected count and makes the percentage one tenth of its correct value.
97.5% represents the 195 conforming items, not the nonconforming-unit percentage.
5 nonconforming items ÷ 200 inspected items × 100 = 2.5%.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-09.stem: Record the ratio obtained from equal volumes of reference water weighing 25 g and a sample weighing 75 g. Which is appropriate?
reasons: Specific gravity is a dimensionless ratio; do not attach the density unit g/cm³ directly.
75 − 25 = 50 g is a mass difference, not a ratio.
The equal-volume ratio is 75 ÷ 25 = 3; also record reference-water, temperature and other conditions.
0.333 reverses the ratio, and kg is additionally a unit of mass.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-03-practical-10.stem: A box label is readable, but its contents are from a different lot. What is needed?
options: Readability means the information is correct.
Check that the product name, specification, quantity and lot match the contents.
Erasing the marking solves the issue.
reasons: Readability and agreement between the marking and contents are separate checks.
Compare the product name, specification, quantity and lot with the actual items, ensuring correct correspondence.
Weight alone cannot verify the part number, specification or lot.
Erasing the marking loses identification information and does not resolve the incorrect-lot issue.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-01.stem: HRC and HV values can be compared directly as the same scale without checking the methods.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. HRC and HV are scales for different hardness tests. Do not directly compare numbers without checking methods and conditions.
False. HRC and HV are scales for different hardness tests. Do not directly compare numbers without checking methods and conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-02.stem: This app’s mock exams are independently created and do not reproduce questions that actually appeared in the exam.
reasons: True. The referenced exam overview specifies CBT, with 30 theory true/false questions and 10 practical multiple-choice questions assessing judgment, planning and related skills. Despite the name “practical,” this format is different from operating an actual machine. This app’s mock exams are independently authored, not reproductions of questions that actually appeared.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The referenced exam overview specifies CBT, with 30 theory true/false questions and 10 practical multiple-choice questions assessing judgment, planning and related skills. Despite the name “practical,” this format is different from operating an actual machine. This app’s mock exams are independently authored, not reproductions of questions that actually appeared.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-03.stem: Do not determine a dimension type merely because one symbol is not visible; also read the target geometry and both ends of the dimension line.
reasons: True. Radius is indicated by R, diameter by φ, and plate thickness by t, for example. Symbols may sometimes be omitted when the dimension-line direction or end marks make the meaning clear. Do not decide the dimension type solely because a symbol is not visible; check the feature and both ends of the dimension line. For example, R6 means radius 6 and φ6 means diameter 6; they do not specify the same shape.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Radius is indicated by R, diameter by φ, and plate thickness by t, for example. Symbols may sometimes be omitted when the dimension-line direction or end marks make the meaning clear. Do not decide the dimension type solely because a symbol is not visible; check the feature and both ends of the dimension line. For example, R6 means radius 6 and φ6 means diameter 6; they do not specify the same shape.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-04.stem: Electrostatic painting and electrodeposition painting mean exactly the same equipment and process.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Electrostatic painting uses forces due to electric charge; electrodeposition uses electricity in a bath. Their adhesion principles, equipment and processes are not identical.
False. Electrostatic painting uses forces due to electric charge; electrodeposition uses electricity in a bath. Their adhesion principles, equipment and processes are not identical.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-05.stem: In the contact CMM example, dimensions and other characteristics are evaluated from coordinates of probe contact positions; a hole-position result cannot be copied directly as an Ra roughness result.
reasons: True. CMM position and dimensional evaluation differs from the microscopic irregularities evaluated by a stylus roughness tester; check the specified parameters and conditions.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Coordinates and roughness parameters are different quantities, so the distinction requiring separate results is correct.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-06.stem: An outside micrometer holds the object between a screw-driven spindle and a fixed anvil.
reasons: True. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-07.stem: The material name “plastic” alone makes a product suitable as protective equipment for any electrical work.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Insulating performance depends on voltage, temperature, damage and other conditions. Do not substitute ordinary plastic products for specified protective equipment.
False. Insulating performance depends on voltage, temperature, damage and other conditions. Do not substitute ordinary plastic products for specified protective equipment.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-08.stem: A V-block helps support cylinders and similar objects, but simply placing a cylinder on it does not mean all its dimensions have been measured.
reasons: True. The V-groove helps support the object; dimensions are measured separately with a defined target, reference, instrument and method.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Supporting and reading dimensions have different roles; placement alone does not establish completed measurement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-04-theory-09.stem: Theory and practical sections are judged only by the combined correct-answer percentage, allowing a shortfall in one section to be offset.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Under this app’s practice conditions, theory requires at least 20/30 and practical at least 6/10 independently. A combined score does not compensate for a shortfall in either section.
