mfg1-surface-mock-08-theory-q26.stem: Check quality and safety impacts even for circular-use improvements.
reasons: True is correct. Confirm resource saving does not increase defects or hazards.
False is inappropriate. Confirm resource saving does not increase defects or hazards.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-theory-q27.stem: Near delivery deadlines, normally ignore abnormal vibration and continue.
reasons: True is incorrect. Continuing abnormalities can increase accidents or quality defects.
False is correct. Continuing abnormalities can increase accidents or quality defects.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-theory-q28.stem: Separate observed facts from suspected causes in reports.
reasons: True is correct. Distinguishing speculation reduces misunderstanding and decision errors.
False is inappropriate. Distinguishing speculation reduces misunderstanding and decision errors.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-theory-q29.stem: Zinc never corrodes even in acidic or alkaline environments.
reasons: True is incorrect. Zinc also corrodes under acid, alkali and other conditions.
False is correct. Zinc also corrodes under acid, alkali and other conditions.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-theory-q30.stem: Fan-noise measures must preserve necessary exhaust performance.
reasons: True is correct. Stopping exhaust must not increase harmful exposure elsewhere.
False is inappropriate. Stopping exhaust must not increase harmful exposure elsewhere.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-01.stem: Checking roundness at one cross section alone does not verify cylindricity requirements for the cylindrical shape over its full length.
reasons: True. A circle’s shape and the shape of the entire cylinder concern different targets; evaluate the required range using the measurement plan.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A good circle at one cross section does not guarantee the same shape at other sections or over the full length; check these as separate requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-02.stem: Casting forms the intended shape by removing solid material as chips.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Casting places molten metal into a mold and lets it solidify. Removing solid material with a tool describes cutting.
False. Casting places molten metal into a mold and lets it solidify. Removing solid material with a tool describes cutting.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-03.stem: Do not operate an unfamiliar machine, or one whose operation you do not understand, on your own judgment.
reasons:
True. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.
When reporting, state the equipment name, when you noticed the condition, the facts observed, and the action already taken. Saying only “I think it is broken” makes it difficult for the listener to assess the situation. Separate assumptions from facts if the cause is not yet confirmed. Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Familiarity alone cannot determine whether a machine is safe. Before work, confirm the equipment you are responsible for, the procedure, how to stop it, and whom to contact. Do not operate an unfamiliar machine or one whose controls you do not understand on your own initiative.
If you notice an unusual sound, smell, or vibration during work, give priority to preventing danger from spreading rather than finding a reason to continue. Stop the machine using the prescribed procedure and notify the person responsible from a safe position. Never put your hand into a running machine to remove chips or parts.
When reporting, state the equipment name, when you noticed the condition, the facts observed, and the action already taken. Saying only “I think it is broken” makes it difficult for the listener to assess the situation. Separate assumptions from facts if the cause is not yet confirmed. Even after stopping, do not restart the machine or open a cover to investigate without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-04.stem: Reducing unnecessary packaging and collecting used packaging to return it to material resources address different stages.
reasons: True. Reduce prevents waste generation, reuse uses an item repeatedly, and recycle uses waste as a resource. These are not different names for the same task. Reducing unnecessary packaging and collecting used packaging to turn it back into material act at different stages.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Reduce prevents waste generation, reuse uses an item repeatedly, and recycle uses waste as a resource. These are not different names for the same task. Reducing unnecessary packaging and collecting used packaging to turn it back into material act at different stages.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-05.stem: A transistor only conducts in one direction and is not used for amplification or switching.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Transistors amplify signals and switch current on and off. Distinguish them from diodes, primarily described by one-way conduction.
False. Transistors amplify signals and switch current on and off. Distinguish them from diodes, primarily described by one-way conduction.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-06.stem: Fixed location defines where items belong; fixed item defines what belongs there; fixed quantity defines how much belongs there.
reasons:
True. The three fixed conditions make the location, type, and quantity of items explicit. Fixed location specifies where to put them, fixed item specifies what to put there, and fixed quantity specifies how much to keep. Combining all three makes shortages and mixed items easier to detect.
Even if a tool outline marks its place, returning a different size of tool fails the fixed-item rule. Likewise, placing the correct parts on the correct shelf but stacking them beyond the limit can make retrieval difficult and lead to toppling or falling items.
More stock does not automatically mean greater reassurance. Set the amount according to the process requirement, replenishment timing, and storage method. Sharing how to report and replenish when stock falls below the lower limit makes the system easier to operate when staff change.
If you cannot read a location or item label, do not replenish parts based only on their appearance. Check the label and instructions; place unidentified items separately in the designated area and ask for advice.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The three fixed conditions make the location, type, and quantity of items explicit. Fixed location specifies where to put them, fixed item specifies what to put there, and fixed quantity specifies how much to keep. Combining all three makes shortages and mixed items easier to detect.
Even if a tool outline marks its place, returning a different size of tool fails the fixed-item rule. Likewise, placing the correct parts on the correct shelf but stacking them beyond the limit can make retrieval difficult and lead to toppling or falling items.
More stock does not automatically mean greater reassurance. Set the amount according to the process requirement, replenishment timing, and storage method. Sharing how to report and replenish when stock falls below the lower limit makes the system easier to operate when staff change.
If you cannot read a location or item label, do not replenish parts based only on their appearance. Check the label and instructions; place unidentified items separately in the designated area and ask for advice.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-07.stem: Specific gravity must always carry the density unit g/cm³.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Specific gravity is a dimensionless ratio of like quantities. g/cm³ is a density unit and must not simply be attached to specific gravity.
False. Specific gravity is a dimensionless ratio of like quantities. g/cm³ is a density unit and must not simply be attached to specific gravity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-08.stem: The basic connection for an ammeter is directly in parallel across the supply.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An ammeter is connected in series in the branch being measured. Direct parallel connection across the supply can cause a dangerous short circuit.
False. An ammeter is connected in series in the branch being measured. Direct parallel connection across the supply can cause a dangerous short circuit.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-09.stem: If you find fire or smoke, notify others using the workplace emergency procedure and secure a safe evacuation route.
reasons: True. On discovering fire or smoke, alert others through the workplace emergency procedure and secure a safe evacuation route. In normal conditions, check not only extinguisher locations but also whom to call, the assembly point and the conditions for evacuation. Do not return to investigate a place obscured by smoke.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. On discovering fire or smoke, alert others through the workplace emergency procedure and secure a safe evacuation route. In normal conditions, check not only extinguisher locations but also whom to call, the assembly point and the conditions for evacuation. Do not return to investigate a place obscured by smoke.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-10.stem: Two people’s readings under different temperature conditions may simply be averaged without checking conditions.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Different temperatures, viewing angles or other conditions change the meaning of reading differences. First align specified conditions and recheck.
False. Different temperatures, viewing angles or other conditions change the meaning of reading differences. First align specified conditions and recheck.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-11.stem: The same number represents different quantities with different units; check that units agree across instructions, displays and recording fields.
reasons: True. The seven SI base units are metre m for length, kilogram kg for mass, second s for time, ampere A for electric current, kelvin K for thermodynamic temperature, mole mol for amount of substance, and candela cd for luminous intensity. Workplaces also use mm, g, and ms. Identical numbers with different units represent different quantities, so check the units in the instruction, display, and record field together.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The seven SI base units are metre m for length, kilogram kg for mass, second s for time, ampere A for electric current, kelvin K for thermodynamic temperature, mole mol for amount of substance, and candela cd for luminous intensity. Workplaces also use mm, g, and ms. Identical numbers with different units represent different quantities, so check the units in the instruction, display, and record field together.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-12.stem: The largest view drawn may be designated the front view without checking.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The front view is selected considering shape, function and the directions of use or machining. Do not choose by drawing size alone.
False. The front view is selected considering shape, function and the directions of use or machining. Do not choose by drawing size alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-13.stem: When choosing a comparative measuring instrument, check that its geometry contacts the intended surface correctly and that its measurement range and resolution are suitable.
reasons: True. A lever-type indicator has a contact point that pivots like a lever. A cylinder gauge has a shape for comparative bore measurement. A dial caliper gauge has inside/outside-caliper-like contacts for hard-to-reach locations such as grooves. Check correct contact with the target surface as well as suitable range and resolution.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A lever-type indicator has a contact point that pivots like a lever. A cylinder gauge has a shape for comparative bore measurement. A dial caliper gauge has inside/outside-caliper-like contacts for hard-to-reach locations such as grooves. Check correct contact with the target surface as well as suitable range and resolution.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-14.stem: For conditions not covered by inspection procedures or items difficult to judge, consult quality staff rather than accepting them by yourself.
reasons: True. Do not independently pass an item whose condition is absent from the procedure or difficult to judge. Keep unjudged items identified and separated, and tell the quality staff the target and uncertainty. A pass-rate goal does not permit relaxing the criteria.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Do not independently pass an item whose condition is absent from the procedure or difficult to judge. Keep unjudged items identified and separated, and tell the quality staff the target and uncertainty. A pass-rate goal does not permit relaxing the criteria.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-15.stem: Sorting means discarding everything, including needed tools.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Sorting distinguishes needed from unneeded items. Do not discard everything including needed tools; also verify disposal authority.
False. Sorting distinguishes needed from unneeded items. Do not discard everything including needed tools; also verify disposal authority.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-16.stem: If an oil leak can be cleaned up, investigating its cause becomes unnecessary.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even after cleaning removes a slipping hazard, the leak recurs if its cause remains. Distinguish temporary action from measures addressing the cause and effectiveness checks.
False. Even after cleaning removes a slipping hazard, the leak recurs if its cause remains. Distinguish temporary action from measures addressing the cause and effectiveness checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-17.stem: In comparative measurement, set the indication using a reference such as gauge blocks, replace it with the workpiece and read the difference.
reasons: True. A dial indicator amplifies contact-point movement. In comparative measurement, set it against a reference such as a gauge block, replace that reference with the part, and read the difference. Do not mistake the small displayed difference for the part’s entire dimension.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A dial indicator amplifies contact-point movement. In comparative measurement, set it against a reference such as a gauge block, replace that reference with the part, and read the difference. Do not mistake the small displayed difference for the part’s entire dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-18.stem: Checking breaks and hydration for heat around a furnace addresses a different hazard from checking dust sources, ventilation and protection.
reasons: True. Heat creates bodily thermal strain, while dust presents particle-exposure and other hazards; breaks and hydration do not replace source control or ventilation.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Heat creates bodily thermal strain, while dust presents particle-exposure and other hazards; breaks and hydration do not replace source control or ventilation.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-19.stem: A morning nod alone constitutes a specific report of an equipment abnormality.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A nod does not communicate the equipment, abnormal facts or action taken. Greetings and specific abnormality reports have different purposes.
False. A nod does not communicate the equipment, abnormal facts or action taken. Greetings and specific abnormality reports have different purposes.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-20.stem: A crane load may fall because of wire-rope or attachment defects.
reasons: True. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A crane load can fall because of a wire-rope or attachment problem. Stay out from under the load and outside designated danger areas; follow access control and signals. Slinging and operation require the necessary qualifications, training and assigned scope. A nearby bystander must not independently start helping.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-21.stem: Deformation remaining after force is removed is called complete elastic recovery.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Deformation remaining after force is removed relates to plasticity. Elasticity is recovery of deformation when force is removed.
False. Deformation remaining after force is removed relates to plasticity. Elasticity is recovery of deformation when force is removed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-22.stem: Sφ8 indicates a sphere diameter of 8 and SR8 a sphere radius of 8, so the same number does not specify spheres of the same size.
reasons: True. A sphere with radius 8 has diameter 16 and differs in size from a sphere with diameter 8.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Losing the diameter/radius distinction between Sφ and SR confuses sphere sizes, so the statement is correct.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-23.stem: Actual examination questions may be freely shared in a private study group.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Do not take out or share actual examination questions or answers, even privately. Learn using independently created general examples.
False. Do not take out or share actual examination questions or answers, even privately. Learn using independently created general examples.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-24.stem: Work hardening never occurs in cold rolling.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Plastic deformation during cold rolling can also cause work hardening. Check heat treatment and other steps as necessary.
False. Plastic deformation during cold rolling can also cause work hardening. Check heat treatment and other steps as necessary.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-25.stem: An impact test examines energy absorbed when a specimen fractures under sudden loading and other characteristics.
reasons: True. Impact tests examine energy absorbed when a specimen breaks under a sudden load. A pendulum apparatus uses the difference in its swing heights before and after fracture. Comparisons require matching specified specimen, temperature, notch and test-method conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Impact tests examine energy absorbed when a specimen breaks under a sudden load. A pendulum apparatus uses the difference in its swing heights before and after fracture. Comparisons require matching specified specimen, temperature, notch and test-method conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-26.stem: Parenthesized reference dimensions may have their parentheses removed and be changed into formal standalone acceptance criteria.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Parentheses identify a reference dimension. Removing them changes its role; separately verify the formal instructions used for machining and judgment.
False. Parentheses identify a reference dimension. Removing them changes its role; separately verify the formal instructions used for machining and judgment.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-27.stem: For near misses, recording the location, actions and surrounding conditions as well as the avoided fall or dropped-load outcome helps investigate causes.
reasons: True. A near miss is an event in which a danger was noticed even though no accident resulted. Examples include an object nearly falling or someone nearly slipping. Record the location, action and surrounding conditions as well as the outcome to help investigate causes. Do not omit a record just because nobody was hurt.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A near miss is an event in which a danger was noticed even though no accident resulted. Examples include an object nearly falling or someone nearly slipping. Record the location, action and surrounding conditions as well as the outcome to help investigate causes. Do not omit a record just because nobody was hurt.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-28.stem: A ring-shaped limit gauge is automatically a reference usable for any inside-diameter setting.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even among ring-shaped gauges, limit-acceptance and setting-reference functions differ. Cross-check the specified use, dimensions and inspection condition.
False. Even among ring-shaped gauges, limit-acceptance and setting-reference functions differ. Cross-check the specified use, dimensions and inspection condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-29.stem: Uppercase and lowercase unit-prefix letters need not be distinguished.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Uppercase and lowercase letters may change unit or prefix meanings. For example, do not treat m and M as the same multiplier.
False. Uppercase and lowercase letters may change unit or prefix meanings. For example, do not treat m and M as the same multiplier.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-theory-30.stem: A specimen generally cannot be used as a product after a tensile test taken through fracture.
reasons: True. A tensile test applies tensile force to a specimen and examines properties from the force and extension. With original cross-sectional area A and force F, engineering stress is F ÷ A. With original gauge length L and extension ΔL, engineering strain is ΔL ÷ L; multiply by 100 for percent. Testing generally continues to fracture, so the specimen cannot be used unchanged as a product.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A tensile test applies tensile force to a specimen and examines properties from the force and extension. With original cross-sectional area A and force F, engineering stress is F ÷ A. With original gauge length L and extension ΔL, engineering strain is ΔL ÷ L; multiply by 100 for percent. Testing generally continues to fracture, so the specimen cannot be used unchanged as a product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-01.stem: After carrying sheet material, you plan to drill using the same gloves. How should you change over?
options: Thicker gloves make rotating work safe.
With glasses, glove requirements do not matter.
Complete every process with the same equipment.
Check requirements for each process and do not wear gloves during drilling operations.
reasons: Even thick gloves do not eliminate entanglement hazards at rotating tools.
Eye protection from glasses does not resolve glove-entanglement hazards.
Sheet handling and drilling have different hazards; do not reuse the same equipment unconditionally.
Change to the process-specific requirements and do not wear gloves while drilling on a running drill press.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-02.stem: You want to inspect surface-breaking cracks and internal cavities in a nonmagnetic material. Which organization of the request is appropriate?
options: Separately confirm methods suited to defect locations and material with inspection staff.
Judge everything using magnetic particles alone.
A good visual result also guarantees the interior.
Treat methods as identical if their names sound similar.
reasons: Surface openings and internal defects occupy different locations; confirm each method’s applicability to nonmagnetic materials with inspection staff.
Magnetic-particle testing presupposes a magnetizable material; do not assume applicability to all defects in nonmagnetic materials.
A visual surface result does not guarantee absence of internal cavities.
Similar names do not mean identical principles, inspection locations or material conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-03.stem: Repolishing is expected to bring the outside diameter close to its lower limit. What should be checked before starting?
options: Remaining machining allowance, required dimensions and roughness, and approved disposition.
reasons: Gloss alone cannot verify outside-diameter or roughness requirements after rework.
Compare removable allowance against outside-diameter and roughness requirements and verify the approved refinishing method.
A shorter duration does not establish that the lower dimensional limit will be maintained.
Follow formal requirements and approved disposition rather than personal preference.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-04.stem: An unknown-composition liquid has a recorded pH of 6.9. How should its usability be treated?
options: It is harmless because it is near neutral.
Mix in alkali to identify it.
Do not use it until identity, temperature, measurement conditions and original records are checked.
Use pH to determine its complete redox state.
reasons: Near-neutral pH does not mean composition or hazards are known.
Mixing alkali into an unknown liquid is hazardous and does not replace identification checks.
Withhold use until the liquid’s correspondence with the original record, temperature, method and other conditions are checked.
pH indicates acidity or alkalinity; it does not determine every aspect of electron-transfer state.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-05.stem: The same dimension is duplicated as 28 and 30. Which inquiry to the responsible person is appropriate?
options: State only that you will machine to the average, 29.
Correct the drawing to the larger value, 30.
Identify the target location and both values, and ask which requirement applies.
reasons: The average, 29, is not an approved requirement and does not resolve the contradiction.
Keeping only the larger value is also an unauthorized drawing change.
Specifically show the same location and both values and inquire about the formally applicable requirement.
Ease of measurement cannot determine the applicable required dimension.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-06.stem: Someone proposes a lift with more widely spread wire ropes than before. What should you do?
options: The same load invariably means the same tension.
Decide the angle by appearance alone.
Adjust it by hand from below the load.
Check the load, lifting gear, specified plan and your assigned scope.
reasons: A changed rope-spread angle can change rope forces even with the same load.
Do not determine safe angles or gear suitability by appearance alone.
Entering beneath a suspended load risks falling loads and contact; do not enter to adjust it.
Check the load, gear, lifting plan, required qualifications and assigned scope; do not change them without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-07.stem: A wire’s covering is damaged, but its material is named an insulator. What should you do?
options: The word insulating guarantees complete safety.
Report defects in its condition and specified requirements; do not continue using it on your own judgment.
Damage does not matter if the color is unchanged.
Apply an ordinary piece of resin and finish.
reasons: The material name insulator alone cannot guarantee the protective performance of damaged covering.
Report the damage and operating conditions; do not continue independently until necessary checks and action are provided.
Even with unchanged color, scratches or dirt can affect insulating performance.
An ordinary resin piece does not verify suitability of the specified repair material or method.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-08.stem: In a micrometer example, the sleeve reads 11.5 mm and the thimble 0.24 mm. What is the total?
reasons: This adds only 0.24 mm to 11 mm, omitting the 0.5 mm half graduation.
This concatenates 11.5 and 24 as text rather than adding values.
Adding the sleeve and thimble quantities correctly gives 11.74 mm, not 35.50 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-09.stem: You want to use a penetrant result for surface-breaking cracks to guarantee absence of all internal defects. What should you do?
options: Every nondestructive method invariably finds all defects.
Substitute a good surface result for the internal result.
Do not guarantee it; check the required internal-inspection scope and method.
reasons: Each nondestructive method has detectable defect types and applicability conditions; finding every defect cannot be guaranteed.
Substituting a surface-opening result for an internal result falsely treats unverified interiors as checked.
Without method, scope and condition records, the meaning of a result cannot be traced.
Do not guarantee the interior from a penetrant surface result; check the necessary internal-inspection method and scope.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-06-practical-10.stem: A returned tray will be used again for the same purpose. What should be checked before approval?
options: Check damage, contamination, mixed part numbers and specified conditions.
reasons: Condition changes even during reuse, so damage, dirt and other factors require checking.
Collected quantity does not guarantee tray condition or reuse requirements.
Before reuse, check damage, contamination and mix-ups and assess compliance with approved conditions.
Hiding dirt prevents checking and appropriate cleaning or other action.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-01.stem: Gauge blocks are used for length and reference ring gauges for comparative measurement of inside diameters and similar dimensions.
reasons: True. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Gauge blocks provide length references and master rings provide references such as bore size. Limit gauges check whether holes or shafts meet specified limits, generally using GO and NO-GO sides together. Even ring-shaped gauges have different roles as setting masters and acceptance gauges.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-02.stem: Components with the same external shape can be judged interchangeable without checking part numbers or terminals.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even identical external shapes can have different part numbers, terminals, ratings and functions. Compare drawings and specified components.
False. Even identical external shapes can have different part numbers, terminals, ratings and functions. Compare drawings and specified components.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-03.stem: For every application, a smaller surface-roughness number is unconditionally better.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Required roughness depends on the application, including friction and lubrication. A lower value is not necessarily better for every function.
False. Required roughness depends on the application, including friction and lubrication. A lower value is not necessarily better for every function.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-04.stem: Safety shoes, protective glasses, gloves and similar equipment may differ in performance and application even under the same name.
reasons:
True. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment is used to shield the body from danger. Safety footwear, protective glasses, and gloves may differ in performance and purpose even when they share the same name. Use the type specified for your task and inspect it for damage, dirt, and proper fit before use.
Gloves protect hands during activities such as handling sharp material. However, they can become a source of danger in work where a rotating tool could catch them. Do not wear gloves while drilling with a drill press. Keep hands away from rotating parts and observe the prohibitions in the procedure.
Wearing protective glasses does not permit removal of a machine guard. Protective equipment must be used together with equipment safety measures and correct working methods. Check that its performance is appropriate for hazards such as flying particles, chemicals, or dust.
If the equipment does not fit, obscures your view, or is damaged, do not tolerate the problem and continue working; ask for replacement or adjustment. Do not substitute another person’s protective equipment without permission.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-05.stem: The more rolling oil is supplied, the better processing invariably becomes.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Follow equipment and product specifications for oil type and supply conditions. More is not necessarily better; do not address defects through quantity alone.
False. Follow equipment and product specifications for oil type and supply conditions. More is not necessarily better; do not address defects through quantity alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-06.stem: When selecting a material to conduct heat away, check thermal conductivity; do not determine heat-transfer performance solely from density or surface gloss.
reasons: True. Thermal conductivity describes ease of heat transfer and is a physical property distinct from density or light reflection.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Being light or shiny alone does not guarantee required heat dissipation, so checking thermal conductivity is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-07.stem: In third-angle projection, the top view is placed above the front view and the view from the right is placed to its right.
reasons: True. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A projection view represents the shape of a solid object on a plane. In third-angle projection, the top view, seen from above, is placed above the front view, and the right-side view, seen from the right, is placed to its right. First check the front view and the stated projection method so you do not confuse left and right on the paper with the direction from which the object is viewed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-08.stem: You may hold down a moving extruded product by hand to examine streaks.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Reaching toward a moving product creates contact, entanglement and other hazards. Investigate after safe stopping and using specified procedures.
False. Reaching toward a moving product creates contact, entanglement and other hazards. Investigate after safe stopping and using specified procedures.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-09.stem: The area around a weld includes a heat-affected zone where heat changes structure or properties without melting; do not assume its properties invariably remain unchanged.
reasons: True. Heat can change metal structure or properties while it remains solid; verify the necessary area through specified inspection.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Remaining unmelted does not prove absence of effects, so the statement requiring evaluation of surrounding areas is not false.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-10.stem: Even if a dial indicator has a short hand, reading only the long hand is sufficient.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. For instruments with a short hand, include the long hand’s complete revolutions. Reading only the long hand can confuse total travel.
False. For instruments with a short hand, include the long hand’s complete revolutions. Reading only the long hand can confuse total travel.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-23.stem: The seven SI base units are meter m, kilogram kg, second s, ampere A, kelvin K, mole mol and candela cd.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-24.stem: Following a work standard allows the measurement frequency in a QC process chart to be omitted.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-25.stem: Rolling oil adjusts friction between rolls and material and helps processing proceed smoothly.
reasons: True. Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-26.stem: Once a machine is stopped, its cover may be opened for investigation without waiting for restart authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-28.stem: The material’s occupational safety and health explanation identifies three aspects: harm-prevention standards, responsibility systems and voluntary activities.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-theory-30.stem: If a contact tip reaches a hole entrance, the diameter of a groove farther inside is also considered measured.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The entrance and inner groove are separate measurement locations. Verify a contact geometry and reference suited to the intended surface; record unreachable locations as unverified.
False. The entrance and inner groove are separate measurement locations. Verify a contact geometry and reference suited to the intended surface; record unreachable locations as unverified.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-01.stem: After a leak countermeasure, oil flows to another location. How should effectiveness be checked?
options: Do not record it because measures are complete.
Finish if only the original location is dry.
Wait until pedestrians get used to it.
Check the original issue and new hazards and review the measures.
reasons: Another leak appearing after measures also needs recording as a fact in the effectiveness check.
Even if the original location is dry, oil merely moved elsewhere leaves a new slipping hazard.
Pedestrians getting used to it does not eliminate the cause of leakage or slipping.
Check both whether the original issue was resolved and whether new hazards exist, and review measures.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-02.stem: Two readings differ; one person read a hot workpiece from an angle. What is needed first?
options: Align temperature, viewing direction, holding, location and instrument conditions and check again.
Ignore other conditions because zero is correct.
reasons: Align temperature, parallax, holding, target location and instrument condition before comparing values.
Averaging values under different conditions does not establish the cause of differences or correctness.
Selecting only the smaller value is choosing conveniently, not following specified measurement.
Correct zero does not eliminate high-temperature or parallax effects.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-03.stem: You observed molten metal solidifying in a mold, followed by hole cutting. Which classification is correct?
options: All steps are forging because the final step cuts a hole.
A process combining casting and cutting.
Everything is pressing because a mold is used.
reasons: Forging is plastic working using pressure or impact, unlike molten-metal solidification or hole cutting.
The process combines casting molten metal to solidify in a mold and cutting a hole with a tool.
Casting and other processes also use molds; not all can be called pressing.
Actual products can combine multiple processes, such as cutting after casting.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-04.stem: One proposal reduces unnecessary packaging when ordering; another returns used packaging to raw material. How are they classified?
options: The first is reuse and the second waste prevention.
The first is reduce and the second recycle.
Both are different names for the same work.
reasons: Reducing generation and returning to raw material both differ from reuse, which uses the item again as it is.
Reducing at ordering is waste prevention; returning to raw material is not reuse.
The first reduces unnecessary generation and is reduce; the second returns material to resources and is recycle.
Prevention before generation and resource recovery after use address different stages.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-05.stem: You are copying R5, φ5 and (20) into notes. Which organization is correct?
options: Retain radius, diameter and reference roles and the parentheses.
Put all into the same field as diameters.
Remove parentheses to make acceptance criteria.
Freely delete the original symbol in R5.
reasons: Copy R as radius, φ as diameter and the parenthesized value as a reference dimension, preserving their roles.
R5 and φ5 impose different geometry requirements; (20) has the separate reference role.
Removing parentheses changes a reference value into a formal judgment instruction without authorization.
Erasing the original R loses the information that the value is a radius.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-06.stem: Only dust protection was prepared although gas is suspected. What needs checking?
options: A particle filter suits every gas.
The substance, oxygen and other conditions, specified protective equipment and facility measures.
reasons: Particle-filter performance does not mean protection against every gas.
Check gas type, oxygen and other environmental conditions and choose suitable specified protection and facility measures.
Layering cloth does not establish suitability for the gas or oxygen deficiency.
Odor alone cannot establish safety regarding gases or oxygen deficiency.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-07.stem: A capacitor is found on a circuit board after power is stopped. How should it be handled?
options: Short it with a tool to check.
Do not touch terminals until the prescribed residual-energy checks are complete.
It is the same as a resistor, so no check is needed.
reasons: Independently shorting it with a tool is not a safe residual-energy checking procedure.
Energy may remain after power is stopped; do not touch terminals until prescribed checks are complete.
Appearance cannot establish completed discharge.
Resistors and capacitors have different functions; stored energy cannot be ignored.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-08.stem: A 3:1 scale drawing labels a dimension 7 mm. What is the actual-size reading?
options: Unknown until the drawing is measured with a ruler.

There is no need to divide the written dimension by 3; dimension values indicate actual size.
The drawing has a written dimension; do not substitute a ruler measurement of the drawing.
The written 7 mm dimension indicates an actual 7 mm even at scale 3:1.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-09.stem: The calibration record is still in date, but the instrument was dropped. What should be done next?

Set zero and guarantee the full range.
reasons: Even within calibration validity, a fall can change instrument condition and cannot be ignored.

Setting zero alone cannot guarantee correctness across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-07-practical-10.stem: Management-system certification information and product dimensional results are shown together. Which treatment is correct?

The standard’s name removes the need to check revisions.
Distinguish organizational information from individual conformity judgments.
A mark removes the need for instrument inspection.
reasons: Certification of an organizational system is not an inspection result for individual products.
Even with the same standard name, check applicability and revision.
Organizational management information and individual dimensional conformity judgments concern different targets and must be distinguished.
A mark does not replace checks for instrument damage and operating condition.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-01.stem: Transistors are used to amplify small signals and control current switching on and off.

False. Even with specialist staff, workers’ observations need sharing. A representative’s name alone does not communicate an abnormality.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-16.stem: Do not merely memorize safety-sign shapes; also check the actions required at that location together with equipment procedures.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-18.stem: Polishing addresses appearance, roughness, friction and other purposes, but stronger gloss is not necessarily better for every application.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-19.stem: If a diameter is within tolerance, parallelism may also be regarded as measured.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Diameter tolerance and parallelism are separate requirements. Verify geometrical tolerances using the relevant target and datum.
False. Diameter tolerance and parallelism are separate requirements. Verify geometrical tolerances using the relevant target and datum.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-20.stem: On a lathe, distinguish the chuck’s workpiece-holding role from the tool post’s cutting-tool-holding role.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-22.stem: Energy stored in a capacitor invariably becomes zero when the power display goes dark.

False. Energy may remain in a capacitor after power is stopped. Do not judge by the stopped-power display; obtain the prescribed checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-23.stem: Read measuring-instrument graduations from directly in front because angled viewing can change readings through parallax.
reasons: True. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Measurements are affected by the instrument, operator, temperature, setup, and other factors. Read the scale straight on because an oblique view creates parallax. Check calibration relating the indication to a reference, daily inspection records, and validity; a correct zero alone does not guarantee correctness across the full range.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-24.stem: If dimensions for the same location conflict, the operator may machine to their average.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An average is not a formal requirement. Identify the conflicting location and ask the responsible person which dimension applies.
False. An average is not a formal requirement. Identify the conflicting location and ask the responsible person which dimension applies.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-25.stem: An observation of low pH does not mean the same thing as explaining that a substance lost electrons.
reasons: True. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Oxidation and reduction can also be explained through electron transfer: losing electrons is oxidation; gaining them is reduction. Rusting iron and combustion illustrate oxidation, but some reactions have no visible change. A low pH observation does not mean the same thing as a statement that a substance lost electrons.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-26.stem: Ra and Rz can be compared directly by number if their units match.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even with identical units, Ra and Rz have different definitions. Compare using the same specified parameter and conditions.
False. Even with identical units, Ra and Rz have different definitions. Compare using the same specified parameter and conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-27.stem: If a 2:1 drawing labels a dimension 12, the actual size is 24 mm.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Written dimensions indicate actual size regardless of scale. A dimension of 12 specifies 12 mm; drawing at twice size does not make it 24 mm.
False. Written dimensions indicate actual size regardless of scale. A dimension of 12 specifies 12 mm; drawing at twice size does not make it 24 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-28.stem: Grounding forms part of equipment protection and relates to current paths during abnormalities such as leakage.
reasons: True. Grounding is part of an equipment protection system and affects current paths during faults such as leakage. Where a grounding conductor is specified, check its connection and report defects. Do not describe grounding as preventing leakage itself or removing every electric-shock hazard.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Grounding is part of an equipment protection system and affects current paths during faults such as leakage. Where a grounding conductor is specified, check its connection and report defects. Do not describe grounding as preventing leakage itself or removing every electric-shock hazard.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-29.stem: When replacing a resistor, do not decide a smaller component is suitable from resistance alone; also check specified ratings and operating conditions.
reasons: True. Identical resistance values can have different ratings or operating conditions. Smaller external size alone does not guarantee interchangeability with the specified part.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Identical resistance values can have different ratings or operating conditions. Smaller external size alone does not guarantee interchangeability with the specified part.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-theory-30.stem: The operator may relax inspection criteria to maintain a target acceptance rate.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. An acceptance-rate target does not justify relaxing inspection requirements. Inspect to approved criteria and report uncertainties.
False. An acceptance-rate target does not justify relaxing inspection requirements. Inspect to approved criteria and report uncertainties.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-01.stem: Part of a cleaning-agent label is unreadable; a similarly shaped container is nearby. What should you do before use?
options: Assume the contents match the similar container.
Smell a small amount to investigate.
Mix it into another container before checking.
Withhold use and check identity, the SDS and instructions.
reasons: Identical container shapes do not necessarily mean identical contents.
Smelling an unknown substance can expose you to it.
Mixing unknown liquids can cause dangerous reactions or loss of identification information.
Withhold use and verify contents and handling using original identification, the SDS and approved instructions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-02.stem: A caliper reads in 0.05 mm increments; the main scale is 16 mm and the sixth vernier line aligns. What is the value?
reasons: This treats the sixth line as 0.06 mm without using the minimum reading of 0.05 mm.
This misreads the sixth line as 0.60 mm; 0.05 × 6 = 0.30 mm.
Main scale 16 + vernier 6 × 0.05 = 16.30 mm.
This adds line number 6 directly to main-scale value 16, ignoring the graduation quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-03.stem: The requirement is Ra 0.6 μm, but the only result given is Rz 2.4 μm. What should be done before judgment?
options: Obtain results for the specified Ra and conditions.
If dimensions conform, pass roughness too.
reasons: Ra and Rz are different parameters; obtain a result for the specified Ra and measurement conditions.
0.6 and 2.4 are values for different parameters and cannot be compared directly as numbers alone.
Rewriting measured Rz as Ra creates a record differing from the actual measurement.
Dimensional conformity does not substitute for surface-roughness conformity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-04.stem: The inspection sheet is revision C, while the standard on hand is revision D. What should be done before judgment?
options: Ask the responsible person which revision applies to the target product.
Ignore revisions because the equipment has a mark.
reasons: Being newer alone does not establish applicability to this product; do not adopt a revision without authorization.
Cross-check number, revision and target, and confirm with the responsible person what is specified for this product.
Reconstructing old conditions from memory does not formally verify applicability.
An equipment mark does not replace checking the document revision applicable to the product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-05.stem: “Parallelism 0.06, datum A” is specified, but the target surface is unclear. What should you do?
options: Check the indicated target and datum, including arrows, and consult about measurement.
Pass using a nearby convenient surface.
Record only the value and omit the target.
Treat parallelism as checked because length passed.
reasons: Compare the target and datum A using the feature-control frame, arrows and other indications; resolve uncertainties before finalizing the measurement method.
Choosing a convenient surface changes the formal target or datum without authorization.
A value alone does not identify which parallelism was measured; record the target surface too.
Length tolerance and parallelism are different characteristics; passing one does not verify the other.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-06.stem: You are considering initial firefighting, but the extinguisher’s suitability marking is unclear. What should you do?
options: Prioritize reporting and safe evacuation and do not attempt unsafe firefighting.
Enter the fire area to find the power supply.
reasons: Extinguishing agents suit different fires; do not treat them as identical.
Prioritize reporting and safe evacuation; do not force a response using an extinguisher of unknown suitability.
Water on oil can dangerously spread the fire and must not be used on your own judgment.
Entering the fire area to find power brings dangerous exposure to fire, smoke and electric shock.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-07.stem: A diode has a similar external shape to the component specified for amplification. Can it be substituted?
options: The same external shape means interchangeability.
Both are semiconductors, so every function is the same.
Try it and accept it if it does not heat up.
Do not replace until role, part number, terminals and ratings are verified as suitable.
reasons: Matching external shape alone does not verify compatible functions, terminals or ratings.
Even within the semiconductor category, diodes and amplification transistors have different roles.
Trial energization of an unknown component and lack of heating alone do not establish safety or functional suitability.
Do not replace until the circuit role, part number, terminals and ratings are verified against specifications.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-08.stem: A dimension is 18.00 ± 0.02 mm and the reading is 17.97 mm. Which simple limit comparison is correct?
options: Below the lower limit of 17.98 mm.
reasons: The range is 17.98–18.02 mm; 17.97 mm is not within range.
17.97 mm does not exceed the upper limit; it is below the lower limit.
Do not round conveniently to change an out-of-range reading into a pass.
The reading 17.97 mm is below the lower limit, 18.00 − 0.02 = 17.98 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-09.stem: A leak is found this morning, although yesterday’s periodic inspection passed. What should you do?
options: Record this morning’s facts and check action and whether operation is permitted.
Ignore the leak because yesterday passed.
reasons: Retain this morning’s leak as a new observation and check action and whether operation is permitted.
Yesterday’s periodic inspection does not guarantee this morning’s condition.
Recording normal after observing leakage contradicts the observation.
Internal inspection and disassembly require safety measures and authority; do not start on your own judgment.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-08-practical-10.stem: An impact test shows higher absorbed energy, but temperature and specimen also differ. How should material selection proceed?
options: Treat the largest number as best for every application.
Align requirements and test conditions and confirm the valid comparison scope with the responsible person.
Average it with post-bend observations as the same quantity.
reasons: Even a larger value cannot establish superiority for every application when test conditions differ.
Erasing temperature and specimen fields loses comparison assumptions and traceability information.
Align requirements and conditions such as specimens and temperature, and verify the scope in which comparisons are valid.
Absorbed energy and post-bend crack observations are different evaluations and cannot be averaged as the same quantity.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-01.stem: Heinrich’s ratio determines next month’s accident count for every workplace.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. 1:29:300 is a learning ratio emphasizing not dismissing warning signs; it is not a formula determining future accident counts for every workplace.
False. 1:29:300 is a learning ratio emphasizing not dismissing warning signs; it is not a formula determining future accident counts for every workplace.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-02.stem: Quality is supported throughout the flow of designing customer requirements, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping.
reasons: True. Quality is supported by the whole flow: translating customer requirements into design, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping. When inspection finds the wrong material, do not assume it is only the inspector’s failure. Share information about instructions, identification and handovers as well.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is supported by the whole flow: translating customer requirements into design, procuring materials, manufacturing, inspecting and shipping. When inspection finds the wrong material, do not assume it is only the inspector’s failure. Share information about instructions, identification and handovers as well.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-03.stem: φ10 and R10 specify the same circle size.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. φ10 specifies diameter 10, while R10 specifies radius 10, equivalent to diameter 20. These are not the same circle size.
False. φ10 specifies diameter 10, while R10 specifies radius 10, equivalent to diameter 20. These are not the same circle size.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-04.stem: A resistor adjusts circuit current and can also convert electrical energy into heat.
reasons: True. A resistor helps control circuit current and also converts electrical energy into heat. Use components that meet the required ratings as well as the resistance value. Do not decide that a smaller part is an acceptable replacement; report unusual heat or discoloration.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A resistor helps control circuit current and also converts electrical energy into heat. Use components that meet the required ratings as well as the resistance value. Do not decide that a smaller part is an acceptable replacement; report unusual heat or discoloration.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-05.stem: In hazard prediction, separately observing equipment, objects, human movements and surroundings helps reduce overlooked hazards.
reasons:
True. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
The four stages of KYT involve identifying several hazards, selecting the most important ones, considering countermeasures, and deciding on the team’s actions. During discussion, share observations from people seeing the situation for the first time as well as experienced workers.
A countermeasure consisting only of “be careful” is insufficient. Decide what to check, when, and how. Do not try to resolve an equipment problem through worker attention alone; discuss improvements with the person responsible.
Review whether the chosen measures were carried out and whether they created another hazard. KYT is not a drill for approaching actual danger to test it. Use safe materials and explanations instead of recreating real hazards.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
The four stages of KYT involve identifying several hazards, selecting the most important ones, considering countermeasures, and deciding on the team’s actions. During discussion, share observations from people seeing the situation for the first time as well as experienced workers.
A countermeasure consisting only of “be careful” is insufficient. Decide what to check, when, and how. Do not try to resolve an equipment problem through worker attention alone; discuss improvements with the person responsible.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-06.stem: If the NO-GO side does not pass, all specified thread turn-count and other conditions need no checking.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Threaded NO-GO gauges are used under specified insertion and turn-count conditions. Stopping alone does not justify omitting condition checks.
False. Threaded NO-GO gauges are used under specified insertion and turn-count conditions. Stopping alone does not justify omitting condition checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-07.stem: When adding upper and lower deviations to the basic size to obtain limit sizes, preserve their signs rather than adding or subtracting absolute values alone.
reasons: True. Add upper and lower deviations to the basic size with their signs. For example, 20 + (−0.02) = 19.98; dropping the sign gives an incorrect limit.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Add upper and lower deviations to the basic size with their signs. For example, 20 + (−0.02) = 19.98; dropping the sign gives an incorrect limit.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-08.stem: Every unhatched area invariably represents a cavity.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Some components are left unsectioned, so not every unhatched area is a cavity. Cross-check other views and the cutting extent.
False. Some components are left unsectioned, so not every unhatched area is a cavity. Cross-check other views and the cutting extent.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-09.stem: The guidance says readings accompany Japanese kanji, but consult the latest organizer information for applications, permitted belongings, eligibility and related matters.
reasons: True. The overview is information at the time recorded in the source. It says Japanese kanji receive furigana, but current organizer guidance must be checked for application, permitted belongings, eligibility and related rules. Passing a mock is not treated as automatically obtaining a qualification or work authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The overview is information at the time recorded in the source. It says Japanese kanji receive furigana, but current organizer guidance must be checked for application, permitted belongings, eligibility and related rules. Passing a mock is not treated as automatically obtaining a qualification or work authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-10.stem: A simple resistance-circuit calculation can be used directly for every motor’s starting current.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Simple constant-resistance DC calculations differ from motor-starting behavior. Do not generalize without checking applicability conditions.
False. Simple constant-resistance DC calculations differ from motor-starting behavior. Do not generalize without checking applicability conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-11.stem: Adding more uninspected items to the denominator makes the sample’s nonconforming-unit rate more accurate.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The sample rate divides nonconforming items by the inspected count. Mixing uninspected items into the denominator changes the target group.
False. The sample rate divides nonconforming items by the inspected count. Mixing uninspected items into the denominator changes the target group.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-12.stem: Do not replace a specified iron component with aluminum solely to reduce weight; also check strength, deformation, temperature and design approval.
reasons: True. Consider a component of volume 20 cm³. Assuming densities of 2.70 g/cm³ for aluminum and 7.87 g/cm³ for iron, their calculated masses are 54.0 g and 157.4 g respectively. However, lower mass does not authorize replacement of a specified iron component with aluminum. Required strength, deformation behavior, temperature conditions, and other factors must also be checked. Density varies with the material and alloy.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Consider a component of volume 20 cm³. Assuming densities of 2.70 g/cm³ for aluminum and 7.87 g/cm³ for iron, their calculated masses are 54.0 g and 157.4 g respectively. However, lower mass does not authorize replacement of a specified iron component with aluminum. Required strength, deformation behavior, temperature conditions, and other factors must also be checked. Density varies with the material and alloy.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-13.stem: In hazard prediction, go beyond an impression such as “dangerous” and consider specifically what causes which accident to whom.
reasons:
True. Hazard prediction should go beyond a general feeling that something is dangerous. Think specifically about what causes the danger, who may be affected, and what accident could occur. Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
The four stages of KYT involve identifying several hazards, selecting the most important ones, considering countermeasures, and deciding on the team’s actions. During discussion, share observations from people seeing the situation for the first time as well as experienced workers.

Looking separately at equipment, objects, people’s movements, and surrounding conditions helps reduce omissions.
