mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-14.stem: Operator training for new equipment automatically authorizes internal settings for which no training was given.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Operation and internal settings can have different training, qualification and authorization scopes. Operator training alone does not automatically authorize every task.
False. Operation and internal settings can have different training, qualification and authorization scopes. Operator training alone does not automatically authorize every task.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-15.stem: If an error is in another person’s record, you need not report it even after finding it.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Another person’s record can also affect products. Identify the original record and target and obtain prescribed correction and impact checks.
False. Another person’s record can also affect products. Identify the original record and target and obtain prescribed correction and impact checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-16.stem: If a crack is suspected in a high-speed grinding wheel, withhold use and obtain specified inspection and verification by the responsible person.
reasons: True. Cracks risk breakage and flying fragments during rotation; do not independently test-run the wheel or use its side to investigate.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Protective equipment does not remove the need to check wheel condition; withholding use is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-17.stem: Reusing a returned container requires no checks for dirt or damage.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Check dirt, damage and mix-ups before reuse too. Reusing an item in its existing form does not justify omitting condition checks.
False. Check dirt, damage and mix-ups before reuse too. Reusing an item in its existing form does not justify omitting condition checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-18.stem: In resin molding, distinguish materials solidified by cooling from those cured by chemical reaction; achieving shape alone does not remove the need to check cooling or curing.
reasons: True. Completion conditions differ with how the material solidifies; check specified cooling, curing, removal and inspection through completion.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Identical external shape can still leave temperature or reaction state unverified, so judging completion from shape alone is inappropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-19.stem: Grounding invariably eliminates leakage itself and every electric-shock hazard.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Grounding is one part of abnormal-condition protection; it does not invariably eliminate leakage itself or every electric-shock hazard.
False. Grounding is one part of abnormal-condition protection; it does not invariably eliminate leakage itself or every electric-shock hazard.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-20.stem: Ability to operate an earlier machine does not necessarily mean new equipment can be operated under the same conditions; check the equipment and training scope.
reasons: True. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-21.stem: For respiratory protection against harmful gases, check suitability for the substance and distinguish it from dust protection and oxygen-deficiency measures.
reasons: True. A dust respirator is intended to filter particles such as dust. Do not assume it removes harmful gases in the same way. Gases require checking protective equipment suitable for the substance, while oxygen deficiency is a separate hazard. Ask the responsible person about the type, applicable conditions and fitting checks.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A dust respirator is intended to filter particles such as dust. Do not assume it removes harmful gases in the same way. Gases require checking protective equipment suitable for the substance, while oxygen deficiency is a separate hazard. Ask the responsible person about the type, applicable conditions and fitting checks.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-22.stem: A motor only converts voltage and does not produce motive power.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A motor converts electricity into mechanical power. A device changing voltage in applicable circuits is a transformer.
False. A motor converts electricity into mechanical power. A device changing voltage in applicable circuits is a transformer.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-23.stem: Unnecessarily repeating the same dimension can cause conflicting values when changes are made.
reasons: True. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Dimensions give the information needed for a part’s function and manufacture and normally specify its finished dimensions. Repeating the same dimension unnecessarily can cause conflicting values after a change. Even if the drawing is printed large, read its stated dimensions rather than measuring the paper with a ruler as a substitute for the requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-24.stem: Watching an instructor demonstrate once allows independent work without checking understanding.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Watching a demonstration differs from being able to work safely alone. Verify understanding and assigned scope through explanation, performance and checking.
False. Watching a demonstration differs from being able to work safely alone. Verify understanding and assigned scope through explanation, performance and checking.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-25.stem: Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct electricity readily and are used for wiring and similar purposes.
reasons: True. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Metals such as copper and aluminum conduct readily and are used in wiring. Good conductivity alone does not establish component suitability: check the required cross-section, temperature, connections and specifications. Do not substitute a similarly colored material without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-26.stem: To reduce temperature effects in micrometer measurement, allow the instrument and object to equilibrate to the specified environment first.
reasons: True. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. An outside micrometer grips the object between the screw-driven spindle and the fixed anvil. Clean the measuring faces and check zero or the datum using a reference suitable for the range. Let the instrument and object acclimatize to the specified environment to reduce temperature effects. The textbook gives 20°C as the reference. Rushing to measure a hot product makes dimensional comparison inappropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-27.stem: A cart tipping without injury has no value as a record for improvement.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Even without injury, the tipping location, actions and conditions provide recurrence-prevention information. Record the facts as a near miss.
False. Even without injury, the tipping location, actions and conditions provide recurrence-prevention information. Record the facts as a near miss.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-28.stem: A nonmagnetic material can be deemed suitable for magnetic-particle testing without verifying its material.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Magnetic-particle testing applies to surface or near-surface defects in magnetizable objects. Do not assume suitability for nonmagnetic materials without material verification.
False. Magnetic-particle testing applies to surface or near-surface defects in magnetizable objects. Do not assume suitability for nonmagnetic materials without material verification.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-29.stem: Check the target equipment, product and revision of work procedures, and report display failures or unreadable paper text.
reasons: True. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A procedure states who does what, when and how. Merely possessing a document is insufficient if it cannot be read when needed at the work location. Check the equipment, product and version covered, and report failed displays or unreadable paper. Do not fill in unconfirmed conditions from memory alone.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-theory-30.stem: Cold rolling is cold, so touching the rotating rolls is safe.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Rotating rolls present entanglement hazards even during cold rolling. Do not treat the temperature-related name as a safety guarantee; follow access and contact prohibitions.
False. Rotating rolls present entanglement hazards even during cold rolling. Do not treat the temperature-related name as a safety guarantee; follow access and contact prohibitions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-01.stem: All dimensions for an order of 120 items pass, but the box contains only 118. Which shipment judgment is appropriate?
options: Check the quantity shortage as a separate nonconformity and consult about disposition.
Prioritize delivery and ship labeled 120 items.
Change inspection values to compensate for the shortage.
reasons: Passing dimensions does not guarantee fulfillment of the order quantity of 120.
Separately verify the two-item shortage as a nonconformity and consult the responsible person about disposition.
Shipping 118 items labeled 120 makes records and actual contents inconsistent.
Changing inspection values cannot supply the missing two physical items and creates false records.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-02.stem: A micrometer has 0.01 mm graduations; the sleeve is 8.5 mm and the thimble is 19. What is the value?
reasons: 19 thimble graduations equal 0.19 mm; 8.5 + 0.19 = 8.69 mm.
This omits the sleeve’s 0.5 mm and calculates 8 + 0.19.
This concatenates 8.5 and 19 rather than adding graduation values.
This fails to convert the thimble using 0.01 mm graduations and differs from the correct sum, 8.69 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-03.stem: An ideal DC resistance circuit has voltage 15 V and resistance 5 Ω. What is the current?
reasons: 15 × 5 multiplies voltage and resistance rather than dividing to find current.
5 ÷ 15 reverses the division and does not follow I = V/R.
I = 15 ÷ 5 = 3 A, under the conditions of an ideal DC circuit with constant resistance.
The difference 15 − 5 is not the equation for current.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-04.stem: Only a post-bend crack check has been completed for a fitting subjected to cyclic loads. What should be discussed next?
options: Treat a good bend result as guaranteed life.
Apply one angle to every material grade.
Verify fatigue-evaluation conditions matching cyclic-load requirements.
reasons: Post-bend crack observations do not guarantee fatigue life under cyclic loading.
Color alone cannot verify resistance to cyclic loads.
Specifications differ by material and conditions; do not generalize one textbook angle to every material grade.
Match cyclic-load magnitudes and conditions to requirements and consult about fatigue evaluation.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-05.stem: The welding arrow has no bend. How should the side to be prepared for the groove be determined?
options: No bend means no groove preparation is needed.
Check the basic symbol, relevant members, dimensions and supplementary instructions together.
Reverse the reference line to judge.
reasons: Examples of unbent arrows exist when the target is clear and in other cases; no bend does not mean no groove preparation.
Do not decide from the arrow bend alone; cross-check basic symbols, members, dimensions and supplementary instructions.
Formal instructions determine the preparation side, not personal preference.
Reversing the drawing and judging independently can confuse the arrow side and opposite side.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-06.stem: Furnace-area work presents both a change in physical condition and increased dust. Which organization is appropriate?
options: Separate heat and exposure information, withdraw safely and report.
A mask alone also solves the health-condition problem.
Stop ventilation because a health examination was completed.
Silently endure until the work is finished.
reasons: Treat physical-condition changes and dust generation as separate information, withdraw safely and report promptly.
A mask does not solve every problem such as bodily heat strain.
A health examination does not replace source or ventilation controls; do not stop them without authorization.
Silently enduring physical-condition changes or increased dust delays response.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-07.stem: A mock exam with equal points per question gives theory 22/30 and practical 5/10. What is the result?
options: Practical falls short of the required 6, so both sections have not passed.
High theory marks compensate for the practical shortfall.
reasons: A combined total cannot compensate for an independent practical-section shortfall.
Practical 5 is below the required 6, so both sections have not passed even though theory is in the passing range.
A high theory score does not replace the independent minimum practical requirement.
Required correct-answer counts are scoring conditions and cannot be freely changed by the examinee.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-08.stem: A learning example specifies density 2.70 g/cm³ and volume 30 cm³. What is the mass?
reasons: Mass = density × volume, so 2.70 × 30 = 81 g.
30 ÷ 2.70 divides volume by density, which is not the mass equation.
Adding density and volume values does not give mass.
810 g is ten times the correct 81 g.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-09.stem: Property changes are suspected outside the melted weld area. What should be examined?
options: There are no heat effects outside melted areas.
Check requirements and inspections including the surrounding heat-affected zone.
reasons: Welding heat may change structure and properties around the melted area as well as within it.
Visible color alone cannot establish all properties such as hardness and internal structure.
Omitting specified heat treatment changes a required process without authorization.
Include the surrounding heat-affected zone and check material/process requirements and necessary inspections.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-09-practical-10.stem: The same hole-dimension note is given to installation, assembly and component-machining teams. Which improvement is appropriate?
options: Verify approved drawings suited to the purpose, such as arrangement, assembly and part drawings.
Let each team freely add to the drawing.
reasons: Even readable text does not make a hole-dimension note sufficient for each team’s information needs.
Installation position relationships cannot be established solely from an individual component’s hole dimensions.
Verify approved drawings appropriate to each purpose: arrangement for installation, assembly for assembly, and part drawings for machining.
Independent additions can depart from formal requirements and destroy consistency among drawings.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-01.stem: Even if the reference changes during comparative measurement, using the old value makes every result reliable.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A changed reference changes the meaning of comparative differences. Check reference stability and affected measurement results.
False. A changed reference changes the meaning of comparative differences. Check reference stability and affected measurement results.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-02.stem: Hot rolling facilitates deformation, but cooling shrinkage, oxide scale and heating energy also need checking.
reasons: True. Check post-cooling dimensions, surface condition and process conditions together with the advantages of high-temperature processing.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. The term hot rolling does not remove dimensional or surface requirements; considering constraints in comparisons is appropriate.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-03.stem: Ordinary clear glasses remove the need to check shading performance for gas cutting.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Clear glasses for flying objects and shading performance against cutting light are different. Verify the performance specified for the work.
False. Clear glasses for flying objects and shading performance against cutting light are different. Verify the performance specified for the work.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-04.stem: A protractor guarantees the correct angle even if one side is lifted away.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. A lifted side does not contact both target surfaces correctly. A displayed reading does not guarantee the intended angle.
False. A lifted side does not contact both target surfaces correctly. A displayed reading does not guarantee the intended angle.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-05.stem: Even during 5S sorting, workers must not independently discard drawings, inspection records, entrusted items or similar materials.
reasons:
True. 5S is not merely about making a workplace look tidy. It is a way to maintain a workplace where necessary items are easy to find, incorrect items are not used, and hazards and abnormalities are easier to notice.
Sorting means separating necessary and unnecessary items. However, do not discard drawings, inspection records, or entrusted items at your own discretion. Confirm the disposal criteria and who has authority. Setting in order means deciding where necessary items belong and how to return them so they can be retrieved without searching.
When cleaning, remove dirt while also looking for abnormalities such as leaks or damage. Cleaning inside machinery must follow the specified stopping and safety confirmation procedure. Maintaining cleanliness means sustaining the results of sorting, organizing, and cleaning. Discipline means understanding the agreed methods and following them as a habit.
An improvement will not last if a one-time cleanup cannot be maintained by the next person. Defining responsibility, when checks are performed, and whom to notify of abnormalities creates an activity that does not rely solely on individual effort.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. 5S is not merely about making a workplace look tidy. It is a way to maintain a workplace where necessary items are easy to find, incorrect items are not used, and hazards and abnormalities are easier to notice.
Sorting means separating necessary and unnecessary items. However, do not discard drawings, inspection records, or entrusted items at your own discretion. Confirm the disposal criteria and who has authority. Setting in order means deciding where necessary items belong and how to return them so they can be retrieved without searching.
When cleaning, remove dirt while also looking for abnormalities such as leaks or damage. Cleaning inside machinery must follow the specified stopping and safety confirmation procedure. Maintaining cleanliness means sustaining the results of sorting, organizing, and cleaning. Discipline means understanding the agreed methods and following them as a habit.
An improvement will not last if a one-time cleanup cannot be maintained by the next person. Defining responsibility, when checks are performed, and whom to notify of abnormalities creates an activity that does not rely solely on individual effort.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-06.stem: Two scratches on one item mean two nonconforming items.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Nonconforming-unit count counts products with nonconformities. Two scratches on one item are two scratch occurrences but only one nonconforming product.
False. Nonconforming-unit count counts products with nonconformities. Two scratches on one item are two scratch occurrences but only one nonconforming product.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-07.stem: Drawings attach parameters such as Ra or Rz and their values to symbols and identify target surfaces directly or with leader lines.
reasons: True. Surface condition affects machine performance and includes waviness and roughness. Drawings add a parameter such as Ra or Rz and its value to a symbol, indicating the relevant surface directly or with a leader line. The same number means something different with a different parameter. Do not reuse a value from another surface; also check the machining-related symbol, relevant surface and measurement conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Surface condition affects machine performance and includes waviness and roughness. Drawings add a parameter such as Ra or Rz and its value to a symbol, indicating the relevant surface directly or with a leader line. The same number means something different with a different parameter. Do not reuse a value from another surface; also check the machining-related symbol, relevant surface and measurement conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-08.stem: At constant voltage, increasing an ideal resistance increases current.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. For an ideal resistor, I = V/R. At constant voltage, a greater resistance gives a smaller current.
False. For an ideal resistor, I = V/R. At constant voltage, a greater resistance gives a smaller current.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-09.stem: Fins on aluminum-extruded heat-dissipation parts help increase surface area, but geometry alone does not guarantee required strength or surface quality.
reasons: True. Fins are an example of heat-dissipating geometry; verify strength, surface condition and other requirements separately.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Understanding the heat-dissipation purpose does not justify omitting other requirements or inspections, so the statement is correct.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-10.stem: More rolling oil is not invariably better; follow equipment and product instructions for oil type and supply conditions.
reasons: True. Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. More oil is not necessarily better; oil type and supply conditions must follow equipment and product instructions. Do not try to address a defect only by changing the amount.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Rolling oil controls friction between the rolls and material to help the process run smoothly. It also carries away heat and helps reduce seizure and surface scratching. More oil is not necessarily better; oil type and supply conditions must follow equipment and product instructions. Do not try to address a defect only by changing the amount.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-11.stem: kg and N represent the same quantity if their numbers match.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. kg measures mass and N measures force; they are different quantities. Do not drop units and equate them even if the numbers match.
False. kg measures mass and N measures force; they are different quantities. Do not drop units and equate them even if the numbers match.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-12.stem: Equipment installation positions can invariably be understood from component hole dimensions alone.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Installation position relationships require arrangement drawings or similar information. Individual component hole dimensions alone do not verify equipment placement.
False. Installation position relationships require arrangement drawings or similar information. Individual component hole dimensions alone do not verify equipment placement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-13.stem: Aluminum extrusion pushes a heated billet through a die to make long products with cross sections corresponding to the die opening.
reasons: True. Aluminum extrusion pushes a heated billet through a die to produce a long product with a cross-section corresponding to the die opening. Applications include window frames and heat-dissipating fins. Specified cooling, straightening, and cutting follow extrusion. Product condition depends not only on die shape but also on material, temperature, and speed.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Aluminum extrusion pushes a heated billet through a die to produce a long product with a cross-section corresponding to the die opening. Applications include window frames and heat-dissipating fins. Specified cooling, straightening, and cutting follow extrusion. Product condition depends not only on die shape but also on material, temperature, and speed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-14.stem: Electrostatic painting attracts charged paint particles through space, while electrodeposition forms a coating electrically with the product in a bath; these are different processes.
reasons: True. Electrostatic painting uses attraction of charged particles, while electrodeposition is a bath process; the means of supplying paint differs.
Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Using electricity in both does not make them the same process; distinguish principles and applicable equipment.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-15.stem: Withstanding one static load guarantees life under every cyclic load.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Resistance to one static load does not guarantee fatigue life under cyclic loading. Evaluate under cyclic conditions matching requirements.
False. Resistance to one static load does not guarantee fatigue life under cyclic loading. Evaluate under cyclic conditions matching requirements.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-16.stem: On joining the company or moving to new work, learn machine and raw-material hazards, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start inspections, sorting and orderliness, emergency evacuation and other matters.
reasons: True. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. When joining a workplace or moving to a new task, learn the hazards of machinery and raw materials, protective equipment, safety devices, procedures, pre-start checks, housekeeping and evacuation in an accident. Experience operating the previous machine does not mean a new machine can be operated under the same conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-17.stem: The app’s independent mock exams reproduce actual official examination questions.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. This app’s mocks are independent practice questions, not reproductions or collections of actual official questions.
False. This app’s mocks are independent practice questions, not reproductions or collections of actual official questions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-18.stem: Standards are agreements to harmonize quality, dimensions, performance, test methods and related matters.
reasons: True. Standards provide agreed requirements for quality, dimensions, performance and test methods. ISO is an organization concerned with international standardization; JIS means Japanese Industrial Standards. Standards covering products or labels address different subjects from standards covering an organization’s management system.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Standards provide agreed requirements for quality, dimensions, performance and test methods. ISO is an organization concerned with international standardization; JIS means Japanese Industrial Standards. Standards covering products or labels address different subjects from standards covering an organization’s management system.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-19.stem: After surface hardening, the interior and surface invariably have identical conditions.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Surface hardening improves surface properties and does not necessarily leave the interior and surface in identical states.
False. Surface hardening improves surface properties and does not necessarily leave the interior and surface in identical states.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-20.stem: Standardize means cleaning once without maintaining the resulting condition afterward.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Standardize means maintaining the sorted, ordered and cleaned condition. It differs from cleaning once without maintaining it.
False. Standardize means maintaining the sorted, ordered and cleaned condition. It differs from cleaning once without maintaining it.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-21.stem: If a depth gauge’s measuring face cannot reach a groove bottom, do not enter the drawing value as an actual measurement of that unverified depth.
reasons: True. A depth gauge measures depth from a reference face. Seat it stably against that face and check that the measuring face reaches the target correctly. If it has not reached the bottom of a groove, do not record a value chosen to match the drawing depth.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A depth gauge measures depth from a reference face. Seat it stably against that face and check that the measuring face reaches the target correctly. If it has not reached the bottom of a groove, do not record a value chosen to match the drawing depth.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-22.stem: Wearing protective glasses permits removal of machine guards.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Protective glasses shield against flying objects and similar hazards; they do not replace equipment measures provided by guards. Do not remove guards without authorization.
False. Protective glasses shield against flying objects and similar hazards; they do not replace equipment measures provided by guards. Do not remove guards without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-23.stem: Handle diodes after checking direction and ratings; do not assume unlimited operation in reverse direction.
reasons: True. A diode primarily conducts in one direction under suitable conditions. An LED is a member of this family that emits light when current flows. This does not mean it may be connected without checking direction and ratings, or used without limits in reverse.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A diode primarily conducts in one direction under suitable conditions. An LED is a member of this family that emits light when current flows. This does not mean it may be connected without checking direction and ratings, or used without limits in reverse.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-24.stem: If a datum is unknown, freely use a convenient nearby surface as a new reference.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. The specified datum is the measurement reference. If unclear, inquire about the target, reference and standard; do not change to a nearby surface without authorization.
False. The specified datum is the measurement reference. If unclear, inquire about the target, reference and standard; do not change to a nearby surface without authorization.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-25.stem: Every height above a surface plate can be substituted for hole depth without checking the reference plane.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Height and depth have different reference surfaces and targets. Do not substitute top-surface height above a plate for depth to a hole bottom.
False. Height and depth have different reference surfaces and targets. Do not substitute top-surface height above a plate for depth to a hole bottom.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-26.stem: Link date and time, target lot, instrument, value and judgment so the items to which results belong are clear.
reasons: True. Carry out inspection using approved criteria and procedures, and record results promptly. Even when results are usually identical, do not copy the last value without measuring. Link date and time, lot, instrument, value and judgment so the items represented by a result can be identified.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Carry out inspection using approved criteria and procedures, and record results promptly. Even when results are usually identical, do not copy the last value without measuring. Link date and time, lot, instrument, value and judgment so the items represented by a result can be identified.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-27.stem: Check a straight ruler for chipped ends and dirty graduations; readable graduations alone do not guarantee every precision tolerance.
reasons: True. A steel rule measures length. Align the end of the object with the reference position and read the scale from directly in front. Check chipped ends or dirty graduations. Do not assume it can guarantee precision tolerances merely because it is read like a paper ruler. Select the instrument specified by the requirement.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. A steel rule measures length. Align the end of the object with the reference position and read the scale from directly in front. Check chipped ends or dirty graduations. Do not assume it can guarantee precision tolerances merely because it is read like a paper ruler. Select the instrument specified by the requirement.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-28.stem: Only the inspection department is responsible for quality; design and procurement information are irrelevant.
reasons: Choosing true for this statement is inappropriate. Quality is supported throughout design, procurement, manufacturing, inspection and shipment. Interdepartmental instructions, identification and handover information are also needed.
False. Quality is supported throughout design, procurement, manufacturing, inspection and shipment. Interdepartmental instructions, identification and handover information are also needed.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-29.stem: ISO is an organization concerned with international standardization, while JIS refers to Japanese Industrial Standards.
reasons: True. Standards provide agreed requirements for quality, dimensions, performance and test methods. ISO is an organization concerned with international standardization; JIS means Japanese Industrial Standards. Standards covering products or labels address different subjects from standards covering an organization’s management system.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Standards provide agreed requirements for quality, dimensions, performance and test methods. ISO is an organization concerned with international standardization; JIS means Japanese Industrial Standards. Standards covering products or labels address different subjects from standards covering an organization’s management system.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-theory-30.stem: When choosing welding, casting or pressing, do not decide from shape alone; also check material, required strength, production quantity and subsequent processes.
reasons: True. Even similar shapes differ in mechanisms and applicability among joining, solidification and plastic deformation. Select using both product requirements and approved process conditions.

Choosing false for this statement is inappropriate. Even similar shapes differ in mechanisms and applicability among joining, solidification and plastic deformation. Select using both product requirements and approved process conditions.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-01.stem: Defects increased after a tool change and material-lot change. Which investigation record is appropriate?
options: Declare only the replaced tool to be the cause.
Determine the cause solely from the operator’s name.
Link change times and the 4Ms to the last conforming and first nonconforming items.
reasons: Do not establish a cause solely from timing relative to a tool change; investigate other 4Ms such as material.
Deleting before-and-after data prevents tracing changes and the affected range.
A name alone cannot prove the cause of defects; facts about equipment, material and methods are needed.
Link change times and the 4Ms to the last conforming and first nonconforming items to organize the investigation scope.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-02.stem: A scale-calculation exercise gives only a drawn length of 20 mm at scale 1:4. What is the actual size?
reasons: 1:4 means the drawing is one quarter of actual size, so dividing 20 by 4 reverses the relationship.
Drawn length 20 mm × 4 = actual size 80 mm. This is scale calculation, not reading a written dimension.
20 mm is the drawn length, not the actual size accounting for the specified scale.
Multiply by the scale ratio of 4 rather than adding 4 to 20.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-03.stem: You are considering a long hollow resin tube with a constant cross section. Which check is appropriate?
options: Hollow means blow molding alone is mandatory.
Every resin solidifies the same way.
Consider extrusion and other candidates and check material and the approved process.
reasons: Even hollow products can be candidates for extrusion when long and of constant cross section; they are not limited to blow molding.
Some resins solidify by cooling while others cure through chemical reactions and other mechanisms.
Consider extrusion and other candidates based on the long constant cross section, and cross-check material, conditions and approved process.
An open mold does not guarantee touch-safe temperature or completed curing.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-04.stem: A difference of +0.02 mm relative to a 40.00 mm reference is specified. What is the dimension?
reasons: This subtracts the specified positive difference as if negative, reversing its sign.
0.02 mm is the difference, not the workpiece’s full dimension.
The difference is not zero, so the dimension cannot remain at reference value 40.00 mm.
Reference 40.00 + difference 0.02 = 40.02 mm.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-05.stem: In a paper example with equal volumes, reference water weighs 40 g and the sample 100 g. What is the ratio?
reasons: 100 − 40 = 60 is a mass difference, not a ratio.
40 ÷ 100 = 0.4 reverses reference and sample order.
For equal volumes, sample ÷ reference = 100 ÷ 40 = 2.5.
100 + 40 = 140 is a mass sum, not a ratio.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-06.stem: An approved new revision exists, but the relief worker’s terminal shows only the old revision. Which response is appropriate?
options: Ignore the terminal and work from memory.
It is complete if only you have the new revision.
Check scope, effective date, updating and communication.
reasons: Filling gaps from memory leaves the target or applicable revision unclear during work.
New and old revisions are used according to verified applicability, not free choice.
Communication is not complete if the relief worker has not received it.
Check the new revision’s scope and effective date, terminal updates, separation of the old revision and communication.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-07.stem: You memorized technical terms but make mistakes by overlooking negation. Which study method is appropriate?
options: Look only at the terms and skip the ending.
Reread the relevant situation and conditions through the sentence ending.
Take actual examination questions away to memorize.
reasons: Technical terms alone do not reveal ending negation or conditions and can lead to reversing the meaning.
Reread the situation, conditions and negation through the sentence ending to verify the meaning.
Do not take actual examination questions away for use as study material.
Do not settle unknown conditions by guessing; ask specific questions and verify.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-08.stem: An ideal DC resistor has voltage 12 V and current 3 A. What is its resistance?
reasons: 12 × 3 multiplies voltage and current, which is not the resistance equation.
3 ÷ 12 gives I/V, the inverse of resistance V/I.
The numerical difference 12 − 3 is not the resistance equation.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-09.stem: Roughness meets requirements, but a dimension is below its lower limit. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: Add gloss and erase the dimension value.
Record roughness and dimension separately and consult about disposition of dimensional nonconformity.
reasons: Roughness and dimension are separate requirements; passing roughness does not compensate for a dimension below its lower limit.
Adding gloss does not make the dimension pass; do not erase the record.
Retain roughness and dimensional results separately and consult about formal disposition of dimensional nonconformity.
Do not change criteria at the workplace without authorization to turn a nonconformity into a pass.

mfg1-mechanical-mock-10-practical-10.stem: Hatching was read as instructions to machine diagonal grooves. What is the correct review?
options: Cross-check other views, treating it as a representation of material sections at an imaginary cut.
Remove material at every diagonal line.
Treat the product as already cut.
Treat all hatched areas as holes.
reasons: Hatching indicates material cut surfaces and similar features at an imaginary cut; read it together with other views and the cutting position.
The diagonal lines themselves are not groove-machining instructions or orders to remove material at every line.
This represents an imaginary cut, not a history showing that the actual object has already been cut.
This confuses hatched material cut surfaces with empty hole spaces.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q01.stem: ISO14001 certification automatically makes all emissions and work compliant.
reasons: True is incorrect. Certification does not mean automatic compliance of individual operations or emissions.
False is correct. Certification does not mean automatic compliance of individual operations or emissions.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q02.stem: PDCA evaluates results after implementation and feeds them into the next plan.
reasons: True is correct. Separate implementation from effect and reflect evaluation in standards or subsequent plans.
False is inappropriate. Separate implementation from effect and reflect evaluation in standards or subsequent plans.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q03.stem: Investigate previous-process removal when deep scratches remain.
reasons: True is correct. Finishing alone may not remove deep prior-process scratches.
False is inappropriate. Finishing alone may not remove deep prior-process scratches.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q04.stem: Cutting safety or inspection to meet delivery is always good QCDS improvement.
reasons: True is incorrect. QCDS must preserve quality and safety too.
False is correct. QCDS must preserve quality and safety too.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q05.stem: Neutralization forming water from H⁺ and OH⁻ always changes oxidation numbers and is redox.
reasons: True is incorrect. The elements' oxidation numbers do not change in this neutralization.
False is correct. The elements' oxidation numbers do not change in this neutralization.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q06.stem: Hydrogen-ion concentration changes with falling pH are not simple numeric subtraction.
reasons: True is correct. pH is logarithmic; one unit corresponds to roughly tenfold concentration.
False is inappropriate. pH is logarithmic; one unit corresponds to roughly tenfold concentration.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q07.stem: Positive finite resistors in parallel always give resistance greater than the largest resistor.
reasons: True is incorrect. Their parallel resistance is smaller than the smallest resistor.
False is correct. Their parallel resistance is smaller than the smallest resistor.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q08.stem: Dyeing and sealing are post-treatments with different purposes.
reasons: True is correct. Dyeing adds color; sealing closes pores and has related functions.
False is inappropriate. Dyeing adds color; sealing closes pores and has related functions.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q09.stem: A rectifier converts AC to DC.
reasons: True is correct. Its main role is converting AC into DC.
False is inappropriate. Its main role is converting AC into DC.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q10.stem: Matching gloss permits unauthorized layer-structure changes.
reasons: True is incorrect. Layer changes affect function and require approval.
False is correct. Layer changes affect function and require approval.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q11.stem: Typical brass mainly contains copper and zinc.
reasons: True is correct. Typical brass is principally Cu and Zn.
False is inappropriate. Typical brass is principally Cu and Zn.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q12.stem: Repeated use of approved boxes is reuse.
reasons: True is correct. Using an item repeatedly is reuse.
False is inappropriate. Using an item repeatedly is reuse.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q13.stem: A molten bath is hot, so water on wet items is irrelevant.
reasons: True is incorrect. High temperature makes rapid water vaporization hazardous.
False is correct. High temperature makes rapid water vaporization hazardous.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q14.stem: pH-meter calibration is a check when investigating out-of-range values.
reasons: True is correct. Separate calibration problems from process changes.
False is inappropriate. Separate calibration problems from process changes.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q15.stem: Do not independently discard unknown containers in the name of tidying.
reasons: True is correct. Chemical disposal follows specified identification and decisions.
False is inappropriate. Chemical disposal follows specified identification and decisions.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q16.stem: An alloy name reveals every exact addition ratio in the actual item.
reasons: True is incorrect. Actual alloys can have other additions or formulation differences.
False is correct. Actual alloys can have other additions or formulation differences.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q17.stem: Tiny holes are always irrelevant to corrosion protection.
reasons: True is incorrect. Water or oxygen can act through small holes.
False is correct. Water or oxygen can act through small holes.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q18.stem: Surface oxide can affect apparent corrosion.
reasons: True is correct. A protective film can suppress reaction.
False is inappropriate. A protective film can suppress reaction.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q19.stem: Operators classify oxides by putting unknown material into acid.
reasons: True is incorrect. Do not test classifications by adding unknown substances to chemicals.
False is correct. Do not test classifications by adding unknown substances to chemicals.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q20.stem: Convert between N and mol/L after checking reaction conditions.
reasons: True is correct. N alone can leave the reaction factor unspecified.
False is inappropriate. N alone can leave the reaction factor unspecified.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q21.stem: Sufficient tank capacity removes the need to check its material.
reasons: True is incorrect. Capacity and chemical/thermal compatibility are different.
False is correct. Capacity and chemical/thermal compatibility are different.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q22.stem: Activation is always better in stronger liquid for longer time.
reasons: True is incorrect. Insufficient and excessive treatment can both cause problems; follow specified conditions.
False is correct. Insufficient and excessive treatment can both cause problems; follow specified conditions.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q23.stem: Records under the same conditions make improvement effects easier to compare.
reasons: True is correct. Different conditions obscure changes attributable to measures.
False is inappropriate. Different conditions obscure changes attributable to measures.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q24.stem: An operator may return items to acid without recording a process reversal.
reasons: True is incorrect. Unauthorized reversal can cause overtreatment or unclear history.
False is correct. Unauthorized reversal can cause overtreatment or unclear history.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q25.stem: Electroless plating still needs concentration, temperature and pH control.
reasons: True is correct. Chemical deposition also depends on controlled liquid conditions.
False is inappropriate. Chemical deposition also depends on controlled liquid conditions.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-theory-q26.stem: A weak electrolyte always means merely a dilute liquid.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q05.stem: A tin bath is assumed harmless including every additive because tin is familiar. What is appropriate?
options: Check bath constituents, application and safety conditions
Immediately use everything for food contact
reasons: Heat and chemical hazards exist.
Discharge needs separate checks.
A metal name does not determine the whole bath's safety.
Product suitability is unconfirmed.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q06.stem: Omitting a thin strike by thickening the main coating is proposed. What is appropriate?
options: Check underlayer adhesion roles and the approved process
reasons: This does not guarantee function.
Interface roles differ.
The approved sequence is required.
Main and underlayers have different purposes.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q07.stem: For a coil, right-hand fingers follow circulating current. What does the thumb show?
reasons: This differs from field direction.
This is a direction rule.
This is the coil correspondence.
This reverses the coil relationship.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q08.stem: A 1:1 exercise titration uses 8.0 mL of 0.200 mol/L standard for 10.0 mL sample. What concentration results?
reasons: Volume units are mixed.
This is one decimal place too small.
The ratio is reversed.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q09.stem: Water droplets appear in a recess before molten-bath immersion. What is appropriate?
options: Hold immersion and check drying and shape requirements
reasons: Quantity alone does not establish safety.
This approaches a hazard.
This ignores splash hazards.
Carried-in water can vaporize rapidly.

mfg1-surface-mock-07-practical-q10.stem: Total treatment area is 4.0 dm² with 10 A. What average current density is calculated?
reasons: Division is reversed.
A per-area unit is needed.
Do not multiply.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q01.stem: A zinc film on iron shows white changes. What is appropriate?
options: Check coating and requirements and record location/environment
reasons: Investigation and approval are needed.
The changed substance and target are unconfirmed.
Whiteness alone establishes neither safety nor acceptance.
Appearance does not guarantee the product of corrosion.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q02.stem: Some same-lot items discolored after storage. What comparison information is appropriate?
options: Locations, drying, rinsing and storage records including unchanged items
Improvement if different light hides it
reasons: Investigate differences with conditions.
This is an unconfirmed hypothesis.
This hides the condition.
Comparison conditions differ.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q03.stem: The current field says 8 V. What is checked before correction?
options: 8 means the same current and voltage
Confirm original instrument, quantity and operator
reasons: They are different quantities.
Traceability is lost.
Letters alone do not establish facts.
What was measured remains unknown.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q04.stem: Someone claims a normal salt must be neutral and harmless. What is appropriate?
options: Separate classification from solution pH and constituent hazards
reasons: It depends on the combination.
Composition and process are unchecked.
Metal salts can present hazards.
A name alone does not establish liquid properties.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q05.stem: A portable pH electrode was replaced. What takes priority before process decisions?
reasons: Replacement still requires calibration and compatibility checks.
Internal solution is model- and procedure-specific.
This is not the current measurement.
A display alone does not guarantee accuracy.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q06.stem: In a dilute-aqueous approximation, pH changes from 6 to 4. How does hydrogen-ion concentration change?
reasons: This ignores pH change.
Two steps give 10×10.
This ignores the logarithmic relationship.
The direction is reversed.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q07.stem: Current toward you in a straight conductor is a dot viewed from the front. Which surrounding field direction follows the right-hand rule?
options: Only toward you along the conductor
A fixed direction unrelated to current
reasons: This corresponds to current away from you.
With thumb toward you, fingers curl counterclockwise.
It circles the straight conductor.
Field direction corresponds to current direction.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q08.stem: Returning a sample deformed by a bend test to a product box is proposed. What is appropriate?
options: Reshape by hand and leave unmarked
Mix it to fill a quantity shortage
Identify it as tested and use designated sample controls
reasons: Color does not establish post-test conformity.
This is unauthorized rework and lost identification.
It confuses supply quantity and sample quality.
Do not mix deformed samples with unused conforming products.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q09.stem: KYT says only pay sufficient attention. What elements make it specific?
options: Person, situation, action and checking method
reasons: KYT does not replace engineering measures.
This loses understanding and authority checks.
Make the goal executable.
This does not lead to measures.

mfg1-surface-mock-08-practical-q10.stem: Thickness fits a comparison table but not the product drawing. What is appropriate?
options: Change the drawing to the table
Identify the product-requirement mismatch and inquire
reasons: Use specified locations and decision conditions.
This is an unauthorized change.
Drawing requirements are ignored.
A general guide does not replace specifications.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q01.stem: In Fe → Fe²⁺ + 2 e⁻, how are the electrons and the change classified?
reasons: This is an oxidation half-reaction of ionization.
The direction is reversed.
Electrons appear on the right-hand side.
The electron balance cannot be checked.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q02.stem: The drawing changes an aluminum alloy to another material. How should the old pretreatment be handled?
options: Only make the main plating thicker
Continue because the outer shape is the same
Write the old material name on the new drawing
Identify the item and ask whether the substrate and pretreatment are compatible
reasons: Thicker plating is not a substitute for pretreatment.
Outer shape does not guarantee chemical compatibility.
Do not falsify facts or requirements.
Compare the substrate change with the process.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q03.stem: The latest procedure is for a different item. What should you do?
options: Check the target item and the valid document
Always reuse it because it is new
reasons: Even a new revision is not necessarily applicable to another item.
The target item has not been checked.
Its scope of application differs.
This is an unauthorized document change.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q04.stem: Two coatings have the same thickness: one is for outdoor coloring and the other for sliding service. What should be checked?
options: Unconditionally seal every item in the same way
The same color means the same insulation
Check specifications for properties such as light resistance for the former and wear resistance for the latter
Finish all evaluation based on thickness alone
reasons: Performance requirements may involve trade-offs.
Defects and conditions can also differ.
The application determines the required performance.
Other properties have not been checked.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q05.stem: Which of CO₂, CaO and Al₂O₃ is an amphoteric oxide?
reasons: This does not distinguish the classifications.
This is an example of an acidic oxide.
This is an example of a basic oxide.
Consider reactions with both acids and bases.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q06.stem: A burette reading changes from 1.8 mL to 14.6 mL. What volume was delivered?
reasons: This is only the starting reading.
This is only the final reading.
The readings have been added.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q07.stem: The diagram calls for AC measurement, but the meter is DC-only. What should you do?
options: Have an untrained person modify the wiring
Hold measurement until the target and meter compatibility are checked
Use it if it displays a number
reasons: Changing actual equipment requires training and authorization.
Check compatibility with AC or DC.
Changing a label does not change the measurement method.
A displayed value alone does not guarantee compatibility.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q08.stem: Abnormal vibration occurs during cleaning, and stopping is possible from a safe location. What is the first action?
options: Continue running until the cause is known
Carry out the specified stop and report the facts
Change operators without recording the condition
reasons: This leaves the abnormal condition unattended.
Prevent the danger from spreading and enable investigation.
There is a risk of entanglement and other injury.
The condition has not been shared.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q09.stem: Which describes the mechanism of CVD?
options: Always deposit onto a cathode by direct current in an aqueous solution
Only physical evaporation in every case
Chemical reactions involving gaseous raw materials and similar substances
Only remove the surface by friction
reasons: This describes ordinary wet electrodeposition.
This loses the distinction from PVD.
This considers reactions that distinguish CVD from PVD.
This describes polishing.

mfg1-surface-mock-09-practical-q10.stem: Unexpected white turbidity appears in a liquid. What information should be recorded?
options: Liquid name, mixing history, temperature, time and the state of the turbidity
Transfer only the clear upper liquid without authorization
Add chemicals until it becomes clear
Conclude that it is AgCl because it is white
reasons: These are useful for identifying components and investigating the cause.
This transfers an uninvestigated abnormal condition elsewhere.
This is unapproved mixing.
Appearance alone cannot identify the substance.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q01.stem: The factory committee is scheduled for next week, but there is danger now. What should you do?
options: Continue working as usual until the next meeting
Only put it on the agenda and omit informing the workplace
Assume that a greeting also communicated the danger
Follow the workplace emergency notification, stopping and evacuation procedures
reasons: A future meeting is not a reason to wait.
Putting it on an agenda alone does not address the present danger.
A greeting differs from a specific report of the location and condition.
Address the present danger through the specified emergency procedures.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q02.stem: Using the Table 7-1 values of 8.93 for copper and 8.9 for nickel, compare their masses at the same volume on paper.
options: Copper has a slightly greater mass
Specific gravity is the melting point and is unrelated to mass comparison
The table values alone guarantee the composition of an actual alloy
reasons: Copper has the larger value, 8.93, in this table.
At the same volume, using these table values, 8.93 is greater than 8.9.
Specific gravity is a density ratio, not a melting point.
Comparing representative values does not guarantee the composition of an actual item.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q03.stem: The conductivity table gives aluminum as 37.7 with the unit 10⁶ S/m. What is the value in S/m?
options: It means the same as 37.7% IACS
reasons: Calculate 37.7 × 1,000,000 and retain S/m.
This omits the 10⁶ in the heading.
This reverses the 10⁶ multiplier.
This confuses an absolute value in S/m with a percentage relative to a reference.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q04.stem: In Cu²⁺ + 2 e⁻ → Cu, what change occurs?
reasons: This is reduction of a metal ion.
The equation represents a chemical reaction.
Electrons are consumed on the left-hand side.
The direction is reversed.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q05.stem: A current of 8 A flows over a total area of 2.0 dm². Only the area changes to 4.0 dm². What is the current density?
reasons: This ignores the area change.
This divides in the opposite direction.
This multiplies instead.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q06.stem: Before a change, 12 of 300 items were defective; afterward, 4 of 100 were defective. How do the rates compare?
options: The rate must be one third as large
reasons: This loses the basis for comparison.
The number of items examined also became one third as large.
This miscalculates 4 ÷ 100.
12 ÷ 300 and 4 ÷ 100 give the same rate.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q07.stem: Someone says, ‘Aluminum can also be used at 660°C.’ What should be checked?
options: The same color means the same heat resistance
Heat the actual equipment to try it
Guarantee it using only the pure metal's melting point
Check the alloy, coating, strength and approved service specification
reasons: Appearance cannot determine this.
Specific authorization and a suitable method are required.
Other properties can change even at lower temperatures.
The melting point is not the upper service temperature.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q08.stem: A two-component material is past its pot life, but its appearance is unchanged. What should you do?
options: Use all of it if its color is unchanged
Give priority to the specified time and follow the responsible person's procedure
Add a hardener from another product
reasons: Color does not guarantee performance.
This is an unapproved change.
Do not disregard reaction conditions based only on appearance.
The combination is unknown.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q09.stem: Another two-component product has the same urethane resin name. What should be checked?
options: The ratio is unrestricted if the color is the same
Check the specified hardener, ratio, pot life and curing conditions
Raise all products to the same temperature
reasons: Color does not guarantee reaction conditions.
The resin name alone does not determine compatibility.
This may differ from the specified combination.
Follow the instructions for each product.

mfg1-surface-mock-10-practical-q10.stem: Contact corrosion is found in a storage box. What information should be investigated?
options: Determine the cause from color alone
Contact materials, moisture, scratches and storage history
reasons: Other factors cannot be excluded.
The cause and conformity have not been checked.
Investigate the environment together with contact conditions.
Liquids and the environment also play a role.
